news.Title: JPMorgan resets Apple stock price target amid iPhone panic
news.Content:
Like clockwork, the fall iPhone launch has been followed by talk of trouble. Apple reportedly told suppliers to cut October component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max by at least 15% from earlier plans after demand came in softer than expected.

Apple stock shrugged it off. Shares climbed about 1.3% to $340.93 on Oct. 12 after one of Wall Street's biggest banks pushed back on the gloomy reading and lifted its price target.

Also read: Apple's priciest iPhone is giving some AT&T customers problems

JPMorgan says the order cuts are nothing new

JPMorgan raised its Apple price target by $20 to $360, only months after trimming it to $340 in July over supply worries.

In a note to investors, analyst Samik Chatterjee kept his Overweight rating and said the reported cuts are no different from the production adjustments Apple makes every year. He added that demand for the iPhone 18 Pro is running fractionally ahead of the iPhone 17 Pro so far, according to Fortune .

Chatterjee argued that supplier cuts reflect Apple's new launch timing rather than a weaker upgrade cycle. He pointed to lead times that suggest demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max is holding up better than it did for last year's Pro models, as reported by Benzinga .

Other analysts are urging caution about reading too much into supplier chatter. Evercore ISI warned that changes to component orders don't always translate directly into consumer demand, while UBS flagged shipping wait times as the signal worth watching. A 15% cut in orders, in other words, is not the same as a 15% drop in demand.

Survey data also leans toward the bulls. Evercore's annual poll of nearly 4,000 U.S. consumers found that 53% of people planning to buy an iPhone expected to pick a Pro or Pro Max model, and the firm noted longer delivery times after preorders opened.

Apple's split launch muddies the holiday quarter

This year's lineup broke from Apple's usual playbook. The company launched its first foldable alongside two premium models this fall, while the standard iPhone 18 was pushed into the first half of 2027.

Rising memory costs and the complexity of building a foldable weighed on the plan. And pricier models give Apple more room to absorb higher component costs.

That foldable, the iPhone Duo, starts at $1,999 and comes with a 7.6-inch inner display, with preorders opening on Oct. 16 and sales beginning on Oct. 23. Citi has called it Apple's biggest new hardware category since the Apple Watch and AirPods, as reported by TheStreet .

Story Continues

The split schedule is the main reason JPMorgan is trimming its December quarter outlook. The bank expects a temporary shortfall as buyers of the base iPhone wait for the early 2027 launch, though higher prices and the iPhone Duo should help offset the gap and allow Apple revenue to rise year over year, even as iPhone revenue declines slightly.

Chatterjee now sees December quarter earnings landing about 4% below the consensus estimate. He expects iPhone shipments to fall 18% from a year earlier, but believes higher average selling prices will make up for most of that drop. He describes this as a price-driven cycle rather than a volume story, according to Benzinga .

What could still go wrong for Apple

JPMorgan isn't blind to the risks. Its analysts flagged the global economy and its effect on consumer demand, local rivals in overseas markets that can move faster on pricing, and foreign tariffs that could favor homegrown brands. They also listed Apple's acquisitions as a possible distraction, though they believe the CEO handover has been handled well so far.

Memory prices remain the biggest wild card. Apple raised prices on several Macs and iPads in June, and a spokesperson said the company had "never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly," TheStreet reported . IDC expects the global smartphone market to shrink by close to 14% this year.

More Apple:

Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge

Apple secret new device is a challenge to Amazon

Bank of America warns Apple investors because of Meta's Muse

The competitive picture in China is tricky, too. Huawei launched its new Mate 90 series on Oct. 1, even as China's smartphone market continues to contract. Rising memory prices have pushed up production costs across the industry, forcing handset makers to raise prices further.

There is also a new leader at the top. John Ternus took over as Apple's CEO on Sept. 1, while Tim Cook moved into the role of executive chairman. The board approved the change unanimously as part of a long-term succession plan announced in April.

What Apple investors should watch next

The company enters this stretch from a position of strength. In its most recent quarterly report, released in late July, Apple said revenue rose 16%, and iPhone sales jumped 22%.

Bank of America is also sticking with the stock. It trimmed its price target to $370 from $380 but kept its Buy rating, even while flagging SpaceX's move into wireless as a longer-term risk to the carrier subsidies that help sell iPhones. The analysts see limited near-term earnings risk and don't expect a real impact until fiscal 2028 or later.

The next big test comes on Nov. 2, when Apple reports its fiscal fourth-quarter results. It will be the first earnings call led by Ternus as CEO, alongside CFO Kevan Parekh.

That call should show whether J.P. Morgan's patience is about to pay off.

news.Title: 美股平靜時光所剩不多 月底起四大事件接力、預期波動增50%
news.Content:
歷經波折不斷的夏季後，美股似乎進入一段平靜期。投資人或許該把握這段寧靜時光，因為選擇權市場正暗示本月下旬起，恐將迎來一波波動潮。

選擇權分析平台ORATS創辦人馬特·安伯森（Matt Amberson）向 MarketWatch 表示，當前情勢堪稱「暴風雨前的寧靜」。

根據道瓊市場數據（Dow Jones Market Data）分析選擇權定價結果，隨著美國聯準會（Fed）即將公布最新利率決策，自 10 月 28 日起標普 500 指數的預期單日波動幅度，平均將激增約 50%。

選擇權市場的定價顯示，隨著聯準會利率決策、重磅企業財報、美國期中選舉以及 10 月非農就業報告這「四大事件」自月底起接連登場，市場恐將告別平靜，並一舉觸發美股新一波劇烈波動。

其中最受矚目的重頭戲莫過於 11 月 3 日的期中選舉，而這波關鍵密集期將在 11 月 6 日公布的 10 月非農就業報告中畫下句點。

安伯森在電子郵件中表示，目前重大總體經濟催化因素不多，周三(14日)公布的消費者物價指數（CPI）報告是少數焦點。

不過，選擇權交易員正為本月底起更劇烈的行情預作準備，屆時投資人將接連面對聯準會決策、多家重要企業財報、期中選舉及 10 月就業報告。

類股輪動 壓低大盤波動

有華爾街「恐慌指數」之稱的芝加哥選擇權交易所波動率指數（VIX），數月來持續走低。然而，標普 500 成分股中仍有個股大幅震盪，不同產業股票的走勢也日益分歧。

這種檯面下的高度分化，有助於抑制指數層級的波動。當受惠人工智慧（AI）熱潮的股票表現疲弱時，所謂的「非 AI」股票便挺身支撐大盤，反之亦然。

BTIG 首席技術策略師克林斯基（Jonathan Krinsky）指出，截至週一為止，標普 500 指數已連續 52 個交易日未曾出現單日 1% 以上的跌幅。若再維持一天，這將創下 2020 年 1 月以來最長無顯著拉回紀錄。他認為，近期成交量萎縮無疑是造成大盤走勢沉悶的主因之一。

克林斯基在報告中分析，市場目前正處於重磅總經數據、關鍵催化劑與財報季之間的真空期，缺乏足以推動大盤的重大新消息，投資人普遍傾向觀望，靜待本週稍後大型銀行股開開首槍後再做決策。

他補充道，指數層級缺乏波動的時間長度，確實超出了他與許多市場人士的預期。

隨著美國大型銀行自周二起陸續公布業績，第三季財報季預料將正式進入高峰。

標普500距上次修正已久 超過歷史平均

標普 500 指數也已有一段時間未出現修正，通常定義為自近期高點下跌至少 10%。根據 Bespoke Investment Group 的分析，截至周一收盤，距離最近一次修正結束，已過了 552 個交易日。

news.Title: Meta expands WhatsApp utility with non-account guest calling features
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META) has expanded WhatsApp's business utility by enabling guest calling capabilities, allowing non-account holders to join end-to-end encrypted voice and video calls at no cost. The strategic update directly targets competitive friction points in the digital communications market by eliminating time limits, account registration requirements, and software download barriers for invitees.

Under the new functionality, WhatsApp account holders can generate call links to host 1:1 or group sessions supporting up to 32 participants. Non-users can access these calls directly through desktop browsers after host approval, accessing core collaborative features such as screen sharing, emoji reactions, and hand-raising.

The feature expansion incorporates strict privacy controls to maintain the platform's security architecture while opening access to external participants. Guest users operate with restricted permissions, remaining unable to view other participants' phone numbers, transmit text messages, or invite additional attendees without explicit host consent.

Later this year, Meta plans to deepen the feature's workflow integration by rolling out native calendar plugins for Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook. The upcoming integration signals a broader ambition to capture professional and educational communications traffic traditionally dominated by legacy videoconferencing tools.

Against that backdrop, the update positions WhatsApp to drive higher cross-platform engagement while reinforcing Meta's broader strategy of converting casual messaging services into productivity infrastructure. By reducing onboarding friction, Meta strengthens the platform's utility for enterprise-adjacent workflows and group collaboration.

Markets reacted cautiously to the heightened competition in the collaboration sector following the announcement. Ringcentral Inc (NYSE:RNG) shares fell 2.7%, while Zoom Communications, Inc (NASDAQ:ZM) slipped 1.8%. Microsoft Corp., which hit an all-time high earlier in the week, pulled back 1.0%.

news.Title: Not Microsoft. Not Alphabet. Here's the Cloud Giant I'm Most Bullish About.
news.Content:
The cloud computing sector is one of the most interesting parts of the stock market right now. There are several companies spending more than $100 billion each to build and equip new data centers this year, and their capital expenditures are projected to rise once again in 2027. That's a ton of money being invested in this sector, but these companies wouldn't be doing it if they didn't see major potential.

The big three providers of cloud computing infrastructure are Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL). While Microsoft and Alphabet have exciting prospects, I'm far more bullish on Amazon for one reason: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has a bigger influence on its overall results than the cloud arms of Microsoft and Alphabet have on those companies. And it's easy to see why I'm so optimistic about it.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

AWS is seeing its growth accelerate

AWS is the biggest cloud computing service in the world, with a market share of about 28%. It was also the first to be launched. Although it looked to be falling behind the other two on artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of the AI race , Amazon has caught back up and established itself as a popular option for running AI workloads.

In its pursuit of that market, it has been spending more and more on cloud infrastructure, and it's on course for around $220 billion in data center capital expenditures this year. That leads the pack, but what returns on investment are shareholders seeing from those outlays?

During the second quarter, AWS revenue grew 37% year over year. For comparison, it grew 28% during the first quarter and 24% in 2025's fourth quarter. That's a strong acceleration for a business the size of AWS, so it's clearly seeing a strong return on investment.

However, investors also want to see these cloud segments turn a real profit, and that's what separates AWS from its peers.

AWS is a huge part of Amazon's business

During the second quarter, AWS' operating income surged 64% year over year, and this is what makes Amazon a better stock pick than Microsoft or Alphabet. The company may be best known for its massive e-commerce operation, but such businesses produce pretty slim operating margins. By contrast, the core business units of Microsoft and Alphabet are high-margin software and advertising businesses.

Story Continues

GOOG Operating Margin data by YCharts; TTM = trailing 12 months.

During the second quarter, AWS posted a 39% operating margin. Alphabet's Google Cloud wasn't far off with a 36% operating income margin. Microsoft doesn't publicly break out its margin figures for individual segments, but I'd guess Azure's operating margin is likely in the same neighborhood.

So, Azure is actually not boosting Microsoft's operating profit margin by growing quickly, and Alphabet's Google Cloud is only helping its operating margin minimally. But AWS is providing a huge boost for Amazon as a whole: The segment accounted for 60% of Amazon's total operating income during the second quarter. This means that the faster AWS grows, the faster the company's overall profits grow, which gives it huge operating leverage.

Anytime a company is on the doorstep of major growth in a high-margin business like this, it should get investors excited, as major stock returns can follow. While all three tech leaders will reap huge benefits from growing their cloud computing business, the effect will be most felt at Amazon.

With Amazon spending hundreds of billions of dollars a year to transform its business, it's on the right track. I wouldn't be surprised to see its stock greatly outperform the other two over the next few years. As a result, I think it's one of the best big-tech stocks to buy now.

news.Title: Should You Buy Alphabet Before Oct. 28?
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is best known for something many of us use daily: Google Search. The search engine, which steadily boasts a market share of 90%, is so popular that it's even entered our vocabulary: When we don't know the answer to a question, we often say, "let's Google it." And the entire market-leading Google platform has been Alphabet's ticket to growing revenue over time.

Meanwhile, in recent years, the company has also benefited from a fresh growth driver, and that's artificial intelligence (AI). Alphabet is one of the early winners in this space and is well-positioned to keep that momentum going. Now, with a catalyst ahead on Oct. 28, should you buy Alphabet shares before that date? Let's find out.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Google ads make up 68% of Alphabet's revenue

So let's dive into the Alphabet story, starting with its Google Search business. As mentioned, the Google platform drives revenue, and this is through advertising. Advertisers, seeing how much time we spend on Google, are eager to place ads for their products and services here to reach us. This has helped Alphabet grow revenue and profit over time.

GOOG Revenue (Annual) data by YCharts

In the most recent quarter, Google advertising made up 68% of the company's total revenue of $119 billion.

Alphabet also generates significant revenue through its cloud computing business. Google Cloud is one of the world's biggest cloud services providers , and AI demand has supercharged growth. In the quarter, enterprise AI solutions and infrastructure drove an 82% increase in revenue to more than $24 billion. What's particularly compelling is that Alphabet offers customers access to a wide range of products and services from others, such as chip designer Nvidia -- and its own products like the large language model (LLM), Gemini.

Alphabet is scoring a win through Gemini in a few ways. The company itself is harnessing the power of this LLM to improve Google Search, with the idea that a better search experience will keep us using the tool longer -- and attract more advertising for Alphabet. We may also directly use Gemini, and here, Alphabet is seeing great success. In August, the Gemini app surpassed one billion monthly users, and this made it Alphabet's fastest-growing product ever. Finally, as mentioned, Google Cloud customers may access Gemini for their specific needs.

Story Continues

Alphabet, like its fellow cloud service providers, has spoken of enormous demand for AI capacity and has been heavily investing in the AI build-out . Though some investors have worried about this spending by Alphabet and peers such as Amazon and Meta Platforms , others argue that the AI story is in its early days and only beginning to address real-world problems. All of this suggests that considerable growth could lie ahead.

Alphabet's effort to "meet growing demand"

In the latest earnings call, Alphabet said that its increase in capital expenditure guidance for the year to as much as $205 billion "is primarily due to an acceleration in the delivery of capacity to meet growing demand."

Now, let's consider the catalyst on the horizon. On Oct. 28, Alphabet is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.

Revenue may reach $127 billion, according to the average analyst estimate, representing a 25% gain year over year. As for free cash flow, Alphabet expects some pressure due to the company's ongoing spending on AI infrastructure. Finally, investors will also be listening closely to updates on demand, and here, there's reason to be optimistic, considering the strength we've seen in recent quarters.

With all of this in mind, should you buy Alphabet before Oct. 28? It's difficult to predict whether investors will be excited about potential good news and rush to get in on the stock or turn away from the stock on concern about capex. But here's the good news: As long-term investors, it doesn't matter if we buy a stock before or after a specific event, and that's because, over time, any gain or loss on one particular day won't have much of an impact on our returns. All of this means Alphabet makes a solid buy -- before or after its next earnings report.

news.Title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. This Under-the-Radar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock Could Be the Biggest Winner in 2027.
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) are two of the stock market's biggest artificial intelligence (AI) success stories. Nvidia dominates AI accelerators, while Micron is benefiting from extraordinary demand for memory chips. Both companies have delivered remarkable growth, rewarding investors who recognized their opportunities early.

But as Wall Street looks toward 2027, another semiconductor stock could be preparing for its breakout moment. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) has already rallied on enthusiasm surrounding custom AI chips and advanced networking.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, the company's latest investor day projections, a lucrative partnership with Nvidia, and an expanding relationship with Alphabet suggest something more substantial than hype. As investors look beyond the obvious AI winners, Marvell could attract considerably more attention.

Marvell covers two enormous AI markets

Marvell isn't trying to replace Nvidia's GPUs or compete with Micron's memory solutions. Instead, the company focuses on two increasingly important components of AI infrastructure: custom silicon and high-speed connectivity.

Custom accelerators allow hyperscalers to design processors specifically optimized for certain workloads. Meanwhile, optical networking and interconnect technologies help move enormous quantities of data between chips, servers, and data centers.

During its recent investor day conference, Marvell estimated its total addressable market (TAM) could approach $400 billion by calendar 2030. Management outlined approximately $37 billion in interconnect revenue and roughly $30 billion from custom silicon by fiscal year 2031. This forecast reflects expectations for annualized growth of approximately 65% and 80%, respectively, across the two businesses.

Nvidia and Google endorsed Marvell

Back in March, Nvidia invested $2 billion in Marvell. The deal helped establish a strategic partnership focused on connecting custom AI processors with Nvidia's computing and networking ecosystem. The relationship focuses on NVLink Fusion, which allows AI developers to integrate specialized processors into Nvidia-based racks.

This is important because it positions Marvell as a beneficiary of the broader data center build-out rather than simply a competitor to Nvidia. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's willingness to invest in Marvell provides a meaningful endorsement of its technology.

Story Continues

In addition, Marvell's expanding relationship with Alphabet involves developing custom silicon supporting Google Cloud's AI infrastructure, including chips that complement its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) ecosystem.

Specifically, Google received warrants tied to as much as $120 billion in potential chip purchases through fiscal 2033. While this isn't guaranteed revenue, it still illustrates the enormous scale of the relationship and the importance of Marvell's position in the AI chip value chain.

Why 2027 could be Marvell's breakout year

For years, memory and storage were viewed as commodity products. For this reason, memory stocks have had to fend off a narrative that they operate in cyclical markets. As AI infrastructure spending continues accelerating, investors are starting to realize that GPUs were only part of the equation. Memory and storage are now essential bottlenecks, sending shares of companies like Micron and Sandisk soaring.

Marvell could experience a similar shift in investor perception in 2027. The reason boils down to how AI spending is evolving. Hyperscalers aren't simply procuring more GPUs. They're building increasingly complex accelerated computing systems that require faster networking, greater bandwidth, and specialized processors designed for particular workloads.

As generative models become more sophisticated and inference deployments expand into new applications, efficiently moving data between processors becomes increasingly important. This is precisely where Marvell's optical networking, interconnect technologies, and custom silicon expertise converge.

Unlike some semiconductor companies waiting for future design wins, Marvell already has major customer programs underway. To get a grasp of how these relationships are impacting Marvell, consider that the company raised its fiscal 2028 revenue target from $18 billion to $20 billion. Importantly, Marvell's fiscal 2028 begins in early 2027 and ends in January 2028 -- meaning the majority of this projected growth will unfold during calendar 2027. Looking even further ahead, management expects total revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion in fiscal 2031. At the midpoint, that's nearly 10 times what Marvell generated during fiscal 2026.

This growth trajectory is why 2027 could represent the inflection point for Marvell. Nvidia has already established itself as the dominant platform for AI factories. Meanwhile, Micron continues to demonstrate the importance of high bandwidth memory and advanced DRAM. Marvell is approaching a period where its own revenue growth could make the importance of connectivity and custom silicon impossible to overlook. For growth investors looking for the next AI semiconductor breakout story, I consider Marvell stock an attractive long-term buy.

news.Title: Will Onto Innovation's Cash Balance Fuel Its Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc .'s ONTO cash balance provides ample financial flexibility to pursue growth opportunities across advanced packaging, metrology and AI infrastructure.

The company had $1.9 billion in cash and short-term investments at the end of the second quarter of 2026, supported by its recent financing activities and improving operational performance

In May, ONTO issued $1.5 billion of 0% convertible notes due in 2031. The financing generated about $1.2 billion in net cash after $300 million worth of share repurchases, capped calls and transaction costs.

Onto Innovation generated $62 million in cash from operations during the quarter. Quarterly revenues of $343.1 million rose 35.3% year over year and nearly 18% sequentially.

Onto Innovation Inc. Cash and Equivalents (Quarterly)

Onto Innovation Inc. cash-equivalents-quarterly | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

The company is leveraging its financial resources to strengthen the technology portfolio and capitalize on the growing opportunities. In August 2026, Onto Innovation completed its approximately $720 million acquisition of a 27% equity stake in Rigaku Holdings Corporation. This move is intended to accelerate joint development of next-generation X-ray-based process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing. Onto Innovation will account for the stake at fair value option and will not consolidate Rigaku's results.

On the last earnings call, management highlighted that the estimates for the semiconductor X-ray technology market is approximately $1 billion at present, with increasingly complex 3D transistor and packaging technology expected to create additional opportunities.

Onto Innovation Inc. Total Long Term Debt (Quarterly)

Onto Innovation Inc. total-long-term-debt-quarterly | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

However, the $1.5 billion convertible senior notes introduce financial obligations that could limit future flexibility. Although the zero-coupon structure eliminates regular interest payments, the notes mature in 2031 and require cash settlement of the principal if converted.

Further, the Rigaku investment represents a significant financial commitment. Rising expenses (certain material input costs, fuel surcharge and freight), increasing inventory requirements and supply-chain pressures also warrant monitoring amid intense competition in the semiconductor space.

Mapping the Competitive Terrain

KLA Corporation KLAC remains a formidable competitor. The company ended fiscal 2026 with $4.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. During the June quarter, KLA generated $906 million in operating cash flow and $817 million in free cash flow, while returning $876 million to its shareholders.

Story Continues

It is also investing in manufacturing capacity and next-generation product development to capitalize on AI-driven semiconductor demand. KLA expects advanced packaging process control systems' revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, up more than 70% year over year. However, at the end of fiscal 2026, the company had long-term debt of $5.89 billion.

Nova Ltd. NVMI ended second-quarter 2026 with more than $1.7 billion in cash and investments, providing flexibility for strategic growth initiatives, research and development ("R&D") and selective acquisitions. The company invests approximately 15% of revenues in R&D and recently expanded its California cleanroom, doubling U.S. manufacturing capacity.

In September, Nova authorized a share repurchase program up to $200 million, underscoring its focus on shareholder returns. Growing adoption of the Nova WMC platform and continued investment in AI-driven metrology solutions strengthen its competitive position.

ONTO Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

ONTO's shares have gained 8.5% in the past month, underperforming the Zacks Nanotechnology industry's growth of 11.3%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

On a forward price-to-earnings basis, ONTO's shares trade at 24.1X, higher than the industry's 4.66X.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ONTO has moved up for both 2026 and 2027 over the past 60 days.

Onto Innovation currently holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: MKSI vs. ROK: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
news.Content:
Investors looking for stocks in the Electronics - Miscellaneous Products sector might want to consider either MKS (MKSI) or Rockwell Automation (ROK). But which of these two stocks is more attractive to value investors? We'll need to take a closer look to find out.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The Zacks Rank favors stocks with strong earnings estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight companies with specific traits.

MKS and Rockwell Automation are both sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) right now. This means that both companies have witnessed positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that both of these stocks have an improving earnings outlook. However, value investors will care about much more than just this.

Value investors analyze a variety of traditional, tried-and-true metrics to help find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

The Value category of the Style Scores system identifies undervalued companies by looking at a number of key metrics. These include the long-favored P/E ratio, P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a variety of other fundamentals that help us determine a company's fair value.

MKSI currently has a forward P/E ratio of 18.85, while ROK has a forward P/E of 28.90. We also note that MKSI has a PEG ratio of 0.52. This popular metric is similar to the widely-known P/E ratio, with the difference being that the PEG ratio also takes into account the company's expected earnings growth rate. ROK currently has a PEG ratio of 2.04.

Another notable valuation metric for MKSI is its P/B ratio of 5.6. Investors use the P/B ratio to look at a stock's market value versus its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, ROK has a P/B of 13.73.

Based on these metrics and many more, MKSI holds a Value grade of B, while ROK has a Value grade of D.

Both MKSI and ROK are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that MKSI is the superior value option right now.

news.Title: BR Stock Rises 14.3% in Three Months: Here's What You Should Know
news.Content:
Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. BR stock has gained 14.3% over the past three months, marginally outpacing the industry's 14.2% growth and significantly outperforming the Zacks S&P 500 Composite's 2.5% return.

Three-Month Share Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Let us delve deeper into the factors contributing to the company's outperformance.

BR's High Recurring Revenues & Backlog Support Expansion

Broadridge's recurring revenue model, high client retention and expanding sales pipeline provide visibility into future growth. In fiscal 2026, recurring revenues rose 8% in constant currency to $4.9 billion, including 6% organic growth, while client retention remained at 98%. Record fourth-quarter closed sales of $158 million lifted the backlog to $470 million, up $40 million year over year. With its sales pipeline growing more than one-third, management projects fiscal 2027 recurring revenue growth of 6-8% and closed sales of $290-$330 million. Continued backlog conversion and new sales should support sustained organic growth and revenue visibility.

BR's AI-Led Innovation Drives Efficiency & Earnings Growth

Broadridge is leveraging agentic artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline operations, accelerate client onboarding and enhance its product offerings. AI-enabled and next-generation solutions accounted for nearly 40% of fiscal 2026 closed sales, reflecting increasing demand for advanced technology.

Management expects $25 million in AI-driven productivity savings in fiscal 2027, supporting reinvestment and operating leverage. Adjusted operating margin is projected to reach approximately 21%, up from 20.5% in fiscal 2026, while adjusted EPS is expected to rise 8-12%. Continued automation and operational efficiencies should strengthen profitability over time.

BR's Strong Cash Generation Supports Shareholder Returns

Broadridge's consistent cash generation supports strategic investments, acquisitions and shareholder returns. In fiscal 2026, operating cash flow reached $1.35 billion, while free cash flow totaled $1.23 billion, representing 110% of adjusted net earnings. The company returned more than $1 billion to shareholders through dividends and net share repurchases. A 12% dividend increase and continued buybacks reinforce its commitment to capital returns. Healthy cash flows and disciplined capital allocation should support long-term shareholder value.

BR's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Broadridge currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Cisco Systems carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. It has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 10.9%.

CSGP beat earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with an average earnings surprise of 21.2%.

news.Title: 台股藏「誘多紅K」訊號！專家曝3招操作：別吃短線回檔的虧
news.Content:
台股今（14）日盤中一度逼近49,000點關卡，終場上漲284.52點，收在48,625.83點。資深分析師周代運對此提出警告，直言今日尾盤暗藏隱性賣壓，屬於極重的「誘多」紅K，呼籲投資人切勿急著追高滿倉，以免「吃短線回檔的虧」。他更提出三招操作策略，建議再等兩天打底。

周代運分析，全年台股長線目標上看53000點，且這波中期多頭趨勢、AI半導體產業週期與法人資金進場邏輯全部完好無損。不過，從今日盤面細節來看，雖然小漲284點，但「誘多屬性極重」，全天最大問題在於尾盤出現隱性出貨。盤中雖靠AI與半導體小幅拉抬穩住散戶信心，但在最後一小時，權值股與中大型電子股卻出現無聲賣壓，呈現緩緩倒貨、邊拉邊出的標準法人操作手法。

此外，今日反彈呈現「大跌有量、反彈無量」的縮量格局，屬於典型的「修復中繼盤」，代表買盤並未真正歸隊，只是空方暫時停手休息。周代運預估，盤面浮籌尚未洗乾淨、高檔獲利盤未充分消化，加上外部數據的不確定性，未來兩天將持續走區間震盪、來回洗盤、假突破真回踩的節奏。他強調，長線53000點是今年的終點價，但多頭行情永遠是「漲一段、洗一段、換籌碼、再創高」，現階段貿然追高不僅賺不到波段，還會因短線震盪洗盤而打亂心態與節奏。

周代運提出以下三招操作邏輯：

第一招：長線底倉，穩穩抱住，一股不賣。 中期53000點目標不變，產業趨勢與資金格局沒有破壞，手中低位布局的主流族群無須被短線洗盤洗掉籌碼。

第二招：短線活倉，全面停手、不追任何反彈。 未來兩天所有盤中拉高皆為短線減碼點而非加碼點，在尾盤賣壓未出清、量能未補、底部未夯實前，堅決不開新倉。

news.Title: History Says This Happens to Taiwan Semiconductor Stock After Oct. 15
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE: TSM) has a big day coming up on Oct. 15: its third-quarter earnings announcement. This is one of only four times in the year to receive an update on how one of the world's most important companies is doing, and Wall Street is expecting quite the quarter. However, Taiwan Semiconductor has a habit of exceeding expectations, which could ignite another rally in the stock.

So, what does history have to say about Taiwan Semiconductor's potential following earnings? Let's find out.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

An immediate reaction isn't always the case with Taiwan Semiconductor

The chart shows Taiwan Semiconductor's price action after earnings.

TSM data by YCharts.

As you can see, in three of the last four earnings reports, Taiwan Semiconductor's stock either declined or was weak following earnings. That's odd, considering it beat consensus earnings-per-share estimates, and it may be a telling sign of what's to come when it reports.

However, there's a longer-term picture here: Taiwan Semiconductor's stock has always done well about a month or two after reporting earnings. I think this just points to the overall trend in the artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor industry , so even if TSMC's quarterly results fail to deliver a one-day price spike, there could still be substantial room to run.

The future looks bright for Taiwan Semiconductor

Taiwan Semiconductor is a logic chip manufacturer and makes chips for nearly every big tech company out there. Taiwan Semiconductor's size is unmatched, providing it with a competitive advantage over its peers. As a result of its connected status, it's a great heartbeat on the AI industry as a whole, and as AI spending ramps up, so will Taiwan Semiconductor's revenue growth.

For Q3, Wall Street analysts expect 47% revenue growth. For Q4, that figure climbs to 54%. Those would be the fastest rates TSMC has delivered over the past three years, which could make TSMC a great investment pick moving forward, as the market may not be ready for the growth it's expected to deliver.

TSM Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

Right now, TSMC is trading within its normal valuation range, at about 28 times forward earnings.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

While that's "normal," TSMC is also expected to grow faster than normal, so this valuation may actually be cheap. One of TSMC's largest clients, Nvidia , noted that next year data center capital expenditures from the big five AI hyperscalers are expected to rise from nearly $800 billion in 2026 to $1.3 trillion in 2027. With TSMC supplying chips to nearly every computing unit maker, this should result in strong future growth for it. As a result, Taiwan Semiconductor could be well-positioned to deliver strong end-of-year gains following its Q3 earnings report. While history doesn't support a one-day spike following earnings, a strong couple of months to close out the year could be in the cards.

Story Continues

Taiwan Semiconductor also has another catalyst in hand -- the company is raising foundry prices by 5% to 10% starting in 2027. While that won't help its third-quarter earnings, the price increase will add to TSMC's already impressive bottom line next year, particularly as its clients have nowhere else to go given TSMC's immense scale.

So, whether Taiwan Semiconductor's stock rallies immediately after earnings or a few months later, I think the long-term outlook for the stock is clear: Taiwan Semiconductor is a great buy today due to its leadership in chip fabrication. Without Taiwan Semiconductor, AI wouldn't look the same, and its status makes it a must-own stock.

news.Title: AI Memory Chip Selloff Looks Overblown: 2 Stocks to Buy on the Dip
news.Content:
Memory stocks are facing fresh selling pressure since Monday as investors question the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI)-related spending and worry about rising competition. The latest trigger came from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, which reported progress over the weekend on a new DRAM architecture that it claims could boost memory density by 30-50%, allowing more data to be stored in the same physical space.

The market reaction has been sharp. Per CNBC, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics dropped more than 10% and 7%, respectively, yesterday in Seoul. Both touched their lowest levels since August.

In the United States, Micron Technology MU, Sandisk Corporation SNDK, Seagate Technology Holdings STX and Western Digital Corporation WDC have also come under pressure. Over the past two trading sessions, shares of Micron, Sandisk, Seagate and Western Digital fell 4.4%, 6.2%, 4.5% and 4.1%, respectively, reflecting growing nervousness across the memory sector. Investors were already worried about how AI spending is being financed, so the CXMT news landed on a fragile market.

However, the sell-off may be getting ahead of itself. Although CXMT's technological progress could intensify competition over time, the company still needs to prove that it can manufacture its chips at scale. Legacy memory makers still hold a technological lead over CXMT.

For investors, this pullback could present an opportunity rather than a reason to panic. Micron and Sandisk are worth buying now on the recent dip, as both are set to benefit from continued demand for memory and storage driven by AI infrastructure.

Let's assess why these two stocks still offer attractive opportunities despite the recent volatility.

Micron

Micron closed fiscal 2026 on a strong note, with record revenues, high margins and strong cash generation. The outlook is even more striking. The company expects fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenues of $61.5 billion (plus or minus $1.5 billion) and adjusted earnings of $38.15 per share (plus or minus $1), implying roughly 351% revenue growth and 698% earnings growth from a year ago.

HBM revenues grew faster than Micron's total revenues in the fiscal fourth quarter, and the company has already contracted most of its 2027 HBM supply at significantly higher prices. Its HBM4 ramp is progressing, and it is working with NVIDIA on a custom HBM4E solution. NAND is a second engine, with data center SSD revenues approaching $10 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, more than 10 times the year-earlier level, as uses like KV-cache offload widen demand for fast storage. Further out, autonomous vehicles and humanoid robots should need far more memory and storage than today's devices.

Story Continues

Micron is also trying to make this boom more durable. It has signed 26 Strategic Customer Agreements, which are expected to account for more than 35% of revenues through 2030. Customer financial commitments have risen to $32 billion, mostly as cash deposits. That could soften the industry's usual boom-and-bust swings. New capacity is coming from the United States, Singapore, Japan and Taiwan, with Singapore HBM packaging due to start in early 2027 and the ID1 fab in mid-2027. Risks remain, including heavy capital spending and slower price increases, but fundamentals suggest that the long-term story is intact.

MU currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and has a VGM Score of A.

Micron Technology, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Micron Technology, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Micron Technology, Inc. Quote

Sandisk

Sandisk has become one of the biggest winners of the AI memory boom, and since its separation from Western Digital it offers a more direct way to invest in demand for NAND flash and data storage. The reason lies in how AI is changing storage needs. As inference and agentic AI generate more data that must be stored, retrieved and served with low delay, NAND is becoming central to architectures built around KV cache and RAG. Sandisk is scaling its datacenter business accordingly, widening its enterprise SSD range and moving toward QLC products. It now expects 2026 datacenter exabyte growth in the mid-70% range. It believes demand keeps rising on a rolling basis, and sees the enterprise datacenter flash market reaching about 1.2 zettabytes by 2030.

What sets Sandisk apart is its effort to escape NAND's usual swings in spot prices. Its eight New Business Model agreements are expected to cover more than half of its bits in fiscal 2027 and roughly two-thirds in fiscal 2028. At floor pricing, the signed deals represent at least $93.9 billion in revenues.

For fiscal first-quarter 2027, Sandisk expects revenues of $10.3 billion to $10.8 billion, up from $8.97 billion recorded in the last reported quarter. With multi-year agreements providing visibility and AI inference driving storage demand, the company looks well placed for the years ahead.

SNDK currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 and has a VGM Score of A.

news.Title: Cisco (CSCO): Can Its Earnings Recovery Turn Into Lasting Cash Growth?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO ) has an opportunity to turn artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending and network upgrades into stronger cash generation. Fiscal-2026 net income increased 30% to $13.3 billion, but operating cash flow stayed near $14.2 billion. Reported earnings also benefited from higher unrealized investment gains, which increased profit without generating operating cash. Cisco's cybersecurity business adds another growth avenue as companies strengthen their defenses against evolving threats. Find our rankings of cybersecurity stocks here.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) trades at approximately 20x forward earnings and 32x trailing earnings. The earnings outlook combines operating growth with accounting exclusions. Fiscal-2027 guidance calls for GAAP EPS of $4.00–$4.06, against $3.33 in fiscal 2026, and company-defined non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $5.05–$5.11. Adjustments include stock compensation, acquisition-related amortization, and restructuring. The lower forward multiple should not be read as pure profit growth.

Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) is the closest operating comparison because it competes in network switching. Its 45.4% second-quarter GAAP operating margin sets a high profitability benchmark for Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO). Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE:HPE) has greater server exposure, and its inventory commitments create a different cash-conversion test . The 20x forward valuation looks reasonable only if its fourth-quarter cash rebound persists.

Installed Networks Support Growth, but Require Funding

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) benefits from established enterprise networks, customer relationships, and the cost of replacing integrated equipment and software. Management says more than half its customers purchase both campus and data-center networking. That breadth creates opportunities to sell upgrades into existing relationships and spread development and support expenses across more revenue. Billionaire Ken Fisher also holds a position in Cisco, reflecting investor interest in the networking company. See which other AI stocks are on the billionaire's radar.

AI demand strengthens that opportunity. Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) booked $9.3 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026 and recognized about $4 billion in associated revenue. Management expects $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue in fiscal 2027. The difference between bookings and sales matters because large AI orders can arrive well before shareholder cash .

Story Continues

Revenue guidance of $72.2 billion–$73.4 billion implies approximately 15% growth at the midpoint. The adjusted EPS midpoint implies about 17% growth from fiscal-2026 adjusted EPS of $4.33. Those forecasts require operating leverage as shipments increase, while memory shortages and higher component prices can absorb part of the benefit.

Subscription revenue gives Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) a recurring base, but it increased only about 1% to $32.0 billion in fiscal 2026. Maintaining that base supports investment; it does not yet establish accelerating software cash growth. Hardware expansion still requires inventory purchases before customer payments arrive, and competitive pricing can limit the profit retained from additional shipments.

A Better Quarter Has Not Removed the Cash Burden

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) generated $5.4 billion of fourth-quarter operating cash flow, up 27%. That is meaningful evidence against treating the annual cash plateau as permanent. Fiscal 2026 also included the final $2.3 billion U.S. transition-tax payment, removing one specific future cash obligation.

Working capital nevertheless remains demanding. Annual inventory and financing-receivable movements absorbed approximately $2.5 billion and $1.8 billion, respectively. Both continued consuming cash in the fourth quarter, when their combined use approached $2.8 billion. Higher deferred revenue and other liabilities helped offset those demands. The rebound did not come from releasing inventory or collecting down customer financing.

Offering payment flexibility can support equipment sales, but customer financing earns its keep only when collections justify the risk . Persistently larger financing balances would tie up capital and reduce the cash available for distributions, even if reported sales and earnings continued growing.

Non-GAAP free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment, declined 4% to $12.8 billion as capital spending increased. Dividends and buybacks consumed approximately 99% of that amount. Sustaining distributions alongside growth investment therefore depends on better conversion, not simply higher accounting profit.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) produced $13.3 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2025 before the latest decline. The business has demonstrated substantial cash generation, but stronger AI demand now brings heavier funding requirements. At 20x forward earnings, shareholders need growth that increases cash after those commitments. More sales alone would provide little valuation protection if funding needs absorbed the additional profit.

Conclusion

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) looks reasonably valued at 20x forward earnings if the fourth-quarter cash recovery becomes sustained growth. Installed relationships and stronger infrastructure demand make that outcome credible. It requires earnings growth to produce more cash after investment, with inventory and financing needs growing more slowly than sales. Continued working-capital expansion alongside flat free cash flow would make the valuation demanding, even if orders remained strong.

While we acknowledge the potential of CSCO as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: AWS Backlog Hits $496 Billion While Cloud Margins Surge to 39% Making Amazon a Must-Own Growth Stock
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) has become one of the most compelling buys among Magnificent Seven stocks and large-cap growth stocks in general. There are two converging factors that make Amazon a screaming buy right now.

One is surging growth, supported by a massive $496 billion Amazon Web Services cloud computing backlog , which is contracts in the pipeline waiting to be executed upon. That is up more than double from the start of 2026 when it had just $244 billion in backlog.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That should allow Amazon to continue the momentum it has seen so far this year. The fiscal second quarter was Amazon's best quarter in more than four years. Overall revenue increased 20% to $200.6 billion, marking its best quarter of revenue growth since 2021.

Operating margin rises 650 basis points

Amazon's cash cow, its AWS business, saw sales jump 37%, marking its best results in 18 quarters. In addition, Amazon saw its AWS operating margin jump 650 basis points to 39.4%, up from 32.9% in Q2 2025. If you exclude a one-time accounting gain, its a 520 basis point increase.

Overall, net income rose to $62.6 billion Q2, or $5.75 per share, up from $1.68 per share in Q2 2025. That is skewed by a huge $53.4 billion gain from its investment in Anthropic, but it still beat adjusted earnings estimates. That is significant growth, especially in the face of huge capital expenditures, which had concerned a lot of investors earlier this year, thinking it would crush earnings.

That leads to the second major factor that makes Amazon a buy: its valuation.

Too cheap to ignore

Amazon stock started the year trending lower out of concerns about its then $200 billion proposed for capital expenditures, now $220 billion. Investors were worried earlier this year for a few reasons -- one, the number was 50% higher than 2025; two, its AWS cloud business saw slowing growth and was losing market share; and three, it would eat into their free cash flow and lead to negative cash flow in Q2.

The stock price has since recovered and is now up about 13% year-to-date. As noted, the concerns about overspending on capex were somewhat alleviated by surging growth, an overflowing pipeline, and the realization that the spending is needed to meet demand.

Cash flow was negative in Q2, but CEO Andy Jassy said on the recent earnings call that "when demand is necessitating so many data centers being built simultaneously in advance of when we can start monetizing them, we'll spend a lot of capex and encounter free cash flow headwinds until these data centers come online." But after a few years when the servers are being used, revenue growth will outpace capex growth and free cash flow will return -- at least that's the plan.

Story Continues

Despite these cash flow headwinds, Amazon looks like a must own stock right now for not just its growth, but its cheap valuation. It is trading at around 20 times earnings, which is near the lowest it has been in more than 10 years. It is a compelling buy at this valuation, given its overflowing near half a trillion dollar pipeline.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

news.Title: Michael Burry Questions Microsoft’s AI Spending. Is Its Valuation Misleading?
news.Content:
Michael Burry has questioned whether Microsoft's AI spending is driven by necessity, suggesting the company may be using its financial figures as leverage, according to Seeking Alpha. He argues Big Tech is spending wildly because it assumes it will be granted an oligopoly too big to fail. Michael Burry reportedly owns Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ) shares and long-dated call options, so this is skepticism about spending, not a short thesis.

Separately, the company made an accounting change at the start of fiscal 2027: it now assumes its data centers and office buildings last 25 years instead of 15. It's worth examining because it changes how that spending is reported. Microsoft's AI spending is under scrutiny, but its cybersecurity business offers another investment angle. See where it stands in our list of the 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy According to Analysts .

Why I Think Burry Has a Point

Microsoft counts finance leases in its capex but leaves out operating leases. One key test for a finance lease is whether it covers most of a building's useful life. With buildings now expected to last 25 years, more leases fall short of that bar and become operating leases. As a result, Microsoft's calendar 2026 capex forecast dropped from about $190 billion to about $175 billion. CFO Amy Hood said that outside of this change, the company's spending plans were unchanged. So the $15 billion drop came from accounting. Microsoft has also signed a huge number of new data center leases. Leases that haven't started yet jumped from $196.6 billion to $329.1 billion in just one quarter. Under the revised lease classifications, more future data center leases will be treated as operating leases rather than included in Microsoft's reported capex. With the company's future data center commitments rising despite a lower capex forecast, investors may want to see which other growth stocks billionaires are backing , including MSFT.

The Valuation Isn't Quite What It Seems

On paper, Microsoft looks reasonably priced. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 26.80x sits about 12% below its 5-year average of 30.51x. Analysts expect EPS to grow 14% this fiscal year, then about 20% and 22% over the next two. The same accounting change also affects earnings. The issue is that the same accounting change affects both earnings and how spending is reported. For a new building, stretching its assumed life from 15 to 25 years cuts yearly depreciation by about 40%. Microsoft says the boost to fiscal 2027 operating income will be minimal, but as more buildings come online, earnings will look better than they would have under the old rules. Meanwhile, the $329.1 billion in leases yet to begin won't appear on the balance sheet until they start, so investors have to track them separately. So earnings could look stronger, and obligations smaller, than they really are. That's why I don't think the stock is quite as cheap as its P/E makes it look.

Story Continues

Hedge fund interest cooled slightly. Funds holding Microsoft fell from 282 in Q1 to 273 in Q2. The value of their stakes, though, rose from $63.6 billion to $66.5 billion.

Microsoft did disclose this change on its earnings call. Still, Burry is right that the headline capex number no longer tells the full story, and Microsoft's valuation may be more demanding than its reported earnings multiple suggests. I'd track total lease commitments alongside capex to see what Microsoft is really spending,

While we acknowledge the potential of MSFT as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: PAYX Shares Rise 17.7% in Six Months: Here's What You Should Know
news.Content:
Paychex PAYX stock has gained 17.7% over the past six months compared with the industry's 22.9% growth. The Zacks S&P 500 Composite gained 10.7% during the same period.

Six-Month Share Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Let us delve deeper into the factors contributing to the company's strong performance.

AI-Driven Innovation to Boost Growth & Margins

Paychex is leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) to expand its offerings, enhance service delivery and improve efficiency. Its WISE platform uses more than 50 trillion proprietary data points to streamline payroll and HR workflows. In a pilot covering more than 50,000 businesses, WISE helped prevent approximately 90% of targeted payroll errors. The company has deployed more than 2,000 AI agents and features, increasing automated payroll processing by nearly 20% from January through August 2026. New offerings such as WISE Hire and WISE Pro drive revenue growth, while greater automation supports productivity and margin expansion.

Paycor Integration Boosts PAYX Cross-Selling Opportunities

The Paycor acquisition has expanded Paychex's enterprise reach and cross-selling opportunities across HR, benefits and advisory solutions. Its One Paychex strategy supports broader product adoption and higher customer value. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, enterprise bookings grew at a double-digit rate, while broker referrals rose 43% year over year. The rollout of Paychex Perks to approximately 2.5 million Paycor employees further expands cross-selling potential. Continued revenue synergies, wider distribution and improving sales productivity support long-term growth.

PAYX's Recurring Revenues & Cost Discipline Support Margins

Paychex's recurring revenue model, improving client retention and pricing power underpin its earnings growth. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, revenues rose 6% to $1.6 billion, while adjusted EPS increased 10% to $1.34. Adjusted operating margin expanded 130 basis points to 42%, aided by productivity gains and cost discipline. Management reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook of 5-6% and adjusted operating margin target of approximately 44%. Continued pricing gains, higher product penetration and AI-driven efficiencies should support sustained profitability and earnings growth.

PAYX's Cash Generation Supports Shareholder Returns

Paychex's consistent cash generation supports dividends and disciplined capital allocation. In fiscal 2026, operating cash flow reached $2.6 billion and free cash flow totaled $2.3 billion, with $2.2 billion returned to shareholders. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, the company paid $424.1 million in dividends, while operating cash flow reached $413.5 million despite tax payment timing effects. Continued earnings growth and prudent capital deployment should sustain long-term shareholder returns.

Story Continues

PAYX's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Paychex currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) at present.

A couple of better-ranked stocks in the broader Computer and Technology sector are Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO and CoStar Group, Inc. CSGP.

Cisco Systems carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. It has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 10.9%. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

CSCO beat earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, delivering an earnings surprise of 2.6%, on average.

CoStar Group also holds a Zacks Rank of 2 at present. It has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 36.6%.

news.Title: Advanced Micro Devices Stock Surges 183% YTD: Time to Hold or Exit?
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices AMD shares have surged 182.8% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's increase of 22.7% and the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry's rise of 123.1%

AMD shares have also outperformed peers, including NVIDIA NVDA, Broadcom AVGO, and Intel INTC, year-to-date. NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Intel shares gained 22.6%, 3.3% and 178.6%, respectively, over the same time frame.

The outperformance reflects accelerating AI infrastructure investment, strong demand for EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators, and expanding hyperscaler deployments. Strong adoption of Ryzen processors, growing enterprise market share and strategic AI partnerships with OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic and Microsoft are strengthening its growth prospects.

AMD Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMD Benefits From Expanding Data Center Footprint

Advanced Micro Devices is benefiting from accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, strong demand for EPYC server CPUs and growing adoption of Instinct accelerators. The company's expanding data center footprint, supported by partnerships with hyperscalers and AI developers, is strengthening its competitive position and driving revenue growth.

The company's Data Center revenues surged 107% year over year to a record $6.7 billion in the second quarter of 2026, which accounted for 58% of total revenues. Strong demand for fifth-generation EPYC Turin processors and MI350 Series accelerators drove growth. Expanding deployments across Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Oracle are further strengthening AMD's presence in cloud infrastructure.

AMD's expanding AI infrastructure portfolio remains a key growth driver. AMD recently introduced AMD Helion, an open rack-scale infrastructure blueprint designed to support agentic AI workloads across hyperscale data centers and enterprises. Based on Open Compute Project specifications, Helion offers flexible CPU-only and integrated CPU/GPU configurations.

The CPU-only rack, powered by sixth-generation AMD EPYC processors, supports up to 32,768 cores, while the integrated configuration combines EPYC CPUs with Instinct MI350P GPUs. The platform incorporates open software, intelligent token routing and flexible cooling options to optimize performance, power efficiency and costs. AMD expects Helion configurations to become available in November 2026.

AMD's Helios platform, powered by EPYC Venice CPUs, MI450 GPUs and Pensando networking, has been a key catalyst. Partnerships with OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic and Microsoft support accelerating deployments. AMD expects the Data Center business to more than double in 2027, while server CPU revenues are projected to increase more than 80% year over year in the second half of 2026 and more than 70% in 2027.

Story Continues

AMD Initiates Strong Q3 View

AMD's expanding AI infrastructure portfolio, stronger hyperscaler partnerships, and robust demand for EPYC processors and Instinct accelerators are expected to drive top-line growth. For the third quarter of 2026, AMD expects revenues of approximately $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million. The midpoint implies growth of roughly 41% year over year and 13% sequentially.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMD's third-quarter 2026 revenues is pegged at $13.07 billion, suggesting growth of 41.34% year over year.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.92 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days and indicates 60% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Price and Consensus

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Quote

AMD Suffers From Stiff Competition, Supply Constraints

Despite its expanding portfolio, AMD faces stiff competition from NVIDIA, Broadcom and Intel. AMD continues to face intense competition in AI accelerators and server processors from NVIDIA's AI GPUs and Intel's CPUs. Intel is aggressively working to regain server market share through its expanding Xeon roadmap, Intel Foundry and advanced packaging technologies. Broadcom is increasing competitive pressure on AMD by strengthening its position in custom AI accelerators and high-performance networking for hyperscale customers.

Supply availability remains one of AMD's biggest headwinds. Management said wafers, advanced process-node capacity, HBM, advanced packaging, substrates and several other components remain tight. AMD has been raising capital spending and working across its supply chain to expand capacity, but demand still runs ahead of supply in some areas.

The increasing contribution from data center AI accelerators and MI450 gross margins, which carry slightly below the company average, could constrain margin expansion. Softer PC demand, declining gaming revenues and reliance on large AI customers could also weigh on AMD's performance.

AMD Shares Trade at a Premium

AMD shares trade at a premium, as reflected in a Value Score of F.

AMD stock trades at a forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E) of 49.86X compared with the broader sector's 20.77X.

AMD Valuation

Here's Why AMD Stock is a Hold Now

AMD's expanding Data Center footprint, strong EPYC demand and accelerating Instinct GPU adoption position the company well to capitalize on the rapidly growing AI infrastructure market. However, stiff competition, supply constraints and stretched valuation remain concerns. Therefore, despite strong AI-driven growth prospects and recent share-price momentum, investors may prefer to wait for a more attractive entry point in AMD shares.

news.Title: Guggenheim lifts Meta target as Muse usage builds
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Guggenheim raised its price target on Meta Platforms to $850 from $700 in a note to clients on Wednesday, pointing to higher 2027 estimates and early traction for the company's Muse AI agent.

Analyst Michael Morris told investors that Muse's usage trajectory and engagement depth are "the primary swing factor for sentiment heading into the 3Q call."

Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users through five weeks, up from 0.3 million in its first week, according to Apptopia.

Even so, that represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily users, and Morris expects management to prioritize scaling usage over near-term monetization.

Over time, he believes Muse will make money mainly through businesses paying to reach consumers via their agents, consistent with Meta's core advertising model, rather than through consumer spending. He pointed to the Shopify and PayPal checkout integrations as early evidence.

Morris called Muse Wonder, launched Oct. 12, an important catalyst if it strengthens the agentic product. He said "a frontier model race without a link to agentic leadership is a competitive cost center rather than a growth investment," and will be listening for management to draw that connection.

"The prevailing concern is that a rival leapfrogs Muse or Wonder and locks Meta into a perpetual over-investment cycle, though in our view Meta's track record (WhatsApp globally, Reels vs. TikTok) and the feedback loop from free distribution to 3.6bn users position the company as the most likely scaled leader," the analyst added,

news.Title: Apple is finally taking the smart home seriously
news.Content:
Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app. But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ).

That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView . Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home .

"Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," Counterpoint Research research director Mohit Agrawal said in a note following Apple's Welcome Home event on Tuesday.

"Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added.

Apple's smarter home

The HomeView takes a lot of its software design cues from the Apple Watch , complete with a series of built-in clock faces. There's a hub screen that lets you control your smart home devices, such as lights, locks, and thermostats, as well as an iPhone-like home screen where you can open apps like FaceTime or Messages.

Users can also view multiple smart camera feeds, use the HomeView's built-in camera as a vanity mirror before they head out the door, and look up things like recipes from their iPhones and then project them on the screen.

Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView. Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions.

The company designed the HomeView to recognize six faces via its facial recognition camera. If you want to access your personal messages, calendar, and so on, you'll need your iPhone on the same Wi-Fi network as the hub so it can authenticate you.

Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup.

The new hardware provides users with a long-awaited Apple-built solution for controlling smart home devices. To date, customers have had to wrangle a collection of do-it-yourself options, such as using iPads as wall-mounted command centers.

HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories .

Story Continues

The company has also partnered with LG and Schneider Electr ic to produce new smart door locks, thermostats, and indoor and outdoor cameras.

But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather.

I've been using Siri AI on my iPhone for the past several weeks, and it's proven to be quite helpful when it comes to asking questions related to texts and emails, such as requesting the name of a restaurant my friend suggested I check out.

But I haven't been able to try the AI assistant with HomeView just yet. Whether it works as advertised will be integral to the overall experience.

"Generative AI has raised expectations for conversational ease and genuinely useful assistance, and Siri has consistently lagged," Forrester vice president and principal analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee said in a press statement.

"The critical question is whether the new Siri capabilities can close that gap and make Apple's home experience as intuitive and compelling as its best products," he explained.

If Apple's strategy to take smart home share from Amazon and Google succeeds, it could provide a boost to the company's bottom line while helping to ensure increased lock-in among its customers.

Apple doesn't break out specific revenue numbers for its smart home sales, instead lumping them in with wearables and accessories. That segment represented $35.69 billion of the company's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025.

That's better than its Mac and iPad businesses, but nowhere near its Services division, which brought in $109.15 billion, or its iPhone arm, which generated $209.59 billion in the same period.

news.Title: 股價區間曝光！ 台積電法說會倒數引爆對決 多空豪賭2.57兆元行情
news.Content:
晶圓代工龍頭台積電15日將舉行法說會，成為股價下一步走勢的重要觀察點。儘管第3季營收已優於財測，市場利多提前反映，投資人接下來更關注毛利率、第4季營運展望，以及AI需求能否支撐目前的高估值。外媒報導，選擇權市場預期台積電財報公布後股價可能波動約4%，以公司約2.1兆美元市值計算，牽動的市值可能超過800億美元（約新台幣2.57兆元）。

台積電ADR周二收在445.12美元，較10月初高點下跌約9%。儘管股價回檔，選擇權市場仍預期財報公布後可能出現明顯反應，顯示市場正等待新的營運訊號。

選擇權預告股價波動4％ 毛利率成財報焦點

據財經媒體《Invezz》報導，10月16日到期的選擇權顯示，台積電財報公布後的預期股價波動幅度約為4%。截至周二收盤，履約價445美元的買權與賣權合計約18美元，對應的股價區間約為427至463美元。

市場部位也集中在接近現價的履約價。450美元買權未平倉合約超過9500口，440美元賣權則超過6000口，這些價位可作為觀察財報後短期股價反應的參考。

由於第3季營收數字已經揭曉，利潤率將是市場檢視的重點。台積電第3季營收達新台幣1.49兆元，約467億美元，年增50%，高於原先446億至458億美元的財測。

不過，台積電先前預估第3季毛利率為65%至67%，營業利益率為56%至58%，均低於第2季的67.7%與60.3%。市場將關注實際表現是否符合預期，以及獲利能力能否支撐股價。

分析師看好獲利成長 第4季財測更受關注

倫敦證券交易所集團（LSEG）的SmartEstimate預測，台積電第3季淨利將年增65%，達新台幣7463億元，有望連續第6季創下獲利紀錄。

美國銀行分析師Haas Liu預期，第3季毛利率將接近67%，第4季營收則可望季增10%至15%。他也將台積電ADR目標價由590美元上調至620美元，並認為以2027年預估獲利計算，約16倍的本益比並不高。

相較於單季獲利，第4季展望可能更直接影響市場對台積電後續成長的評價。摩根士丹利分析師預期，台積電可能將2026年營收成長預測，由目前的超過40%上調至400%出頭至400%中段的區間。法說會對未來營收成長的說明，將成為投資人判斷股價能否獲得進一步支撐的關鍵。

AI需求與資本支出 左右台積電估值能否維持

除了財報數字，台積電能否持續受惠於AI需求，同時控制先進製程與海外擴廠成本，也是市場關注的焦點。

台積電今年7月將2026年資本支出預測上調至600億至640億美元。美國銀行分析師Haas Liu預估，今年支出約630億美元，2027年可能高達830億美元，主要用於擴充3奈米、2奈米、A16製程及先進封裝產能。

投資人將關注輝達與客製化AI加速器需求、CoWoS先進封裝產能，以及2奈米製程進度。由於新製程成本較高，在產能利用率提升前，可能對毛利率形成壓力。

因此，這場法說會不只是檢視台積電第3季是否再創獲利紀錄，更重要的是公司能否提出足以支撐未來成長的展望。若毛利率與第4季營運指引優於市場預期，將有助

news.Title: Arm vs. Sandisk: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in October?
news.Content:
Choosing between high-margin design licensing and high-volume hardware manufacturing is a classic dilemma for investors. Your choice between Arm (NASDAQ:ARM) and Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) depends on your preference for valuation versus growth.

Arm focuses on the architectural blueprints of modern computing, while Sandisk manufactures the actual memory components required to store and process data. Both companies are positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of AI, but their financial structures and market roles are vastly different.

The case for Arm

As a leading developer of processor designs, the company is a central figure among semiconductor stocks by licensing its blueprints to global hardware manufacturers. Arm does not produce chips itself but instead collects royalties and licensing fees from companies that use its architecture in smartphones, laptops, and data centers. This business model enables a high degree of scalability because the company avoids the massive capital costs of operating its own factories.

In fiscal 2026 (ending in March), revenue reached $4.9 billion -- a 23% year-over-year increase over the previous year. This expansion helped the company achieve a net income of $698 million. While the business continues to grow its top line, the net margin (the percentage of revenue retained as profit) is about 14%, reflecting stable profitability for a design-focused firm.

As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio (a measure of a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with short-term assets) stands at approximately 5.3x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.1x, indicating that the company's debt is low relative to its equity.

On a trailing 12-month basis, free cash flow was $705 million. However, stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 69% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow.

The case for Sandisk

Sandisk specializes in NAND flash memory products used in everything from consumer mobile devices to enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure. The company serves a wide array of original equipment manufacturers and cloud service providers. In its latest annual report, it noted that no single customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue. This diversification helps mitigate the risk of losing a primary buyer, although the business remains sensitive to the broader demand for storage hardware.

In fiscal 2026 (ending in July), revenue reached $20 billion, representing a massive 175% increase over the prior year. Net income was $11.4 billion for the period, marking a significant turnaround from previous years. This resulted in a net margin of nearly 56%, highlighting how effectively the business capitalized on rising demand and pricing for memory storage solutions.

Story Continues

Based on its July 2026 balance sheet, Sandisk maintains a current ratio of approximately 2.3x, and the company maintains a solid financial position with zero debt.

Free cash flow for the period reached nearly $11.5 billion, providing the business with significant capital to reinvest in its technology or return to its owners through other means.

Risk profile comparison

Arm faces competition from other chip architectures, including open-source alternatives that could challenge its licensing dominance. Furthermore, its heavy concentration in the smartphone market makes it vulnerable to any slowdown in consumer electronics spending. Because the company relies on a royalty-based model, any shift in how its partners design their hardware could directly impact its long-term revenue streams.

Sandisk relies heavily on its joint ventures with Kioxia for its supply of flash memory, creating a strategic dependency that financial or operational issues could disrupt at its partner. The storage market is also notoriously cyclical and faces intense competition from Samsung Electronics , Micron Technology , and SK Hynix .

Valuation comparison

Sandisk appears significantly cheaper than Arm on both an earnings and sales basis, reflecting the market's high growth expectations for the chip designer.

Metric

10.5x

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The Forward P/E compares the current stock price to future earnings estimates for the next year. The P/S ratio measures the market value of the company compared to its sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

I would buy Sandisk. While it operates in a more competitive and volatile industry, where memory prices have historically fluctuated wildly based on demand/supply dynamics, it is benefiting from substantial demand for flash memory that exceeds what the industry can supply -- and this situation could last for another few years.

Arm offers more consistent, high-margin growth from its licensing business model. However, the stock's high forward P/E prices in a lot of growth, leaving relatively lower upside compared to Sandisk.

The market is still pricing Sandisk like a cyclical memory supplier, despite the industry shifting to long-term customer agreements. Sandisk has signed eight of these so far, which put a floor under selling prices. These deals don't completely remove the risk of lower revenue and earnings if memory pricing drops, but it means Sandisk can still earn a healthy profit margin in the next downturn. Management said on the recent earnings call that these strategic agreements will make up two-thirds of bits shipped by fiscal 2028.

It's a high-risk, high-reward proposition, but it's one I would be willing to make, especially compared to paying over 100x earnings for Arm.
