news.Title: Will Rising Capex Weigh on Oracle's Free Cash Flow Outlook?
news.Content:
Oracle 's ORCL aggressive AI infrastructure buildout has put its free cash flow (FCF) outlook under scrutiny. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, capital expenditures jumped to $28.5 billion from $8.5 billion a year ago, pushing FCF to negative $5.4 billion despite record operating cash flow of $23 billion, up 184% year over year. Net of customer prepayments, cash capex was about $18 billion.

Guidance indicates the pressure will persist. Oracle reiterated fiscal 2027 capex of $90-$95 billion, with net cash capex capped at $70 billion, and has not set a timeline for FCF to turn positive after a negative $23.7 billion in fiscal 2026. The company plans to raise about $40 billion in debt and equity this year, including a $20 billion at-the-market stock sale completed in the first quarter, which dilutes shareholders. Gross margin is also expected to decline in fiscal 2027 as new sites ramp.

Still, the demand backdrop supports the spending. Remaining performance obligations rose $209 billion year over year to $664 billion, aided by more than $30 billion in new AI cloud contracts that Oracle said require no incremental capital raising and largely affect capex only from fiscal 2028. The company delivered 850 megawatts of capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs, while cloud infrastructure revenues surged 121% to $7.4 billion. Management expects projects to generate strong FCF soon after ramping, with conversion potentially near 100% of post-tax EBITDA.

For second-quarter fiscal 2027, Oracle expects total revenue growth of 30-34% and cloud revenue growth of 65-71% in USD, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.85-$1.93. Full-year revenues are now projected at a minimum of $90 billion, with non-GAAP EPS raised to $8.10 from $8.05. While the revenue trajectory is encouraging, FCF is likely to remain negative in the near term, making capex discipline and the upcoming Oct. 28 Investor Day key to watch.

How ORCL's Capex Strategy Compares With Microsoft & Amazon

Oracle's cash-flow strain mirrors a broader AI spending wave among U.S. hyperscalers. Microsoft MSFT spent $41 billion on capex, including finance leases, in fourth-quarter fiscal 2026, up 69% year over year, yet Microsoft still generated $19.6 billion in FCF, though down 23%. Microsoft expects FCF to stay positive in fiscal 2027. Amazon AMZN raised its 2026 capex outlook to $220 billion from $200 billion after second-quarter capex climbed to $54.2 billion from $32.1 billion. Consequently, Amazon's trailing 12-month FCF swung to an outflow of $7.6 billion from an inflow of $18.2 billion, leaving Amazon's cash profile closer to Oracle's current position.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: Tesla (TSLA) Q3 Earnings Expected to Decline
news.Content:
Tesla (TSLA) is expected to deliver a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 21, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

For Tesla, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -11.35%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #4.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Tesla will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Tesla would post earnings of $0.5 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.33, delivering a surprise of -34.00%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates two times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Tesla doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

An Industry Player's Expected Results

news.Title: IBM Stock Before Q3 Earnings Release: To Buy or Not to Buy?
news.Content:

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for sales and earnings is pegged at $16.84 billion and $2.87 per share, respectively. Earnings estimates for IBM for 2026 have remained static at $12.33 per share over the past 60 days, but are up 0.08% for 2027 to $13.20.

IBM Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Earnings Surprise History

The cloud and data platform provider delivered a four-quarter earnings surprise of 4.6%, on average, beating estimates thrice. In the last reported quarter, the company matched the earnings estimate.

Earnings Whispers

Our proven model does not predict an earnings beat for IBM for the third quarter. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the chances of an earnings beat. This is not the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

IBM currently has an ESP of -0.63% with a Zacks Rank #3. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the third quarter, IBM entered into a multi-year, $240 million agreement with Together AI to support the growing demand for enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) inference. The partnership will enable IBM to expand its cloud infrastructure offerings for open-source AI workloads and strengthen its position in the rapidly growing AI infrastructure market. IBM also introduced a new set of AI-powered experiences for the 2026 U.S. Open to make live tennis more personalized, informative and interactive for millions of fans worldwide. By turning complex court-level data into accessible insights, the company helped fans better understand the game through advanced technology. Such investments in innovation and collaborations will likely boost IBM's commercial prospects and are likely to have generated incremental revenues for the Software segment.

During the to-be-reported quarter, IBM partnered with India-based AI company Sarvam to develop and test sovereign AI technologies for government agencies and regulated industries in the subcontinent. The collaboration aims to build AI systems that give organizations greater control over data, governance and operations while supporting digital transformation across the public sector. IBM also collaborated with Arm Holdings plc ARM to give enterprises more software choices for mission-critical workloads. IBM's latest processor will enable Arm-native Linux environments to run alongside z/OS and Linux on IBM Z, giving enterprises access to a broader software ecosystem while maintaining security, reliability and scalability. These are likely to have generated additional revenues for the Consulting segment.

However, despite solid hybrid cloud, quantum technology and AI traction, IBM faces stiff competition from Amazon Web Services and Microsoft's Azure. The company is also facing challenges from AI firm Anthropic as the latter's Claude Code tool can modernize legacy COBOL systems — a foundational programming language deeply embedded in IBM's mainframe ecosystem. By proposing to substantially automate code exploration, documentation, refactoring and security analysis, Claude Code threatens to reduce enterprises' reliance on specialized legacy service providers like IBM, putting its business model at stake. This is likely to redefine the competitive landscape, leading to a broad-based downslide across the sector. Increasing pricing pressure is eroding margins, and profitability has trended down over the years, barring occasional spikes.

Story Continues

Price Performance

Over the past year, IBM has plummeted 17.8% against the industry's rise of 140.6%, lagging its peers like Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN. While Microsoft has gained 5.8%, Amazon surged 19.8% over this period.

One-Year IBM Stock Price Performance

Key Valuation Metric

From a valuation standpoint, IBM appears to be trading at a premium relative to the industry and above its mean. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company shares currently trade at 17.73 forward earnings, higher than 10.74 for the industry and the stock's mean of 17.2.

Investment Considerations

IBM aims to benefit from the increasing propensity of business enterprises to undertake a cloud-agnostic and interoperable approach to secure multi-cloud management with a diligent focus on hybrid cloud and generative AI solutions. With a surge in traditional cloud-native workloads and associated applications, along with a rise in generative AI deployment and quantum computing, there is a radical expansion in the number of cloud workloads that enterprises are currently managing. This has resulted in heterogeneous, dynamic and complex infrastructure strategies, which have led to a healthy demand trend.

However, IBM's margins might have been strained by limited cost-cutting opportunities and intense competitive pressures, likely delaying key product launches. Stiff competition from established players and new challengers has dented its growth prospects. Management observed that rapidly evolving, industry-wide cybersecurity concerns adversely impacted the client's buying patterns as quarterly capex spending shifted more toward servers, storage and memory purchases. This is likely to have affected its Infrastructure business in the quarter.

End Note

IBM is trading at a premium valuation, and investors could wait for a better entry point to cash in on its long-term fundamentals. The stock has also witnessed a downtrend in its price performance over the past year. Consequently, it might be prudent to trade with caution at the moment.

IBM expects its growth to be driven primarily by analytics, cloud computing and security services. A better business mix, improving operating leverage through productivity gains and increased investments in growth opportunities will likely be conducive to long-term growth. IBM is expected to benefit in the long run from strong demand for hybrid cloud and AI, which will likely drive growth in the Software and Consulting segments. Investors might therefore hold the stock for long-term gains.

news.Title: Wall Street Analysts See a 25.6% Upside in Lam Research (LRCX): Can the Stock Really Move This High?
news.Content:
Lam Research (LRCX) closed the last trading session at $301.11, gaining 11.2% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $378.2 indicates a 25.6% upside potential.

The average comprises 30 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $260.00 to a high of $500.00, with a standard deviation of $52.84. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 13.7% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 66.1% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.

However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in LRCX. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Story Continues

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Here's Why There Could be Plenty of Upside Left in LRCX

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0.2% over the past month, as two estimates have gone higher compared to no negative revision.

Moreover, LRCX currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much LRCX could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

news.Title: ASML Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Upgrade Demand, Revenues Miss
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $12.93 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $12.47 by 3.69%. Earnings increased 135.9% year over year. Revenues of $11.66 billion missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $13.18 billion by 11.49% but increased 55.2% year over year.

The performance benefited from a strong demand for lithography systems and productivity upgrades, supported by accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) investments. Installed Base Management revenues surged 67.6% year over year, while gross margin expanded significantly on favorable sales mix and higher volumes.

ASML Holding N.V. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

ASML Holding N.V. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ASML Holding N.V. Quote

System Sales Rise on Strong Customer Demand

Net system sales increased 50.8% year over year and 27.5% sequentially. The company sold 121 lithography systems during the quarter compared with 72 in the year-ago period and 91 in the preceding quarter.

Installed Base Management revenues increased 67.6% year over year and 19.1% sequentially. The business benefited from strong customer demand for productivity upgrades, which enable chipmakers to increase manufacturing capacity using existing equipment.

Management highlighted that Installed Base Management revenues exceeded its guidance by approximately 13.8%. The stronger-than-expected performance reflected customers' urgency to expand production capacity amid increasing demand for advanced semiconductor technologies.

Broad-Based Lithography Growth

Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) systems accounted for 46% of third-quarter net system sales, while ArFi immersion systems contributed 36%. KrF, ArF dry and metrology and inspection equipment accounted for the remaining revenues.

The company sold 17 EUV systems, compared with 16 in the preceding quarter. ArFi system sales increased to 40 units from 23 sequentially, reflecting stronger demand for immersion lithography equipment.

Logic applications represented 54% of net system sales, while memory accounted for 46%. Geographically, Taiwan contributed 32% of system revenues, followed by South Korea at 31% and China at 23%. The United States accounted for 13%, with the rest of Asia contributing 1%.

Profitability Improves on Favorable Product Mix

Gross profit increased 72.7% year over year, supported by stronger system sales and productivity upgrades. Gross margin expanded 590 basis points to 57.5% from 51.6% in the prior-year quarter. Sequentially, gross margin improved 350 basis points.

Research and development expenses increased 5.9% year over year, while selling, general and administrative expenses rose 16.3%. Despite higher operating expenses, operating income surged 109.6% year over year. Operating margin expanded to 44.4% from 32.8%.

Net income increased 133.5% year over year. The result included a gain on equity investments related primarily to the revaluation of ASML's initial investment in Mistral AI. Net profit margin expanded to 42.5% from 28.3% a year earlier.

Story Continues

Cash Flow and Liquidity Strengthen

Operating cash flow improved significantly during the quarter, supported by favorable changes in assets and liabilities. Free cash flow also increased substantially from the year-ago period, reflecting stronger cash generation despite higher capital expenditures.

Cash and cash equivalents increased 20.4% sequentially, while total cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments rose 68.0%. Inventories increased 1.4% from the second quarter, reflecting continued investment in manufacturing operations.

ASML repurchased approximately 2.8 million shares during the third quarter under its existing 2026-2028 share repurchase program. The company also announced a second interim dividend for 2026, payable Nov. 4, 2026.

Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, ASML expects continued revenue growth, supported by strong semiconductor equipment demand and higher Installed Base Management sales. Gross margin is projected at approximately 57%, reflecting a favorable business mix and increasing upgrade activity.

For full-year 2026, management expects revenues to increase approximately 36% year over year, with gross margin around 56%. EUV revenues are expected to increase more than 45%, while non-EUV revenues are projected to grow approximately 20%. Installed Base Management revenues are anticipated to rise around 50%.

Management also expects China to account for approximately 20% of total revenues for 2026. Higher equipment volumes, favorable product mix and growing demand for upgrades remain important contributors to the company's profitability outlook.

ASML Accelerates Capacity Expansion Plans

Management highlighted strengthening demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment as customers expand capacity to support AI-related investments. Customers anticipate that semiconductor supply constraints could persist through at least 2028, with some expressing interest in placing orders for 2029 and 2030.

ASML expects to ship approximately 65 EUV systems in 2026, representing an increase of more than 50% year over year. The company plans to expand low-NA EUV and immersion manufacturing capacity by 30% in 2027 and is evaluating additional expansion beyond its previously planned 30% increase for 2028.

Technology developments remain central to these efforts. The upcoming NXE:3800F system is expected to increase throughput to 260 wafers per hour from 230. Next-generation immersion systems are expected to deliver 330 wafers per hour, while the YieldStar 550B metrology platform offers more than 60% higher productivity, supporting advanced logic and memory manufacturing.

Zacks Rank

ASML currently has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

news.Title: 曾文生：科技業資金投入電力建設 台電碳捕捉計畫不缺席
news.Content:
電廠或電網投資金額巨大，近日討論讓民間科技業如台積電等出錢參與議題興起，台電也有相關規劃。台電董事長曾文生14日指出，近期已有報導台積電正跟民營電力公司研商碳捕捉與封存(CCS)，而台電身為國營事業，自然不會缺席。他透露目前已有廠商來接洽，可相關工作還要共同規劃跟決策。

曾文生直指台電這家電力公司長期走向，就是要「產業化」，未來要與產業共同決策，這已經開始在做了。做伺服器、封裝、記憶體、晶圓製造的產業，從園區的開發開始，到規劃用電，雙方都需要共同規劃出一個機制，這慢慢正在開始。

他說近日已經有媒體披露，台積電正跟民營電力公司共同研商碳捕捉與封存(CCS)相關工作，台電身為國營事業，雖然研議階段不能說，但這件事情不會缺席。

台電有11座火力電廠，先前就規劃在台中火力電廠設置「減碳技術示範園區」，於9號機設置碳捕捉（CCUS）裝置，預計明年底正式啟用，每年可捕捉2000公噸二氧化碳。

只是，與民間合作在電廠做CCS，哪些人要來做，產能規劃多少，後端要怎麼加裝輔助裝置，以及碳捕捉下來是要再利用還是封存？曾文生指需要與業界共同規劃跟決策。他透露已有需求者來找台電，但是還不能講(哪家企業)。

至於科技業為何願意出錢投資電力建設？曾文生回應，當年Apple是拿著錢來台灣包產能，現在很多半導體的製造者，也拿一些資金去支持一些獨角獸、不錯的供應商，讓他們去擴張產能。

雖然與科技業共同投資決策已經是方向，可是他強調，現在還不能說達成了一個什麼共識，雙方怎麼做，需要彼此有一些討論的時間空間。

news.Title: 台股暴漲暴跌是空頭？郭哲榮曝真相：台積電法說有驚喜
news.Content:
台股今（14）日行情如驚濤駭浪，加權指數早盤一度猛攻超過 700 點、逼近 49,000 點大關，終場大漲 284.52 點，收在 48,625.83 點，成交金額達 9,286.24 億元。前一日盤中暴跌近千點，今日又上演劇烈洗盤震盪，讓不少散戶驚慌失措，質疑台股暴漲暴跌是否為空頭訊號？ 摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮 特別指出，這絕非空頭來臨，而是主力洗盤甩轎的極限過程，大跌反而是上天給予樂觀者的絕佳禮物，並搶先預告台積電(2330)法說會的震撼財測，為市場注入強心針。

【暴漲暴跌是空頭訊號嗎？郭哲榮曝關鍵內幕】

面對台股近期的大幅波動，許多投資人焦慮難眠，郭哲榮分析指出，今日台股開高後尾盤漲幅收斂，主因是受到韓國股市重挫拖累，並非台股基本面轉壞。 這波暴漲暴跌實為主力清洗浮動籌碼的甩轎手段，絕非空頭架構。

他更首度透露關鍵內幕，表示自己在大盤重挫近千點時完全沒有恐慌拋售，反而選擇逆向操作、密集加碼優質個股。他感性地分享獨門投資哲學：「悲觀的人邏輯正確，樂觀的人賺大錢！」提醒投資人切勿在市場最絕望時跟風殺低，唯有保持理性與信心，才能在危機中把握財富重組的良機。

【揭密獨門投資心法 散戶翻身看兩大指引】

談到散戶長期無法獲利的痛點，郭哲榮直言，許多散戶同時持有十檔以上的股票，資金過於分散反而大幅增加風險， 正確做法是精簡持股、集中資金才能直球對決。

對於總經與權值股風向，他提出兩大關鍵指引：

1. 美CPI數據與降息預期： 市場預估美國CPI通膨數據達3.6%已被充分消化，10月聯準會不升息機率高達79%，一旦利空出盡，將直接帶動台股與AI族群迎來新一波行情。

2. 預測台積電法說會震撼彈： 在台積電(2330)法說會前夕，郭哲榮搶先預估其第四季營收將達 525 億至 530 億美元，季增高達 12% 以上，全年營收成長更將衝破 43% 至 45%，遠優於市場預期。

【逆風中的曙光！低基期與被動元件迎契機】

在洗盤後的黑夜裡，潛力標的已展露曙光。郭哲榮點出，被動元件族群如國巨(2327)（指出逢600元以下為買點）、華新科(2492)與日電貿(3090)等已展現築底回溫的強勁態勢；而精材(3374)、智原(3035)、華邦電(2344)與南亞科(2408)等低基期股票，更是具備爆發力的精選標的。

郭哲榮感性結語，投資是一場克服恐慌的心理戰，只要看清AI產業大趨勢、選對低基期優質個股，隨同年底前AI族群回溫的浪潮，定能在這波震撼洗盤過後迎來豐收。

news.Title: Google Is Turning Scientific AI Into a European Cloud Growth Strategy
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet Inc ( GOOGL , Financials ), the parent company of Google, is increasing its AI presence in Europe by directly delivering more of its research tools to academics.Google DeepMind and Google Cloud are providing 200 European researchers with access to cutting-edge AI models and $3 million in computing credits.The program contains tools like AlphaFold 3 for molecular research, AlphaGenome for genomics, WeatherNext for forecasting, AlphaEvolve for algorithm development and AlphaEarth Foundations for Earth observation.From Alphabet's perspective, $3 million is hardly a huge financial commitment. More intriguing is the strategic value.Giving researchers early access to Google's models and cloud infrastructure might cement such tools into scientific processes, creating a long-term demand for Google Cloud.It also provides Alphabet another option to show that its AI goal goes beyond consumer products like Gemini. The program is aimed to speed up scientific discovery and improve research competitiveness in Europe, Google says.The challenge for investors is whether projects like these eventually convert into greater cloud usage and better acceptance of Google's own AI capabilities.It will be interesting to see which European research teams join the program, and whether Google extends the effort beyond the first 200 participants.

news.Title: Microsoft Azure Reportedly Seeks 20% Cost Cuts Despite 40% Revenue Growth
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

The software and cloud-computing behemoth, Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT , Financials ) is suffering the same old dilemma in its fastest-growing business : Revenue is soaring but so are the expenditures to maintain that growth.Girish Bablani, president of Azure, has allegedly ordered top management to find methods to slash expenses by at least 20%.Microsoft rejected the characterization, stating Azure leadership had not instructed workers to establish formal cost-cutting strategies and that the business frequently prepared for many eventualities. The debate important, though.Azure produced $101.9 billion in revenue in the 12 months ending in June, a 40% increase from a year before. Revenue increased 43% in the June quarter, accounting for nearly 31% of Microsoft's overall revenue. The question is what does it cost to keep up that pace?Microsoft is also vying with businesses such as Meta and Anthropic for limited technical expertise, while AI infrastructure expenditure is rapidly expanding. They might save costs by hiring fewer outside contractors and by deploying AI to make their employees more productive.Azure employs over 60,000 people whereas Bablani's organization has about 11,500. For investors the question is no longer if Azure can grow. It's whether Microsoft can maintain that growth profitably as AI gets more capital heavy.Next, investors will want to see whether the announced efficiency drive leads to actual budget reduction, personnel changes or improved Azure margins.

news.Title: Grab These ETFs to Capitalize on the Physical AI Wave
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving at an extraordinary pace, moving beyond chatbots and content generation into something far more consequential: machines that can perceive, reason, and act autonomously in the physical world. Currently, physical AI represents the convergence of AI with robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones and smart manufacturing systems.

The growth prospects for this market reflect this momentum, with the global physical AI market projected to grow from $1.50 billion in 2026 to $15.24 billion by 2032, representing a 47.2% CAGR (as predicted by Markets & Markets).

For investors, this transformation is putting companies working on physical AI in the spotlight, and by extension, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) holding these stocks are emerging as compelling low-risk investment options to capture the trend.

Before examining these funds, it is important to understand the industry's key players and the extent to which physical AI is transforming the market. This broader perspective can help investors assess the growth opportunities and make informed investment decisions.

Key Players in the Transformation

Physical AI marks a fundamental shift from AI as a digital tool to AI as a system capable of driving real-world outcomes. As NVIDIA's CEO mentioned last year: "AI's next stage is called physical AI, where AI interacts with the physical world, and it means robotics."

Several companies are currently leading this charge, with NVIDIA NVDA at the center of the physical AI ecosystem. The company provides full-stack AI computing for physical AI and robotics through its GPUs, Jetson edge platforms, and Isaac robotics framework. NVDA has partnered with companies like Unitree to release open humanoid robot reference designs to accelerate academic and industry research.

Beyond humanoids, NVIDIA's Jetson and Hyperion platforms power autonomous tractors, mowers, delivery bots (like Serve Robotics), and L4 autonomous mobility solutions.

Tesla TSLA is another key player in this space, which applies physical AI primarily through autonomous vehicles and mobility services, in addition to humanoid robotics. The company's Cybercab is a purpose-built, driverless autonomous vehicle designed from the ground up without steering wheels or pedals, built specifically to run on Tesla's physical AI driving models.

On the other hand, ABB ABBNY applies physical AI — what it calls Autonomous Versatile Robotics (AVR) — to transform how industrial robots learn, adapt and operate in the real world. The company has partnered with NVIDIA to integrate Omniverse libraries into its RobotStudio software to create photorealistic, physics-accurate digital twins that close the "sim-to-real gap" in industrial robotics, with up to 99% accuracy, making physical AI deployable at scale.

Story Continues

Using AI-based learning models, including Vision-Language-Action models, the software enables robots to learn demonstrated tasks in simulation and validate their behavior across multiple virtual scenarios, reducing reliance on physical prototypes and on-site testing.

Regal Rexnord RRX, another key player in this space, is expanding into physical AI and smart automation by supplying precision motion control, industrial powertrain components, and collaborative robotics that bridge digital software with physical machinery. The company joined forces with ABB Robotics to simplify integration of its GoFa cobots into 7th Axis Cobot Transfer Units (CTUs) from Thomson, one of Regal Rexnord's leading linear motion brands.

Extent of the Transformation and the ETF Playbook

The transition to physical AI is not happening in isolation — it is an industry-wide overhaul spanning hardware components, software platforms and domain-specific robotics. According to a Markets and Markets projection, the industrial robotics segment within physical AI is projected to witness a staggering 56.7% CAGR through 2032, driven by widespread factory automation.

Because this physical AI transformation spans multiple industry players — from pure-play chipmakers like NVIDIA and EV/autonomy innovators like Tesla, to industrial automation leaders like ABB and motion control suppliers like Regal Rexnord — picking individual winners can be challenging in a rapidly evolving market.

Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) provide diversified exposure across this entire value chain, capturing both the high-growth software and hardware enablers alongside traditional industrial manufacturers. This thematic approach should help mitigate single-stock volatility while allowing investors to participate in the broader, long-term physical AI megatrend.

Physical AI ETFs to Grab

Considering the aforementioned discussion, investors interested to capitalize on the growing trends of physical AI and robotics may add the following ETFs to their portfolios:

WisdomTree Physical AI, Humanoids, and Drones Fund WDRN

This fund, with net assets worth $17.3 million, offers exposure to companies enabling and deploying Physical AI across robotics, drones, and automation, capturing the transition from digital intelligence to real-world machine action and industrial transformation. NVDA holds the first spot in this fund, with 5.84% weight, while TSLA holds the second position with 5.64% weight.

WDRN charges 45 basis points (bps) in fees.

KraneShares Global Humanoid Robotics and Physical AI Index ETF KOID

This fund, with net assets worth $345.1 million, offers exposure to companies engaged in humanoid and embodied intelligence-related business. RRX holds the first spot in this fund, with 2.25% weight.

KOID charges 69 bps in fees.

Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF BOTZ

This fund, with net assets worth $3.29 billion, offers exposure to companies positioned to benefit from the growing adoption and utilization of robotics and artificial intelligence. NVDA holds the fourth spot in this fund, with 8.07% weight, while ABBNY holds the fifth position with 7.96% weight.

BOTZ charges 68 bps in fees.

news.Title: 施羅德首檔主動式ETF 00419A於11/2開募 10元甜甜價搶搭台股AI浪潮
news.Content:
全球資產管理巨頭施羅德投信今（14）日宣布，正式將主動式ETF版圖延伸至台灣，推出深耕台灣近40年來的首檔主動式ETF「施羅德AI科技台股主動式ETF」 (00419A-TW) 。該基金預計於 11 月 2 日至 11 月 6 日進行募集，發行價格為新台幣 10 元，最低申購門檻僅需 1 萬元，並採季配息（預定 3/6/9/12 月）且導入收益平準金機制，滿足投資人追求資本利得與現金流的需求。

截至 2026 年 8 月底，施羅德在台管理資產規模已達新台幣 5,673 億元。施羅德投信董事長謝誠晃表示：「台灣不僅是全球科技產業重鎮，也是亞洲最活躍、發展最迅速的ETF市場之一。ETF架構兼具靈活性與高透明度，而主動式管理能讓我們適時因應市場變化、發掘潛在的新興贏家，建構高信心的投資組合。」

施羅德全球ETF主管 Tom Stephen 亦指出，台灣企業處於半導體創新與下一代科技發展的最前線，隨著AI應用加速滲透，產業鏈蘊含極大的投資潛力。本次結合施羅德全球橫跨 24 個地區、逾 650 位專業投資人的研究平台，將發揮深厚的台股選股實力。

針對投資人最關心的選股策略，施羅德台股團隊00419A基金經理人游信凱於記者會上直言，這一波AI浪潮與過去產業景氣循環不同，而是「產品規格升級帶來的選擇性成長週期」。隨著雲端服務商（CSP）資本支出持續激增，預估明年資本支出將突破 1.06 兆美元，AI 算力對於基礎建設的要求已不可同日而語。

游信凱進一步分析，當前單一晶片功耗大幅提升，一架AI伺服器機櫃的功耗動輒高達 125 千瓦（kW），「這相當於一棟大樓的用電量在持續運轉！」因此，龐大的發熱與耗電需求，將帶動電源供應、散熱模組（如液冷技術）、電力基礎建設與重電族群的強勁規格升級需求。

00419A 將從超過 300 檔AI相關企業中，精選出 30 檔以上的優質個股，三大核心佈局方向包含：

關鍵零組件與半導體：包含先進製程、先進封裝（CoWoS）、IC設計與高速傳輸。

基礎建設與電力散熱：涵蓋散熱模組、重電設備與不斷電系統等算力支援供應鏈。

新型AI應用與軟硬整合：延伸至邊緣AI、機器人開發及新軟體應用等未來十年的潛力領域。

面對市場關注主動式ETF如何擊敗大盤，施羅德團隊強調，台股科技產業並非所有公司都能吃到訂單，唯有能夠滿足科技大廠嚴格規格要求的企業才能脫穎而出。團隊每天透過嚴謹的基本面分析與評判，尋找具備產品升級能力與獲利上修潛力的個股。

游信凱指出：「我們追求的是長期績效表現與高信念的投資佈局，而非短線跟風。透過團隊合作與徹底的基本面功課，協助投資人不僅能喝到AI浪潮的『肉湯』，更能精準抓到最核心的獲利主軸。」

施羅德AI科技台股主動式ETF (00419A) 將於 11 月 2 日正式募集，風險報酬等級為 RR5，提供投資人以小額資金靈活卡位全球AI供應鏈核心的絕佳工具。

news.Title: Softcat H2 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Softcat (LON:SCT) reported fiscal 2026 growth ahead of its initial expectations, with gross profit rising 24.7% to £616.3 million and underlying operating profit increasing 19.4% to £215.1 million, as demand remained strong across its IT infrastructure portfolio.

Chief Executive Officer Graham Charlton described the results as "an exceptional set of annual results," citing broad-based growth, market-share gains and continued investment in the company's people, systems and capabilities. The company also highlighted its recently announced acquisition of GDT, which management said would expand its international offering and add infrastructure and networking capabilities.

Revenue Growth Supported by Hardware, Services and Software

→ 3 Stocks Chopped in Half: Why These Drops May Be Structural, Not a Dip

Gross invoiced income rose 30.5% to £4.7 billion during the year. Hardware gross invoiced income increased 41.6%, supported by data center and networking sales, including larger solutions projects and customer orders brought forward amid memory shortages. Services grew 30.1%, while software increased 25.3%, aided by cybersecurity, licensing and Microsoft cloud service provider activity.

Revenue increased 35.4%, with hardware accounting for a greater proportion because it is reported on a gross basis under IFRS 15. Gross profit margin as a percentage of gross invoiced income declined by 60 basis points, reflecting a shift toward lower-margin products, changes to Microsoft enterprise agreements and the lower-margin effect of large projects.

→ Q3 Earnings Could Blow Past Consensus—Be Ready for What Comes Next

Gross profit growth was strongest in the corporate business, where enterprise and small and medium-sized customers posted strong double-digit growth. Public-sector gross profit rose by high single digits. Data center infrastructure, networking, security and client devices were among the major technology contributors.

The company's customer base grew 3.4% to more than 10,500 recurring customers. Gross profit per customer rose 20.6% to £58,500. Among customers generating at least £1,000 in annual gross profit, the number of customers increased 7.1% and gross profit per customer rose 16.5% to £70,000.

→ Why Wall Street Expects Even More From SanDisk After Its 575% Rally

Charlton told analysts that growth from existing customers was driven primarily by Softcat displacing competing providers, rather than simply benefiting from larger customer IT budgets. He said the company's approach has been to establish an initial presence with customers before expanding its share of their infrastructure spending over time.

Story Continues

Investment Raised Costs, While Cash Generation Remained Strong

Underlying operating costs increased 27.7%, exceeding gross profit growth as Softcat reinvested in technical, specialist sales support and back-office roles, as well as internal systems, data, digital capabilities and offices. Average headcount rose 10.8%, including the Oakland acquisition.

Underlying operating profit margin, measured as a percentage of gross profit, declined to 34.9% from 36.4% a year earlier. Statutory operating profit rose 13.6% to £196.4 million after £18.7 million in non-underlying costs. These included £15.6 million in development costs related to new cloud-based sales and human-resources systems that could not be capitalized, plus costs related to the Oakland acquisition.

Chief Financial Officer Katy Mecklenburgh said non-underlying costs are expected to rise by roughly two to two-and-a-half times in fiscal 2027, as lower systems-development expenses are offset by GDT acquisition and integration costs.

Profit after tax increased 13.0% to £150.3 million, while underlying basic earnings per share rose 19.7% to 83.2 pence. Underlying cash conversion was 93.6%, near the upper end of Softcat's 85% to 95% target range. The company ended the year with £199.9 million of cash after returning £137.5 million to shareholders through dividends and a £45 million share buyback.

The board proposed a final dividend of 21.6 pence per share, bringing the full-year ordinary dividend to 31.5 pence, up 7.5% year over year.

GDT Acquisition Expands International Ambitions

Management said GDT will enhance Softcat's ability to support customers with international operations, particularly in the U.S. and wider Americas. Charlton said the acquisition gives Softcat customers access to GDT's fulfillment capabilities, while GDT gains access to Softcat's broader portfolio and international capabilities across the U.K., Ireland, Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Charlton said the company had already won new business from U.K. and Ireland customers as a direct result of the acquisition announcement. He added that the combination could make the enlarged business one of a limited number of providers capable of supporting large, complex customers globally.

To fund the transaction and broaden its liquidity options, Softcat extended its revolving credit facility to £450 million and arranged a £100 million term loan after year-end. Following completion of the deal, the company expects net debt leverage of about 1.3 times EBITDA, falling below one times by July 2028. Outside temporary financing needs for major strategic investments, Softcat is targeting net debt of 0.5 to one times EBITDA.

AI and Infrastructure Demand Shape Outlook

Charlton said artificial intelligence is supporting demand across Softcat's technology areas, as customers require more data infrastructure, networking, security, storage and related services. He said Softcat has limited exposure to hyperscaler hardware spending, deriving less than 2% of gross profit from the neocloud segment during the year, but sees substantial opportunity in corporate and public-sector investment in AI-capable infrastructure.

The company is also deploying AI internally through its data and systems investments. Its new HR platform has gone live, while a new sales system is being introduced in phases after an initial pilot. Management said the projects were being delivered on time and within budget.

For fiscal 2027, excluding GDT, Softcat expects high-single-digit underlying operating profit growth, slightly ahead of gross profit growth. Mecklenburgh said the outlook reflects a tougher comparison following unusually large projects in fiscal 2026 and some first-half order pull-forward related to memory supply constraints, rather than a weakening in the underlying business.

Management said Microsoft's latest partner-incentive changes were included in guidance and are expected to be a slight net positive, as the changes favor partners with capabilities to support technology adoption.

About Softcat (LON:SCT)

Softcat plc operates as a value-added IT reseller and IT infrastructure solutions provider in the United Kingdom. The company advices, procures, designs, implements, and manages technology, such as software licensing, workplace technology, networking, security, and cloud and datacenter for businesses and public sector organizations. It also offers public cloud, collaboration, connectivity, data centre and private cloud, devices, and financial solution services. In addition, the company provides IT asset management, lifecycle solutions, modern management, security, software licensing, supply chain operation, and virtual desktop and application.

news.Title: Silicon Motion Technology Corporation (SIMO) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
news.Content:
Silicon Motion (SIMO) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Over the past month, shares of this chip company have returned +3.1%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +2.1% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which Silicon Motion falls in, has gained 3.9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Silicon Motion is expected to post earnings of $3.30 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +230%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $11.16 points to a change of +214.4% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $16.34 indicates a change of +46.5% from what Silicon Motion is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

Revenue Growth Forecast

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. news.Title: 〈台幣〉台積電法說前夕市場觀望 匯市高低洗盤1.5角微升1.2分
news.Content:
觀望美國關鍵消費者物價指數(CPI)報告發布，加上台積電 (2330-TW) (TSM-US) 法說會前夕市場觀望氣氛濃厚，新台幣兌美元匯率今(14)日呈現震盪整理走勢。早盤隨台股開高帶動一度反彈，但隨後外資持續在台股提款並匯出，新台幣升幅逐步收斂，全天高低震盪波動，高低震盪達1.5角，持續在32元整數關卡上演攻防戰，最終以微升1.2分的32.073元兌 1 美元作收。

台北外匯市場新台幣兌美元匯率今日以32.060元開盤，微升2.5分；盤中在台股衝高與出口商拋匯帶動下，最高一度升至32.010元，隨後在外資匯出賣壓湧現下由升轉跌，最低下探至32.160元，高低震盪達1.5角；終場升幅大幅收斂，收在32.073元，微升1.2分，升幅約0.04%。台北外匯市場成交金額為22.24億美元，元太外匯市場成交金額為11.595億美元，兩市合計總成交量達33.835億美元，顯示匯市交投氣氛依然十分熱絡。

從國際匯市來看，美元指數自先前高檔溫和回落，目前在102點附近進行盤整。由於市場正密切關注即將公佈的美國通膨數據，以及美聯儲（Fed）未來降息路徑，國際主要貨幣包含歐元與日元呈現窄幅震盪。歐美主要股市高檔整理，亞洲股市今日則出現洗盤格局，整體國際資金流向仍受到總體經濟數據影響。

國內股市方面，台股今日高低波動劇烈，早盤在台積電及半導體族群衝高帶動下，一度大漲超過700點，一舉衝上49000點大關。然而，高檔獲利了結賣壓傾巢而出，尾盤漲幅明顯收斂，終場上漲284.52點，收在48625.83點，成交量放大至9286.24億元，大盤留長上影線。

籌碼面部分，台北外匯與股票市場連動密切，三大法人今日在台股合計賣超153.97億元。其中，外資持續站在賣方，單日賣超約159億元，已連續六個交易日呈現淨賣超，持續將資金匯出；自營商亦順勢調節；僅有投信獨自力挺台股，逆勢加碼買超161.11億元

news.Title: The S&P 500 Is Dangerously Concentrated in 5 Tech Giants. Are They Still Buys?
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) is no longer as balanced as it has been in the past, with the index's top five positions making up nearly 30% of its holdings. This is the most concentrated the S&P 500 has ever been, and these tech five stocks -- Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG), and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) -- will play a crucial role in the benchmark's performance, as well as in the performance of all the exchange-traded funds (ETFs), like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO), that track it.

Let's see if these five tech stocks look like buys.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia

Nvidia is the main arms dealer in the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure race, with its graphics processing units (GPUs) as the primary chips powering AI workloads. The company has a huge moat in AI model training, as most early AI code was written on its CUDA software platform for its chips. Meanwhile, over the years, it has evolved into a comprehensive AI infrastructure player that offers end-to-end solutions for specific AI tasks, including training, inference , and agentic AI.

Wherever AI infrastructure spending goes, Nvidia is sure to follow, given its market position. With spending predicted to continue to soar and the stock cheap, with under a 14.5 times forward P/E based on fiscal 2028 (ending January), Nvidia remains a buy.

Apple

Apple has one of the best business models on the planet, as its ecosystem locks in customers and keeps them there. While its hardware, like the iPhone and MacBook, is the draw, it generates a lot of high-margin service revenue from selling cloud storage, commissions on apps and subscriptions, getting a small cut on transactions through Apple Pay, and through its revenue-sharing deal with Alphabet to allow Google to be the default search engine on its devices.

At 35 times forward P/E, the stock is a bit pricey, which could limit upside, but investors are getting a great compounding company that should perform well over the long term.

Microsoft

Microsoft is a leading cloud computing and enterprise productivity software-as-a-service (SaaS) company that also owns 27% of ChatGPT maker OpenAI. Its Azure cloud unit has shown consistent, rapid growth of more than 30% each quarter over the past three years, while it has a huge computing backlog of $678 billion anchored by commitments from OpenAI.

Story Continues

At the same time, given how entrenched its software is in the enterprise space, it's also becoming an AI software winner. It's seeing strong adoption of its AI assistant, Copilot, with paid users nearly doubling sequentially last quarter to 30 million seats. With the company firing on all cylinders, the stock looks reasonably valued, trading at 27 times fiscal 2027 analyst estimates (ending in June 2027) and just above 22.5 times fiscal 2028 consensus estimates.

Alphabet

While best known for Google Search, Alphabet is the most complete AI name, having both its own top-tier AI model and chips. Its chips business is a real differentiator. It allows Alphabet to train and run inference for its AI models more cheaply than competitors do, while its cloud unit achieves a one-year payback on its AI chip and networking investments when it uses its own chips. On top of that, it has started letting partner Broadcom sell directly to Anthropic, which has opened up another high-margin revenue stream for it.

Trading at a forward P/E of 23 times 2027 analyst estimates, the stock looks attractively valued given its growth and position in the market. I'd buy the stock.

Amazon

Amazon is the market share leader in both cloud computing and e-commerce. Its cloud business is accelerating, and the company thinks this could eventually become a $1 trillion revenue business. It's investing aggressively and has a huge backlog, with backing from Anthropic and OpenAI. It also has an emerging chip business.

On the e-commerce side, the company has been seeing strong operating leverage stemming from its investments in robots, automation, and AI. The company does not get nearly the credit it deserves in this area, in my view, while it's also become one of the world's leading digital ad platforms.

At a forward P/E of 25 times based on 2027 estimates, Amazon is trading at a historically attractive valuation, making it a buy.

The S&P 500 and VOO

While the S&P 500 and ETFs like VOO are now highly concentrated, I still see attractive valuations and strong upside potential in four of the index's top five stocks. Apple is the lone exception; I see it as a little pricey, but it is still one of the world's great compounding businesses, and the stock will work over time.

As such, I wouldn't be too worried about the S&P 500's high concentration levels at this point and would continue to be a buyer of VOO, as well.

news.Title: Prediction: Alphabet Stock Is Going to Soar After Oct. 28
news.Content:
The S&P 500 hit a fresh record high last week, and it's trading at an elevated valuation as investors price in some very high forward expectations for artificial intelligence (AI) companies. As a result, strong corporate earnings are the key to keeping this bull market going, and most technology giants will report their latest quarterly results over the next month.

Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) is scheduled to release its operating results for the third quarter (ended Sept. 30) on Oct. 28. Its stock happens to be reasonably valued heading into the report, and here's why I predict it could soar in the weeks and months that follow.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Wall Street will be focusing on Google Search and Google Cloud

Alphabet is an incredibly diverse tech conglomerate , but Google Search and Google Cloud are currently its most important businesses. Search accounts for more than half of the company's total revenue, whereas Cloud is the fastest-growing segment.

There were some concerns that AI chatbots would disrupt traditional internet search engines like Google Search, but Alphabet introduced a series of AI features to transform the user experience. AI Overviews, for instance, use text and images to provide AI-generated responses to queries, which appear above the traditional search results. Then there is AI Mode, which opens a chatbot-style interface where users can expand on their original queries by asking additional questions.

During Alphabet's last quarterly conference call, CEO Sundar Pichai said AI Mode had surpassed 1 billion monthly users, and that these new features were driving an increase in Google Search usage overall. This means users are seeing more ads, which is why the platform generated a record $63.3 billion in revenue during the second quarter (ended June 30), up 17% year over year. Investors should look for a fresh update on how AI is improving the search business on Oct. 28.

Google Cloud is also coming off a record second quarter with revenues of $24.8 billion, which represented an accelerated growth rate of 84%. The platform provides its enterprise customers with access to computing capacity from state-of-the-art data centers, and a suite of ready-made foundation models, which are the primary ingredients for developing AI software. As of June 30, Google Cloud had a staggering $514 billion order backlog from customers who were waiting for Alphabet to build more AI infrastructure.

Story Continues

The backlog might be a good predictor of future revenue, so it's one of the main numbers Wall Street analysts will be looking at on Oct. 28. If it increased during the third quarter, it will be a sign that demand for AI computing capacity remains very strong.

Alphabet stock looks attractive heading into Oct. 28

Alphabet's second-quarter earnings soared by 294% year over year to $9.11 per share, mostly because of the Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) initial public offering (IPO) in June. Alphabet invested $900 million in SpaceX through a private placement in 2015, but accounting rules required the company to recognize the fair market value of its position after the IPO, which was over $90 billion as of June 30. Hence, there was a huge one-off increase to Alphabet's earnings, which had nothing to do with its operating performance.

With that out of the way, Wall Street's average estimate (provided by Yahoo! Finance) suggests Alphabet's earnings likely stabilized at around $3.02 per share in the third quarter, representing a more modest year-over-year growth rate of 5%.

It's disingenuous to value Alphabet based on its trailing-12-month earnings because of the inflated second-quarter result. But looking ahead, Wall Street thinks the company will generate earnings of $14.98 per share during 2027, placing its stock at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23.4. That represents a slight premium to the Nasdaq-100 index which has a forward P/E of 22.1, but I think it's justified given the incredible AI-related strength in Google Search and Google Cloud.

Alphabet stock has returned around 45% over the past 12 months, but I think the company's third-quarter report will lay the groundwork for the next leg of upside, as long as its operating results show further momentum in the search and cloud businesses.

news.Title: Intel vs. Marvell Technology: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
The semiconductor landscape is shifting as artificial intelligence demands new hardware. Deciding between a turnaround giant like Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and a networking specialist like Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) requires looking at their 2026 trajectories.

Intel is pivoting toward becoming a world-class foundry while maintaining its CPU dominance. Marvell focuses on the plumbing of the data center, providing the high-speed connectivity needed for modern AI clusters. Both companies compete for space in the global infrastructure market, but they offer distinct financial profiles for investors.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures x86 processors while scaling Intel Foundry to offer advanced packaging and design enablement to the broader industry. The company is leaning into its manufacturing strength through a deepened partnership with Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) for next-generation equipment. Intel continues to be a central player among semiconductor stocks as it expands its foundry business.

For the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, revenue was nearly $52.9 billion, essentially flat (down just 0.5%) compared to the prior year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $267 million. While still in the red, this result was a significant improvement over the previous fiscal year, when it recorded a massive net loss of about $18.8 billion.

Intel carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4, which compares its total debt to the value of shareholder equity. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, its current ratio of 2 indicates it has twice as many short-term assets as liabilities. Free cash flow was negative at nearly $4.9 billion, while stock-based compensation represented roughly 25.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology focuses on data infrastructure, providing networking and storage solutions that power modern cloud and carrier environments. The company has aggressively expanded its AI portfolio through the recent acquisitions of Celestial AI and Polariton Technologies. Like its peers, Marvell faces significant concentration, with its 10 largest customers representing roughly 82% of total revenue and two specific customers each accounting for more than 10% of sales.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $8.2 billion, a significant 42.1% increase over the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $2.7 billion, yielding a net margin of 32.6%. This margin reflects the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses are paid, showing a sharp recovery from the net loss reported in its previous annual report.

Story Continues

The balance sheet shows a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.3 as of January 2026. Its current ratio of 2 suggests a healthy cushion to cover short-term obligations. Free cash flow was roughly $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 33.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since this is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Intel faces significant pressure from customer concentration, with one distributor and one direct customer together accounting for half of its revenue. Rapid advancements in AI could disrupt its business model if the company fails to keep pace with competitors or if customers choose to design chips internally. Furthermore, Intel's reliance on third-party partners in Taiwan for certain manufacturing stages creates geographic risks related to political instability and global supply chain tensions.

Marvell's recent spree of acquisitions, including XConn Technologies, carries the risk of integration challenges and high financial burdens. The company faces intense competition from established giants like Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), who are all vying for the same data center sockets. Additionally, carrying $4.5 billion in debt may limit its operational flexibility if interest rates remain high or demand for networking chips slows.

Valuation comparison

Comparing these companies on price reveals a significant gap in how the market values their current sales and future earnings estimates.

Metric

Intel

Marvell Technology

Forward P/E

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Part of the reason Intel reported that gigantic loss in the previous fiscal year is because it's in the midst of a turnaround. It's pivoting toward providing chip manufacturing services for third parties. In other words, the chipmaker is having to shell out quite a lot of money in order to build fabrication plants. That spending will likely continue, as turning around a ship of Intel's size is neither a fast nor an easy endeavor. The U.S. government's investment in Intel also gives me pause.

Marvell concerns me less. It's not in the middle of overhauling its business. The company faces customer concentration, but not on the same level as Intel. Marvell's forward P/E is marginally less expensive. And perhaps most importantly, Marvell is growing, and Intel is not. The former's revenue surged more than 40% in its most recent fiscal year, and it flipped from reporting a loss to a healthy profit. Intel can claim neither.

There are too many uncertainties tied to Intel's business makeover. Marvell looks like the better bet here.

news.Title: Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy and Hold Through 2030
news.Content:
As artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscalers invest hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure, demand for advanced processors, custom silicon, networking equipment, and semiconductor manufacturing capacity is accelerating. The biggest winners will be the companies that control the technologies stitching the AI ecosystem together.

For investors looking toward 2030, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO), and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) stand out as three compelling semiconductor stocks to buy and hold.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia: The platform powering AI factories

Nvidia is no longer simply a graphics processing unit (GPU) company. Its ecosystem now encompasses GPUs, CPUs, CUDA software, high-speed networking, and sophisticated systems that connect clusters of processors inside AI factories.

The company's financial performance reflects its dominance. In fiscal 2024, Nvidia's data center revenue totaled $47.5 billion. Through the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the company's data center business is operating on a run rate toward $328 billion. This level of growth underscores Nvidia's leadership position as hyperscalers race to build AI infrastructure.

Nvidia's next chapter could be even more interesting. The company's Vera Rubin CPU architecture creates new opportunities beyond traditional GPU design, while its networking portfolio is expanding through products such as NVLink, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and InfiniBand.

Nvidia is smartly forging partnerships across the semiconductor supply chain to broaden its reach. The company has made investments in and is collaborating on products with Nokia , Marvell Technology , Coherent , and Lumentum . These moves demonstrate how the company is expanding into telecommunications, custom silicon connectivity, and optical networking.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's technology stack increasingly supports next-generation use cases across autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, and even space-based computing ambitions. These markets have the potential to create additional growth opportunities beyond traditional data centers.

Nvidia's greatest competitive advantage isn't manufacturing faster processors. It's controlling the hardware and software layers that competitors struggle to replicate at scale.

Story Continues

Broadcom: Dominating the custom silicon opportunity

While Nvidia dominates the merchant GPU market, Broadcom is helping AI developers design specialized processors around their own AI workloads. These chips are known as application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and can offer attractive performance and efficiency for particular use cases.

Broadcom works with Alphabet on Google Cloud's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), while its relationship with Meta Platforms supports the development of Meta Training and Inference Accelerators (MTIA). Moreover, the company is also working with OpenAI on its inference processor, called Jalapeño.

The financial opportunity behind custom silicon is substantial. Broadcom's leadership is guiding toward $58 billion in AI revenue for fiscal 2026, representing an 186% year-over-year increase. Given the company's secured supply and deployment visibility, AI revenue is expected to surge to $115 billion and $230 billion in fiscal 2027 and 2028, respectively. In other words, Broadcom's AI-driven growth is expected to double for three consecutive years.

Similar to Nvidia, Broadcom also benefits from the networking infrastructure required to connect systems within data centers. Its Ethernet switches, networking silicon, and connectivity technologies offer additional avenues to participate in the upside of AI infrastructure spending. As a result, Broadcom is positioned to benefit whether hyperscalers purchase Nvidia GPUs or embrace custom processors.

Taiwan Semi: The backbone of AI chip manufacturing

The common denominator connecting Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom, and many other semiconductor designers is that they depend on Taiwan Semiconductor to manufacture their most advanced processors. TSMC operates the world's largest semiconductor foundry, helping transform chip designs into physical products. Taiwan Semi controls an estimated 72.5% of the global foundry market, compared with Samsung 's 5.9%. That competitive advantage is difficult to overstate.

Whether a hyperscaler orders Nvidia GPUs, AMD accelerators, or custom silicon developed with Broadcom, Taiwan Semi frequently participates in the manufacturing process. The company also supplies advanced logic chips used alongside memory products from manufacturers such as Micron , enabling it to benefit from the ongoing memory supercycle. Unlike individual chip designers, Taiwan Semi doesn't need to predict which AI architecture ultimately dominates.

TSMC's financial results showcase its AI-driven momentum. During the third quarter, revenue reached approximately $46.7 billion, representing roughly 41% year-over-year growth in U.S. dollars. What's encouraging is that the company's catalysts extend beyond today's AI capex. Demand for advanced 2-nanometer manufacturing, sophisticated chip packaging, and increasingly complex AI processors should support years of expansion into the next decade as new applications move into production.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Meta Platform, Micron, SK Hynix, SanDisk and and ASML
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 14, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Meta Platform META, Micron MU, SK Hynix SKHY, SanDisk SNDK and ASML ASML

Bearing AI Headlines: An Artificial Wave of Panic

Misleading AI Headlines Drag Down Memory Names

Over the past few weeks, three bearish AI headlines have dragged down the industry and sparked fear, uncertainty, and doubt among investors. Although short-term price action has been negative and bears have been in control, the headlines are misleading or downright inaccurate. Below are the three headlines:

1. "OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Nears $50B, Below Earlier $70B Reports": Earlier this month, the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's recent revenue growth was $20 billion below what Wall Street had expected. However, the article's editor failed to account for how OpenAI calculates revenue. In reality, the $70 billion revenue figure was never revised down, it was a completely different number. The $70 billion annualized revenue reported in late September by Axios and Reuters included enterprise sales, which more than doubled since July. Conversely, the FT's $50 billion OpenAI revenue figure did not include the full value of sales through cloud partners. In other words, nothing has changed. The $70 billion gross revenue and $50 billion net revenue remained the same, signaling that OpenAI's business is still growing rapidly.

2. "Meta Muse Growth Plateaus": Recent headlines suggest that Meta Platform's agentic AI platform "Muse" is seeing sluggish growth. However, data show that Muse is growing faster than any AI platform since ChatGPT launched in late 2022.

3. "Why this Little Known Chinese Chipmaker Has Caused a Global Stock Rout": Earlier this week, memory-related stocks like Micron, SK Hynix and SanDisk fell amid reports that China-based ChangXin Memory Technologies has made progress on new architecture that will increase memory density on its AI chips. Memory stocks have soared over the past few years as demand has dramatically overwhelmed supply. While a higher memory supply is bearish for names like Micron, investors have overreacted for a few reasons.

First, CXMT has difficulty accessing chipmaking equipment from companies like ASML due to U.S. export controls. Second, the legacy memory makers still have a wide technological advantage over CXMT. In other words, companies are unlikely to dump SKHY or MU in favor of CXMT technology.

Bottom Line

Short-term headline noise has led to bearish price action among AI leaders. However, misinterpreted revenue metrics, overstated platform slowdowns, and exaggerated competitive threats have created an artificial wave of panic.

news.Content:

Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven demand and improving pricing give reason to be optimistic about Intel's Q3, especially as its Data Center and AI (DCAI) business continues to grow rapidly.
