Intel's Q3 Outlook: Demand and Pricing to Power Revenue and Earnings

Intel is positioned for solid third-quarter growth, supported by rising demand for computing infrastructure, improved pricing, and growing adoption of its data center products. Its broad product portfolio, spanning CPUs, GPUs, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and processors designed for emerging agentic AI workloads, provides multiple avenues to capitalize on expanding investment in AI and cloud infrastructure.

Intel reported $16.1 billion in Q2 revenue, while its AI-related businesses expanded more than 70% year over year. The momentum will likely continue in Q3 and beyond. Management expects third-quarter revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion. At the midpoint of $16.3 billion, the forecast implies 19% year-over-year growth, indicating strong demand and pricing.

The DCAI segment is likely to remain a key growth driver. The business generated $6.3 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 59% year-over-year and 24% sequentially, reflecting stronger demand from hyperscale cloud providers and enterprise customers. Intel's purpose-built silicon portfolio is also gaining traction, with revenue up about 20% sequentially and having nearly tripled year-over-year in Q2. These trends will likely continue in Q3.

A key factor supporting Intel's growth is strong CPU demand, as AI workloads shift from model training to inference, agentic AI, and multi-agent systems. The company expects industry server CPU shipments to grow, with momentum extending into 2028.

Story Continues

Beyond revenue growth, Intel's profitability is expected to improve in the third quarter. The company projects a gross margin of 42%, up from 40% in the year-ago quarter. Stronger revenue, improved manufacturing yields, and higher average selling prices driven by product mix and pricing initiatives are expected to support the expansion.

Intel forecasts adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.38 for the third quarter, up 65% year over year. The projected increase reflects stronger sales, improving gross margins, and cost discipline. Analysts expect Intel's earnings to more than double in Q3.

Overall, Intel's third-quarter outlook points to continued progress on its turnaround plan, with data center demand, AI-related growth, and pricing improvements serving as the key catalysts.

Conclusion: Intel's Q3 Could Push Stock Higher

Analysts are cautiously optimistic about Intel stock ahead of its third-quarter earnings release and maintain a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating. INTC's high valuation remains a key concern. Intel trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 102.9, significantly higher than those of peers such as AMD (AMD) and Nvidia (NVDA).

Despite this premium valuation, Intel's Q3 results could serve as a major catalyst for the stock. Strong demand for AI infrastructure, improved pricing, and accelerating growth in its DCAI business could support higher revenue and earnings. Management's guidance also points to continued operational improvements. Meanwhile, expectations for higher gross margins and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) reflect the potential benefits of a favorable product mix, greater manufacturing efficiency, and tighter cost control.

Another potential growth driver is rising demand for server CPUs as AI workloads increasingly shift toward inference and agentic AI. This trend could create a longer-term growth opportunity for Intel, helping the company capitalize on the expanding AI market.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Sandisk, Lumentum and Jabil
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 14, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Sandisk Corp. SNDK, Lumentum LITE and Jabil JBL.

3 Best AI Stocks to Buy on This Pullback

Rising risk-off sentiment is once again weighing on AI and semiconductor stocks, with some of the market's strongest performers selling off. Concerns over rapidly rising interest rates and uncertain central bank policy, compounded by geopolitical tensions and persistently strong energy prices have prompted investors to rotate into more defensive sectors.

We've seen this play out numerous times throughout the AI bull market. Periodic corrections shake out weaker hands, but the underlying growth trends continue to strengthen. And for investors willing to look beyond short-term volatility, these pullbacks have consistently presented attractive buying opportunities.

The key, in my view, is focusing on companies supplying the mission-critical infrastructure behind the AI buildout, particularly businesses benefiting from supply constraints, strong pricing power and accelerating earnings growth.

Three stocks that stand out today are Sandisk Corp. , Lumentum and Jabil . Each represents a different but essential piece of the AI infrastructure boom, spanning memory and storage, optical networking, and advanced electronics manufacturing.

More importantly, all three are benefiting from powerful fundamental tailwinds that appear likely to persist well beyond the current market correction.

Sandisk: AI's Insatiable Demand for Memory and Storage

Sandisk has emerged as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI-driven memory boom. Following its separation from Western Digital, the company has become a more direct way to invest in the rapidly expanding demand for NAND flash memory and data storage.

AI systems generate and process enormous volumes of data, and that information needs to be stored, retrieved and moved efficiently. As AI workloads expand, particularly inference applications, demand for high-performance storage continues to grow.

At the same time, memory manufacturers have struggled to keep up with demand, creating one of the most significant supply-demand imbalances the industry has experienced in years. The result has been extraordinary pricing power.

Sandisk's latest quarterly results illustrate just how powerful this trend has become. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue surged 372% year over year to nearly $9 billion, including a 51% sequential increase. Approximately two-thirds of that sequential growth came from higher pricing, with the remainder driven by increased shipment volumes.

Story Continues

Profitability has exploded alongside revenue. Gross margins reached 84.6%, compared with just 26.2% a year earlier, while non-GAAP earnings climbed to $39.25 per share. The company's data center business has been particularly impressive, with annual revenue surging 437% to more than $5.1 billion.

And according to consensus estimates, the momentum is expected to continue.

For fiscal 2027, analysts forecast revenue growth of 143% to $49.25 billion, followed by another 18.7% increase to $58.46 billion in fiscal 2028. Earnings estimates are even more impressive, with EPS expected to surge 201% this year to $213.31, before climbing another 18.5% to $252.80 next year.

These are extraordinary numbers, and even more remarkable considering the scale of the business.

Yet despite the enormous earnings growth, Sandisk currently trades at just 7x forward earnings and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) .

Of course, that seemingly cheap valuation needs to be considered in the context of the highly cyclical memory industry. When supply is constrained and pricing is exceptionally strong, earnings can surge, making stocks appear unusually inexpensive near the peak of a cycle.

That is the primary risk here. Today's extraordinarily high margins should not be assumed to persist indefinitely, and additional supply or a slowdown in demand could eventually reverse some of the pricing gains.

However, the AI infrastructure boom has introduced a significant new source of structural demand, potentially making this cycle more durable than those of the past. If memory pricing remains elevated longer than investors anticipate, Sandisk's valuation could prove genuinely attractive.

Following its extraordinary rally over the last year, SNDK shares have spent the past six months consolidating in a wide and volatile trading range. Given the size of that range, the most attractive tactical opportunities may come either on a pullback toward support near $1,200 or on a decisive breakout above resistance around $1,800.

The former would offer a more favorable entry near support, while the latter would signal renewed bullish momentum and potentially the start of another leg higher.

Lumentum: The Optical Networking Bottleneck

One of the most significant challenges facing the AI infrastructure buildout is no longer simply obtaining enough computing power. Increasingly, it is figuring out how to connect all that computing power efficiently.

This is creating an enormous opportunity for Lumentum, a leading developer of advanced optical and photonic technologies.

The company manufactures high-performance lasers, optical components and networking systems that allow enormous quantities of data to move through modern data centers.

As AI clusters become larger and more sophisticated, moving information between GPUs, servers and data centers has become an increasingly difficult engineering challenge. And while adding more computing power is essential, that hardware is only as useful as the networks connecting it.

Traditional electrical connections are increasingly challenged by the bandwidth, distance and power requirements of next-generation AI systems. Optical technologies offer substantially greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency, making them a critical part of the industry's ongoing expansion.

Demand has become so intense that Lumentum recently indicated that some of its AI-related optical components are effectively sold out through early 2029.

That is an extraordinary level of demand visibility, particularly for a hardware supplier, and suggests the industry's capacity constraints are unlikely to disappear overnight.

The financial implications are becoming increasingly apparent.

Lumentum's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue more than doubled year over year to approximately $1.01 billion, while non-GAAP earnings surged to $3.23 per share from $0.88 in the year-ago quarter. Operating margins have also expanded dramatically, reaching 36.6% from just 15% a year earlier.

And based on current analyst forecasts, the company is only getting started.

According to Zacks consensus estimates, fiscal 2027 revenue is projected to more than double, rising 107% to $6.25 billion. Analysts then expect another 60.5% increase in fiscal 2028, bringing annual sales above $10 billion.

Earnings growth should be even more explosive. EPS is expected to surge 146.8% to $21.40 this fiscal year, followed by another 64% increase to $35.08 next year.

These forecasts represent one of the more aggressive growth trajectories anywhere in the AI infrastructure industry.

That growth comes at a price, however. Lumentum currently trades at approximately 46.4x forward earnings , a considerable premium even among rapidly growing technology companies.

While the valuation is elevated, it is not necessarily unreasonable given the company's extraordinary earnings outlook and unusually strong demand visibility.

Beyond its existing products, Lumentum is positioned to benefit from emerging technologies including optical circuit switching, 1.6-terabit networking modules and co-packaged optics. These technologies should become increasingly important as hyperscalers build larger AI clusters while attempting to contain networking costs and power consumption.

The main risk is that expectations have become exceptionally high. Any disappointment in orders, capacity expansion or margins could trigger substantial volatility, particularly following the stock's enormous rally.

Nevertheless, with its products occupying an increasingly critical position in AI infrastructure and demand expected to substantially exceed available supply, Lumentum remains one of the most compelling growth stories in the sector.

After breaking out from a significant consolidation earlier this month, LITE shares have pulled back to retest the breakout level.

This is a critical area to watch. Ideally, the stock should find support here and resume its uptrend, confirming the breakout. A failure to hold this level, however, could open the door to further downside and potentially serve as an early warning sign for the broader AI infrastructure trade.

Jabil: My Favorite AI Stock on This Pullback

Of the three stocks discussed today, Jabil may offer the most compelling combination of growth, valuation and technical positioning.

Unlike Sandisk and Lumentum, which operate in highly specialized areas of memory and optical networking, Jabil provides advanced manufacturing, engineering and supply chain services to some of the world's largest technology companies.

Its capabilities span data center hardware, server infrastructure, networking equipment, power systems and other sophisticated electronics.

Building AI infrastructure at scale involves far more than purchasing GPUs. Companies need complex server assemblies, networking systems, power distribution equipment, cooling infrastructure and an enormous network of components and suppliers.

Jabil helps customers manage this complexity, allowing them to ramp production and deploy infrastructure more efficiently.

And as hyperscalers continue committing hundreds of billions of dollars to AI infrastructure, Jabil is capturing a rapidly growing share of that spending.

In fiscal 2026, revenue increased 21% to $36 billion, while core operating margins expanded by 40 basis points. The company also generated more than $1.5 billion in adjusted free cash flow.

More importantly, management expects the growth to accelerate considerably in fiscal 2027.

The company recently guided for approximately $44.5 billion in revenue this year, representing 24% growth, while core earnings are expected to rise 34% to $17.55 per share.

AI-related revenue alone is expected to surge 54% to approximately $22.1 billion, approaching half of total sales.

That is a remarkable transformation for a company that has historically operated in the relatively mature electronics manufacturing industry.

And the consensus outlook suggests the momentum should continue well beyond the current year.

Analysts expect fiscal 2027 revenue of $44.62 billion, followed by another 15.3% increase to $51.45 billion in fiscal 2028. Earnings are expected to grow 34.5% to $17.61 per share this year, then another 25% to $22.02 next year.

What's particularly attractive is that investors aren't being asked to pay an excessive premium for that growth.

Jabil currently trades at just 17.7x forward earnings and carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , highlighting the strength of its earnings outlook and estimate revision trends.

For a company expected to grow earnings more than 34% this year and another 25% next year, that valuation looks especially reasonable.

Jabil also offers some diversification beyond AI infrastructure, with exposure to healthcare, automotive, industrial and other end markets. While AI has become an increasingly important growth driver, the company is not entirely dependent on a single industry.

There are risks, of course. Electronics manufacturing is a relatively low-margin business, and even modest disruptions to customer spending or manufacturing efficiency can have an outsized impact on profitability.

However, the combination of accelerating revenue growth, improving margins and substantial free cash flow generation puts Jabil in a particularly attractive position.

Along with the broader AI trade, JBL shares began correcting over the summer. Since then, the stock has carved out a compelling bullish wedge pattern, with support near $285 and resistance around $320.

A decisive breakout in either direction would provide an important signal, with a move above resistance suggesting the uptrend is ready to resume, while a breakdown below support could open the door to further downside.

Of the three stocks highlighted today, I think Jabil has the cleanest technical setup. Combined with its Zacks Rank #1, impressive growth forecasts and comparatively modest valuation, it stands out as my favorite opportunity on the current pullback.

AI Infrastructure Still Offers Compelling Opportunities

The recent selling pressure across AI-related stocks is understandably frustrating, particularly after the enormous gains many of these companies have delivered.

But investors should distinguish between deteriorating business fundamentals and a correction driven by changing sentiment, crowded positioning or valuation concerns.

For now, the fundamental picture across the most critical areas of AI infrastructure remains exceptionally strong.

Importantly, these companies are not merely trading on distant expectations of AI adoption. Their revenue, earnings and forward guidance already reflect significant real-world demand.

That doesn't mean the stocks cannot fall further. Valuations remain elevated in parts of the sector, and a meaningful slowdown in hyperscaler capital expenditures would present a serious risk to the broader investment thesis.

But until there is convincing evidence of a sustained deterioration in AI infrastructure spending or earnings expectations, I continue to view these corrections as opportunities rather than a reason to abandon the theme.

For investors looking to take advantage of the current weakness, Sandisk, Lumentum and Jabil represent three compelling ways to gain exposure to some of the most important and supply-constrained segments of the AI infrastructure boom.

news.Title: Tesla to Post Q3 Earnings: Will Automotive Margins Play a Spoilsport?
news.Content:
Tesla TSLA is slated to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 21, after the closing bell. The company's automotive business remains a key focus as vehicle deliveries show mixed trends, with year-over-year declines despite a sequential increase. Tesla's ability to sustain vehicle demand, manage costs and improve profitability will be important factors.

TSLA missed earnings estimates in two of the trailing four quarters, with the average negative surprise being 3.7%.

Tesla, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Tesla, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tesla, Inc. Quote

Q2 2026 Highlights

Tesla's second-quarter production totaled 451,758 vehicles (442,936 Model 3/Y and 8,822 other models), up 10% year over year. The company delivered 480,126 vehicles worldwide, up 25% from 384,122 units in the year-ago quarter, setting a record for second-quarter deliveries. Model 3/Y deliveries rose 25% year over year to 467,762 units, while deliveries of other models increased 19% to 12,364 units.

Total automotive revenues of $20.5 billion rose 23% year over year. Automotive sales, excluding revenues from leasing and regulatory credits, totaled $20 billion, while automotive regulatory credit revenue declined to $146 million from $439 million in the year-ago quarter. Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits was 16.3% compared with 15% a year earlier and 19.2% in the preceding quarter.

TSLA to Face Margin Pressure in Q3

Tesla's third-quarter delivery report provides an early indication of automotive demand ahead of its earnings release. The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, up from 480,126 in the second quarter, but down 2.1% year over year. Model 3/Y deliveries reached 478,237 units, while deliveries of other models totaled 8,295. Production was 464,391 vehicles, below deliveries for the quarter.

Tesla cautioned that vehicle deliveries alone do not determine quarterly financial results, which also depend on average selling prices, cost of sales, foreign-exchange movements and other factors. In its second-quarter 2026 update, the company said it remains focused on maximizing factory capacity utilization and growing vehicle sales through a differentiated product portfolio. Tesla also plans to optimize existing production capacity before building new factories and production lines.

Competitive pressure in the electric vehicle market, production costs, changes in vehicle mix and average selling prices may affect revenue and margin growth. Our model predicts gross profit from automotive sales at $3.39 billion, down 0.6% from the year-ago quarter level.

Story Continues

The company's ability to sustain customer demand while protecting automotive margins will therefore remain an important factor in assessing the segment's performance.

Overall Earnings & Revenue Projections for Tesla

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter sales and earnings is pegged at $27.8 billion and 43 cents/share. The consensus mark for earnings per share has moved down by 3 cents over the past 30 days.

Our proven model does not conclusively predict an earnings beat for Tesla, as it does not have the right combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a favorable Zacks Rank. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

The company has an Earnings ESP of -11.35% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) at present.

Stocks With the Favorable Combination

Here are a few players from the auto space that, per our model, have the right ingredients to post an earnings beat this time.

Garrett Motion Inc. GTX is slated to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 22. The company has an Earnings ESP of +1.24% and a Zacks Rank #3 at present.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Garrett's to-be-reported quarter's earnings and revenues is pegged at 49 cents per share and $945.6 million. GTX surpassed earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 16.76%.

Rivian Automotive, Inc. RIVN is slated to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29. The company has an Earnings ESP of +7.38% and a Zacks Rank #3 at present.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Rivian's to-be-reported quarter's loss and revenues is pegged at 66 cents per share and $1.97 billion. RIVN surpassed earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 15.14%.

Lear Corporation LEA is slated to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 30. The company has an Earnings ESP of +3.26% and a Zacks Rank #3 at present.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lear's to-be-reported quarter's earnings and revenues is pegged at $3.28 per share and $5.8 billion. LEA surpassed earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 13.49%. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

news.Title: Amazon Just Spent $7 Billion to Break Nvidia’s Weak Spot Wide Open
news.Content:
If Amazon's (AMZN) chips unit were a standalone company selling to outside buyers, CEO Andy Jassy estimates it would bring in about $50 billion a year. He believes that would rank it among the three largest data center chip businesses in the world. That context helps explain why Amazon is reportedly willing to spend around $7 billion on Decart, an Israeli AI startup, according to The Wall Street Journal . No deal has been finalized yet.

Trainium's pitch is simple. It offers more AI performance for every dollar spent. Jassy says Trainium2 delivers about 30% more performance per dollar than comparable GPUs, and Trainium3 improves on that by another 30% to 40%. Customers have clearly noticed. Amazon has more than $225 billion in Trainium revenue commitments, and it's even discussing selling the chips directly to companies outside AWS. The hurdle is that most AI software was built for Nvidia (NVDA). Moving it to a different chip takes time and engineering work, which keeps many customers loyal. That's where I think Decart fits in. Its optimization software is designed to run AI models efficiently across different chips, which could lower that switching cost for Amazon's customers.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Marvell Stock

Dear Accenture Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for Oct. 14

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 13

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

The price does raise questions. Decart's valuation was about $4 billion in May, and in September, Anthropic decided against buying it at roughly $6 billion after doing its own review. Amazon is offering more than both. In my view, though, if Decart helps even a small share of Nvidia users try Trainium, the payoff could easily outweigh the cost.

About Amazon Stock

Amazon is a multinational technology company best known for its online shopping platform. It also operates several other businesses. The North America segment offers retail sales of consumer products, including from sellers, advertising, and subscriptions through online and physical stores. The Amazon Web Services segment provides cloud computing services such as data storage, databases, and computing power to businesses, startups, governments, and universities around the world. Founded in 1994, the company is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

Over the past year, AMZN has climbed almost 19%, slightly outperforming the S&P 500's ($SPX) gain of 17% during the same period. The stock has benefited from strong growth in Amazon Web Services, rising demand for AI infrastructure, and improving profitability across its retail and advertising business. Investors are also betting that the company's heavy AI investments will support future earnings growth. On a year-to-date basis, it gained almost 16%, outperforming the S&P 500's gain of 13%.

Story Continues

Amazon's valuation looks unusual at first glance. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 31.59x sits about 80% below its five-year average of 158.90x. That average is misleading, though. Amazon generated a loss in 2022, which pushed its historical multiple to extreme levels. The forward Price-to-sales ratio is a better guide. At 3.42x, it sits about 19% above its five-year average of 2.88x, indicating a modest premium. Year-over-year earnings comparisons are also unreliable right now. Large non-cash gains on Amazon's Anthropic stake have lifted 2026 profits, so analysts' estimates show EPS falling 18% in 2027. Amazon carries $251.64 billion in debt and lease obligations against $122.99 billion in cash, leaving it roughly $129 billion in net debt. Over the past year, though, the company generated $161 billion in operating cash flow, so a $7 billion deal looks easy to absorb. For investors, the bigger question is whether deals like Decart help Trainium keep up its rapid growth.

Amazon's Q3 Outlook Tests Whether Strong AI Demand Can Sustain Growth

Amazon reported its second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on July 30. It reported stronger-than-expected results, with revenue of $200.6 billion, ahead of Wall Street estimates of $196.16 billion. Earnings per share came in at $5.75, comfortably beating the Wall Street consensus of $1.81. The company's revenue rose 20% from a year earlier, and operating income climbed 43% to $27.5 billion. North America segment revenue was $116.2 billion, up 16% year-over-year, while International revenue was $42.2 billion, up 15% year-over-year, excluding foreign exchange. AWS revenue was $42.2 billion, up 36.7% year-over-year. The company's capital expenditures were $53.1 billion, mainly for AWS and generative AI.

Looking forward to the third quarter, Amazon expects net sales between $197 billion and $202 billion. Operating income is expected to be between $22.5 billion and $26.5 billion. AMZN also raised its full-year 2026 cash capital expenditures forecast to about $220 billion from $200 billion. The increase reflects higher memory costs and continued investment in AI and cloud infrastructure. Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak asked whether data center spending could slow in 2027 and whether Amazon might sell its Trainium AI chips to outside data centers. CEO Andy Jassy said much of Amazon's data center capacity for 2028 has already been reserved. He also said the company may sell Trainium chips to third-party data centers in the future.

What Do Analysts Expect for AMZN Stock?

Wall Street remains bullish on Amazon stock. Recently, Tigress Financial analyst Ivan Feinseth raised the firm's price target from $315 to $385 and kept a Buy rating. The analyst believes the company's AI investments are accelerating AWS and AI growth, increasing advertising revenue, and encouraging more frequent purchases. These investments are also helping the company expand its operating margins. Similarly, Needham analyst Laura Martin reiterated a Buy rating and assigned a price target of $300.

Based on 56 Wall Street analysts covering the stock, AMZN holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Out of those, 47 have a "Strong Buy" rating, six have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and three have a "Hold" rating. The median price target of $328 reflects an additional 25% upside from the current level. The high price target of $405 implies 54% upside from the current share price.

news.Title: Why Wall Street Is Cautious About Tesla, and Why I'm Not Worried
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) has plenty of ways to make Wall Street nervous. Competition is intensifying in the electric vehicle (EV) space , its automotive profit margins have come under pressure, and investors are now paying a premium for a company whose future increasingly depends on businesses that have yet to prove themselves commercially.

Those concerns are legitimate. But focusing exclusively on Tesla's EV sales means ignoring much of what could drive the company's growth over the next decade.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Why Wall Street is cautious

The EV segment Tesla operates in has become significantly more competitive. Chinese manufacturers, particularly BYD , have expanded aggressively, while traditional automakers keep introducing new electric models, though most still fall short of its models on range and price.

Tesla also faces a difficult balancing act. Cutting its vehicle prices can help stimulate demand, but it also reduces the profits earned on each car sold. And of course, the financial impacts of previous price cuts are already taking their toll. Tesla's automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, fell from 26.7% in 2022 to 16.3% in the second quarter of 2026. Meanwhile, the company's current valuation reflects expectations for substantial future growth.

Make no mistake, if you're buying Tesla stock today, you're not just paying for an automobile manufacturer. You're paying for anticipated successes in autonomous driving, robotics, and energy storage.

Why I'm looking beyond vehicle sales

Tesla's energy business is one of the clearest areas where it's growing outside of the EV segment. In Q2, its energy generation and storage revenue increased 13% year over year to $3.14 billion. And this followed a strong 2025, when the energy business generated $12.77 billion in total revenue, up 27% from 2024.

Tesla also has an advantage that many emerging robotics and autonomous vehicle companies lack: manufacturing experience. The company has spent years developing batteries, electric motors, power electronics, and software. Those capabilities could support its ambitions in autonomous transportation and humanoid robots.

To be sure, the Optimus robot remains an early-stage project, and there's no guarantee it'll become commercially successful. But the company has the engineering resources and manufacturing infrastructure to pursue the opportunity without starting from scratch.

Story Continues

Autonomous driving offers another potential source of growth. A commercially successful robotaxi business could eventually generate significant recurring revenues.

The longer-term picture

I wouldn't dismiss investors' concerns about Tesla's valuation, nor do I assume its robotics ambitions will succeed. But I also wouldn't value Tesla solely based on its quarterly vehicle deliveries.

Its energy storage operations already generate billions in annual revenue, while its autonomous driving and robotics plans provide avenues for expansion. In fact, while Tesla stock is currently trading in the neighborhood of $375, a recent Morningstar analysis valued it at $450 per share, with roughly 30% of that estimate tied to its robotaxi opportunity. That translates to more than $135 per share. Meanwhile, Piper Sandler valued Tesla's existing business lines at approximately $400 per share while maintaining a $500 price target, implying $100 per share in potential value for Optimus, AI inference, and other opportunities. These estimates are speculative, but they illustrate how much of Tesla's potential is based on businesses beyond electric vehicle sales.

So while Wall Street is understandably focused on the company's near-term profitability, I'm more interested in whether Tesla can turn its technology and manufacturing capabilities into several substantial businesses over the next decade. I believe it can, and that's why I'm willing to look beyond the current concerns.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

Jeff Siegel has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Tesla. The Motley Fool recommends BYD Company. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy .

news.Title: 績效前20%投資人買什麼基金？ 「鉅亨買基金」揭曉：近9成集中台股基金
news.Content:
投資市場波動不斷，績效表現相對突出的投資人，究竟都買哪些基金？「鉅亨買基金」今(14)日表示，觀察客戶近3年報酬表現，針對報酬率排名前20%的客群進行持倉分析，發現這群投資人的股票型基金占比高達96.6%，台股及台灣中小型股票基金合計占這群客戶總基金資產88.1%，約為其他客群的2.7倍，顯示台股基金為這群客戶配置的主力。

除了股票型基金比重明顯偏高，績效前20%客群在基金類型與投資方式上，也呈現出與其他客群不同的特色。鉅亨買基金統計數據顯示，這群投資人持有累積型基金的比重達96.4%，明顯高於其他客群的62.5%；境內基金占比也達95%，相較其他客群的48.1%高出不少，反映其基金配置更集中於國內市場，且累積型基金是主要選擇之一。

鉅亨買基金投資研究部主管羅瑤庭表示，從這次持倉分析可以觀察到，績效前段客群的配置相對集中，尤其對台股基金有較高比重。這項結果呈現的是近三年報酬表現排名前20%客群的持倉特徵，有助於了解不同投資人之間的配置差異，但不能據此認定集中投資台股就是績效較佳的原因，也不代表採取相同策略就能複製過去的報酬表現，進一步比較其他資產配置，績效前20%客群配置於多重資產與債券型基金的比重合計僅3.3%，遠低於其他客群的31.6%，兩者差異相當明顯。

但羅瑤庭指出，股票型基金比重較高，代表投資組合的表現更容易受到股市行情影響；當市場震盪或回檔時，集中配置也可能放大資產波動，因此選擇基金時仍應回到自身的投資目標、資金用途與投資期限，並衡量可承受的風險，而非只看過去績效排名。

累積型基金也是績效前20%客群的配置特色之一。羅瑤庭表示，累積型基金通常將收益留在基金內持續運作，對著眼長期資產累積的投資人而言，是可以評估的投資方式；但是否適合，仍須視個人資金需求與投資目標而定，若有定期現金流需求或對資產波動較為敏感，也應一併考量不同基金類型的特性，而非單純跟隨市場上的熱門選擇。

「鉅亨買基金」也提醒，績效前段客群的持倉可作為觀察市場投資行為的參考，但不宜直接複製為個人投資組合，投資人應先確認自身的投資目標、資金需求與風險承受能力，再規劃合適的資產配置，並定期檢視投資組合。過去績效不代表未來表現，基金投資具有風險，投資前應審慎評估。

news.Title: Google Signed a Deal for Existing Reactors. So Why Did Oklo and NuScale Jump on the Constellation Energy News? The Read-Through Investors Are Missing.
news.Content:
The technology sector's commitment to nuclear energy continues to strengthen. Just last week, Google's parent company Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) agreed to purchase nuclear-generated electricity from utility company Constellation Energy 's (NASDAQ: CEG) existing nuclear power plants for 15 years, in addition to making a 20-year agreement to purchase 890 megawatts' worth of power from nuclear power production facilities that Constellation will build in the future. Alphabet's long-term commitment will enable Constellation Energy to confidently invest $4.3 billion in new nuclear energy capacity, adding to its already-extensive nuclear power portfolio.

Constellation shares jumped on the news, of course. But so did shares of small modular reactor (SMR) developers Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) and NuScale (NYSE: SMR), despite having no involvement in Constellation's agreement with Google. What gives?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

A new way to create and consume nuclear energy

NuScale and Oklo may be positioned to enter the nuclear energy business. However, they're not like Constellation. Constellation Energy's typical nuclear power facility is built to serve hundreds of thousands of utility customers.

NuScale and Oklo, on the other hand, are working on small-scale reactors designed to power facilities such as refineries, smelters, and desalination plants, built where the electricity is consumed.

The two approaches to providing power are obviously very different -- different enough that investors seemingly shouldn't conflate the two. Yet, they did. Why?

Because there's a more philosophical message being delivered here. That's the general recognition that nuclear energy is a far more practical solution to the growing power shortage that renewables were expected to shore up by now. Alphabet's management may not be interested in small modular nuclear reactors ( yet ). Other companies could be, given the broader reacceptance of this once-waning energy source. Investors are simply connecting the dots, and reasonably so.

Small modular reactors will feature prominently in the future

SMRs will never account for the lion's share of the planet's nuclear power generation, to be clear. Their fiscal math just doesn't make sense at scale.

Nevertheless, when grid independence is necessary and desirable, and the need is modest, they do have their place. That's why there are now over 70 small modular reactors already planned, if not already being built, according to estimates from the World Nuclear Association, compared to none in true commercial operation.

Story Continues

Moreover, the International Atomic Energy Agency expects about one-fourth of the world's new nuclear energy production capacity established between now and 2060 to come from small modular reactors, aligning with the International Energy Agency's prediction that the SMR power output will grow from less than 1 gigawatt in 2030 to around 100 gigawatts by 2050.

Don't miss the forest for the trees

For what it's worth, Constellation Energy isn't ignoring the potential of small modular reactors. In July 2026, it made a strategic equity investment in privately held modular reactor developer Blue Energy. Constellation just has more pressing, larger-scale concerns to focus on right now.

Investors are more forward-thinking, recognizing that Alphabet's long-term interest in Constellation's supply of nuclear-generated electricity is a sign of a much broader philosophical movement with room for more than one winner.

news.Title: Sandisk Could Still Earn Triple Its 2026 Profits Even If Memory Prices Crash
news.Content:
On Oct. 5, Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh raised his Sandisk (SNDK) price target from $1,875 to $2,050, keeping an Outperform rating. He believes AI agents will create a fresh wave of storage demand. These agents keep working on tasks in the background, and everything they do creates data that has to be stored and accessed quickly. Rakesh expects AI workloads to make up 22% of NAND demand by 2030. He sees the strong reception to Meta Platforms' (META) Muse and OpenAI's Dots as proof that agents are already part of everyday work. It isn't the first time the firm has pushed back on memory fears.

The Contracts Most Investors Are Overlooking

Some investors are still wary of memory stocks, and I understand why. Memory has always moved in boom-and-bust cycles, and much of Sandisk's current run higher came from rising prices. As I covered earlier, China's push to expand its own memory production has only added to that worry. What I think many investors overlook is how differently Sandisk now sells its chips. Customers are signing multi-year deals with firm commitments and minimum prices. These deals add up to at least $93.9 billion in expected revenue, even at those minimum prices. Management even expects margins to stay attractive at those levels.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Marvell Stock

Dear Accenture Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for Oct. 14

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 13

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Bernstein, which reiterated its $3,000 target on Oct. 5, the highest on Wall Street, makes the same point. It estimated that even if prices crashed 72% from their peak, Sandisk could still earn $214 per share in fiscal 2030 thanks to its contracts. That's nearly triple what it earned in fiscal 2026. Without the contracts, the same crash would cut that figure to $81.

The data center segment now makes up 38% of the storage Sandisk ships, up from about 12% a year ago. Together with its contracts, I believe that gives Sandisk two ways to win. If prices soften, the contracts offer a cushion. If agentic AI lifts volumes as Mizuho expects, Sandisk can keep growing after its price increases slow down.

About Sandisk Stock

Sandisk develops, manufactures, and sells data storage devices and solutions using NAND flash technology. The company provides solid-state drives for desktop and notebook PCs, gaming consoles, and set-top boxes. It created the world's first flash-based 20MB solid-state drive for IBM's (IBM) ThinkPad laptop. Moreover, Sandisk is a well-known brand for small, portable USB drives used to transfer and store data. Founded in 1988, the company is headquartered in Milpitas, California.

Story Continues

Sandisk delivered exceptional gains over the past 12 months, with the stock climbing roughly 1,075%. By comparison, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) generated gains of around 96% during the same period. The rally was driven by surging AI-related demand for memory and storage solutions, improving NAND pricing, and investor optimism following SNDK's spin-off from Western Digital. The trend has continued this year as well, with SNDK shares up approximately 475%, outperforming the ETF's gain of 78% over the same period.

There's no multi-year average to compare Sandisk's valuation against, since it only became a standalone company in February 2025. On their own, though, the multiples look remarkably low for a stock that has run this far. The forward non-GAAP P/E is 7.75x, while the forward Price-to-sales ratio is 4.96x. That tells me the market still expects the memory boom to fade. Analysts expect EPS to jump 202% in fiscal 2027 and 24% in 2028, with a small dip in 2029 before recovering in 2030. The balance sheet is solid, though, as Sandisk is nearly debt-free, holding $4.76 billion in cash against just $201 million in debt.

Overall, if the contracts protect earnings as Bernstein expects, today's single-digit multiples look fairly cheap.

Higher Memory Prices and Shipment Growth Drive SanDisk's Outlook

Sandisk reported its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on August 5. Revenue for the fourth quarter was $8.97 billion, up 372% year-over-year. The non-GAAP EPS came in at $39.25, comfortably beating the Wall Street consensus of $34.59. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 84.6%, far above the 26.4% margin reported a year earlier, while non-GAAP operating margin rose to 79.2%. The company's growth was driven by its data center business, which generated $2.98 billion in quarterly revenue. Edge revenue also grew to $5.43 billion, up 48% sequentially.

Looking forward, for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Sandisk guided for revenue of $10.3 billion to $10.8 billion, non-GAAP gross margin of 83% to 85%, and non-GAAP EPS is expected to be between $44 and $46. For the full year, the company expects capital spending to rise from fiscal 2026, mainly to support BiCS8 and BiCS10 ramps, while capital spending as a share of revenue should stay near 6%. CFO Luis Visoso said the company estimates the NAND market to exceed $300 billion in revenue in calendar year 2026 and approach $500 billion in revenue in calendar year 2027. He added that demand from customers is growing faster than the company's supply.

What Do Analysts Expect for SNDK Stock?

Over the past two months, Wall Street has remained bullish on SNDK. Recently, Citi analyst Asiya Merchant reiterated a Buy rating and set a price target of $2,100. Similarly, Bernstein analyst Mark Newman also maintained a Buy rating on SNDK with a price target of $3,000.

Based on 25 Wall Street analysts covering the stock, SNDK holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. The mean price target of $2,161 reflects 37% upside from current levels. The stock's high price target of $3,000 is impressive, implying 90% upside from the current share price. This reflects analysts' confidence in the long-term prospects of the company.

news.Title: 台股收紅外資賣壓收斂　新台幣由貶翻升終止連4黑
news.Content:
（中央社記者潘姿羽台北14日電）台灣昨天經歷股匯雙殺，今天甩開陰霾，台股收紅，新台幣兌美元也上演戲劇性反轉，盤中一度重貶逾1.4角、跌破32.2元，午後跌幅逐步收斂，尾盤更是由貶翻升，收盤收32.073元，升1.2分，終止連4黑，台北及元太外匯市場總成交金額33.835億美元。

昨天受到中東戰火延燒、AI疑慮升溫、晶片股賣壓沉重等利空夾殺，台灣股匯市慘遭血洗。外資狂砍台股新台幣1653.42億元，創下外資單日賣超金額第3大，熱錢瘋狂匯出，導致新台幣貶勢難止，盤中狂殺逾3角，當日台北及元太外匯市場總成交金額爆出71.145億美元的史上最大量。

儘管市場對AI疑慮猶存，美股4大指數全收黑，台指期夜盤上揚，提振投資人信心。台股今天盤中震盪670點，一度收復49000點關卡，達到49059.12點，終場漲勢收斂，收在48625.83點，上漲284.52點。

外資依舊站在空方，今天續砍台股200.37億元，呈現連6賣，累計提款台股逾3300億元，但賣超金額已大幅收斂。

相較於台股回穩，新台幣兌美元今天早盤仍承受貶值壓力，一早以32.1元開出後，迅速貶至32.2元價位，盤中最低32.228元，不過午後外資反手匯入，加上出口商積極拋匯，跌幅迅速收斂，央行也於尾盤調節，匯價再度上演「神龍擺尾」，收在32.073元，終止連4黑。

外匯交易員指出，一早匯市延續昨天的貶值走勢，新台幣貶至32.2元價位，但主要反映外資先前賣超台股後的資金匯出需求，並非資金持續撤離，市場氛圍已逐漸回穩。尤其新台幣貶破32.2元後，出口商拋匯意願明顯升高，帶動市場供需趨於平衡；成交金額也從昨天的逾70億美元縮減至30多億美元，交易逐漸回歸常態。

外匯交易員指出，午後隨台股收紅，部分外資甚至反手匯入，與出口商站在同一陣線，貶幅因此逐步收斂，加上央行調節，終場得以小升作收。

新台幣匯率回穩，不過美國今晚將公布9月消費者物價指數（CPI），牽動市場對美國聯準會的升息預期，週四則有台積電法說登場。外匯交易員表示，投資人屏息以待本週兩件關鍵大事，尤其新台幣匯率升貶多由外資主宰，如果台積電法說釋出正面訊號，台股得以重整旗鼓、攻破5萬點，不只外資匯出壓力減輕，甚至可望回頭回補資金，支撐新台幣走勢。（編輯：楊蘭軒）1151014

news.Title: Apple's new hardware strategy capitalizes on trust — just in time for the AI era
news.Content: The Apple household just got a new lineup. On Tuesday, the company unveiled several new smart home devices , including the HomeView hub, the HomePod Mini 2, and Apple TV 4K. The company's new releases are a clear pivot in its corporate strategy. Not only is it trying its hand at smart home products once again after its HomePod failure, but Apple and its accelerating hardware releases show new CEO John Ternus's ambitious strategy as a company meeting the AI era head-on. Tim Cook was Mr. Services, growing that business massively. But Ternus is clearly saying, why not both? Finally, it seems, Apple has figured out a new way to take its "walled garden" design philosophy — a closed, safe ecosystem that favors trust, its signature design language, and vetted partners — and apply it to the home, putting its customers literally inside it. You can see how this is low-hanging fruit for the company. Securing your home and your physical safety is already a big business that involves iPhones and Apple Watches. Why not directly capitalize on it, further monetizing its seamlessness and trust? After all, its privacy record looks very different than , say, the Amazon Ring privacy record . One can only imagine Apple has thought of that, even if trumpeting the contrast would be too low a blow for the company's advertising style. It's clear also that Apple's smart home strategy echoes its approach to AI, which we argued recently positions its brand of trust front and center . At the heart of both experiences is your iPhone, the quarterback for your AI-enabled smart assistant, but also all your domestic gadgets: the new indoor and outdoor cameras, thermostats, temperature sensors, the video doorbell, and the door lock. The new lineup gives people more reasons to put Apple's hardware in their home and their routines. The other side of this is more subtle: For every app integration and product purchase, customers might find it harder to leave the pleasures of Apple's garden. There isn't any AI-first alternative to an iPhone just yet. But if one emerges, it'll have to pry Apple's consumers out of a deeper hole — which could buy time for Cupertino to come up with an answer. All this shows that while other tech companies are busy expounding on their LLMs, Apple is clearly in a totally different conversation. Superintelligence and everything else in the AI debate might as well be unfolding on another planet. The company's vision, in its marketing of new hardware and its design ethos, is selling relief from home-based chaos and is ready to harness whatever AI capabilities emerge to tame and smooth our lives. Story Continues Apple isn't strictly selling AI hardware, but rather touting its ecosystem, its walled garden. Won't you step inside? Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban . news.Title: As Big Tech Designs Its Own AI Chips, the Companies Behind the Scenes Win
news.Content:
For years, AI data centers have almost exclusively relied on GPUs for all AI processing and learning. But as tech companies have deployed more advanced models and AI agents become prolific, custom processors have become increasingly important. That's because custom processors can be fine-tuned to run specific AI models for agents faster and more efficiently than general GPU processors for some tasks.

And some of the biggest winners in this space are custom chip designers Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL), as well as the world's leading processor manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's why their position in the custom processor space matters, as Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG), Microsoft , Amazon , and other companies spend hundreds of billions on this expanding market.

In-house custom chips are rising in popularity

To understand why tech companies need customer processors, it's important to know that many of them rent out cloud computing processing and AI services to customers.

For example, Alphabet's Google Cloud business includes everything from cloud computing to its Gemini Enterprise subscriptions. Sales from this segment soared 82% in the second quarter to $24.8 billion, making it Alphabet's fastest-growing revenue segment.

To offer some of the best AI services to its cloud customers, Alphabet leans on its own custom-designed Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). Just a few months ago, the company signed a multiyear deal with Broadcom for custom processors through 2031.

The financial details of the agreement weren't released, but it's certainly helping to accelerate Broadcom's sales of custom processors. Management says revenue from AI semiconductors will reach $56 billion this year and soar to more than $100 billion next year.

Marvell is tapping into the custom chip space, too. The company is a custom chip designer for Amazon's Trainium and Microsoft's Maia AI processors. That's notable because Amazon and Microsoft are the two leading cloud computing platforms, and Microsoft's popular Azure just surpassed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time, thanks to rising AI compute demand.

Marvell also just secured a $2 billion investment from Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), which gives Nvidia's customers access to Marvell's custom processors. This shows just how intertwined the AI processor market is now, and how customer AI processors can work alongside traditional GPUs for AI compute.

Story Continues

While Nvidia benefits from including Marvell's custom chips in its network offerings, the rise of custom AI processors could eventually erode Nvidia's market share. The latest TrendForce data shows that custom processors will grow by an estimated 45% this year, while GPUs will rise by just 16%.

Still, traditional AI chip companies aren't going anywhere anytime soon. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) recently won a massive deal with Meta worth up to $60 billion, and has AI compute agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic. Demand for AMD's processors resulted in the company's sales rising 50% to $11.5 billion in the second quarter and non-GAAP (generally accepted accounting principles) earnings per share soaring 246% to $1.66.

One company benefits no matter how all of this goes

Some investors will no doubt wonder where Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) fits into this surge in demand for processors, especially considering its investments from the U.S. government and Nvidia. But while its share price has soared 188% over the past year, analysts estimate its sales will rise by just 15% next year.

Intel has secured major deals, including with Space Exploration Technologies and Tesla , to help manufacture chips for its Terrafab data center project. But Intel's overall success is still very much up in the air, considering its foundry business lost $2.1 billion in the second quarter -- and just $293 million of its sales came from outside customers.

Rival Taiwan Semiconductor, also called TSMC, is doing much better. TSMC manufactures about 73% of the world's processors, and an estimated 90% of the most advanced processors -- custom or otherwise.

This means that no matter how many GPUs Nvidia and AMD sell, or whether Broadcom's and Marvell's custom processors expand further into the AI processor market, TSMC will benefit. The company's second-quarter sales were up 36% to over $40 billion, and non-GAAP diluted earnings popped 77% to $4.31 per American depositary receipt (ADR).

For investors looking for a custom AI processor play, TSMC, Broadcom, and Marvell are the best bets. Of the three, Broadcom could have the most potential to benefit, as its sales and earnings are increasing faster than those of TSMC and Marvell.

What's more, Broadcom's stock has a forward price-to-earnings ratio of just 19, making it far cheaper than the broader tech sector and a relatively good bargain.

news.Title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Purchased Nearly $4.8 Billion of the Oracle of Omaha's Favorite Stock This Year -- and He Likely Just Spent Several Billion More
news.Content:
For the first time in more than half a century, Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB) entered the year in uncharted territory. Its longtime CEO, Warren Buffett , retired on Dec. 31, giving control of the company's day-to-day operations and its $356 billion portfolio to successor Greg Abel.

Abel wasted little time making his mark . During the first quarter, he sent 16 stocks packing and reduced Berkshire's stakes in six others. He also piled into Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG), which has become Berkshire's No. 3 holding.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

While some changes are apparent, such as tech stocks being on the menu in a way that never existed when Warren Buffett was running the show, several core principles remain the same. Abel shares Buffett's long-term ethos and his unwavering desire for value.

Image source: Getty Images.

This latter point has been on full display through the first six months of 2026, with Abel spending close to $4.8 billion buying the Oracle of Omaha's favorite stock -- and chances are he spent billions more in the third quarter.

Buffett and Abel have plowed approximately $82 billion into this trillion-dollar company

Quarterly filed Form 13Fs with regulators allow investors to track which stocks Wall Street's savviest money managers have been buying and selling. However, Warren Buffett's favorite stock won't show up in Berkshire's quarterly 13Fs.

Rather, investors will have to peruse the company's quarterly filing for info on the stock Buffett and Abel have been actively buying over the last eight years. On the page preceding the executive certifications, investors will find a detailed trading history from the latest quarter for the stock Buffett holds nearest and dearest to his heart... Berkshire Hathaway.

Before mid-July 2018, Buffett and his now-late right-hand man, Charlie Munger, could only repurchase their company's stock if it fell to or below 120% of book value (as of the most recent quarter). Given that Berkshire never dropped to this line in the sand, not a dime was spent on buybacks.

On July 17, 2018, Berkshire's board amended its buyback program to allow its investing superstars to get off the proverbial bench. As long as Berkshire had at least $30 billion in combined cash, cash equivalents, and U.S. Treasuries on its balance sheet, and the Oracle of Omaha viewed shares as intrinsically cheap, buybacks could continue without an end date or ceiling.

Story Continues

Buffett repurchased shares for 24 consecutive quarters after these covenants were amended. Meanwhile, his successor, Greg Abel, spent $234 million buying back Berkshire's stock in the first quarter and an additional $4.53 billion during the second quarter. Collectively, Abel and Buffett have deployed around $82 billion for buybacks since mid-July 2018.

Over the last eight years, capital has always been available for share repurchases. The only wildcard has been whether Berkshire Hathaway's stock was attractively valued.

BRK.A Price to Book Value data by YCharts.

For a 21-month period (June 2024-February 2026), Berkshire's stock spent most of its time at a 60% or greater premium to book value. Unsurprisingly, not one penny was spent on buybacks during this time frame.

However, a sub-50% premium to book value has historically been a green light for share repurchases. Given that Berkshire Hathaway spent almost the entirety of the third quarter oscillating between a 40% and 50% premium to book, the odds are good that Abel deployed billions on buybacks of Warren Buffett's favorite stock in the September-ended quarter.

news.Title: 台塑四寶集體強攻還能追嗎？施羅德：短線健康輪動
news.Content:
台塑四寶14日集體強攻，南亞盤中攻上350.5元漲停價創歷史新高，台塑、台化以88.9元、85.5元攻上漲停，台塑化早盤最高漲至129元，漲幅達8.4％，塑膠類股指數大漲9.6％，吸引市場資金轉進傳統產業股；施羅德投信台股投資團隊主管游秋華表示，塑化、面板類股近日轉強，這是屬於短線健康輪動，不同族群輪漲，對台股指數未來漲勢是正面的訊息。

台塑四寶股價漲勢凌厲，投資人關心「還能追嗎？」游秋華未正面回應，但她認為，台塑集團旗下部分子公司與 AI供應鏈相關，帶動集團整體獲利，股價有一定的支撐。

護國神山台積電今最高來到2535元，游秋華進一步指出，台積電漲多，其他便宜類股也應該要有輪動，短期輪動會讓指數更健康；不僅台股塑化類股上漲，游秋華表示，美國近來類股輪動也有同樣趨勢，近2個月上漲多是防禦型的類股。

施羅德正式將主動式ETF版圖拓展至台灣市場，14日宣布推出(00419A) 施羅德AI科技台股主動式ETF ，是施羅德繼澳洲、美國及歐洲既有的主動式ETF管理經驗之後的台灣首秀，台灣推出主動式E TF亦是施羅德在亞洲首檔，為投資人提供一檔聚焦於台灣上市AI及科技價值鏈企業的投資商品。

(00419A)主動施羅德AI台股聚焦投資受惠於AI發展趨勢的台灣企業，掌握台灣AI生態系長期成長機會。投資範圍涵蓋半導體、光通訊、零組件、基礎建設及重電等AI應用領域企業，完整布局AI產業鏈不同發展環節。

news.Title: 當近半數個股默默下跌20% 專家如何評估美股目前榮景？
news.Content:
在標普500指數持續強勁的背後，金融媒體《The Motley Fool》分析師Steven Porrello警告，當前股票市場表面看似堅不可摧，實則已在暗處響起罕見的歷史警訊。

他強調，這場延續4年的多頭行情過去未曾被關稅、戰爭或升息所打斷，但市場內部的脆弱性與極端的估值水準，正預示著未來可能面臨的動盪。

近半數成分股已陷入熊市

據《MarketWatch》報導，標普500指數已有高達 44% 的成分股，目前處於熊市領域，即股價較其 52 周高點下跌了至少 20%。

其中，約 24% 的股票自高點下跌至少 30%；8% 的股票跌幅高達 40% 以上；甚至有 3% 的成分股暴跌了 50%。

Porrello指出，這意味著整體指數強勁的績效表現，實際上掩蓋了近半數企業個股運營與股價的困境，市場漲勢僅由少數大型權值股所支撐帶動。

CAPE 比率突破40

除了個股分化的隱憂，市場估值過高更是Porrello的核心警訊。報導指出，「席勒周期調整本益比」(Shiller P/E ratio，又稱 CAPE 比率)已連續至少5個月發出異常訊號。CAPE 比率是用來評估股票相對於長期盈利是昂貴還是便宜的估值工具，在過去 155 年的歷史中，其平均值約為 18。

如今，標普500指數的 CAPE 比率已跨越 40 大關，這是美股歷史上第二次出現如此極端的估值水準。

Porrello特別提醒，上一次 CAPE 比率突破 40 是在 1999 年網路泡沫時期，隨後市場便迎來了極具破壞性的熊市。雖然 CAPE 比率並非直接預測股市崩盤的精準工具，但歷史經驗清楚表明：當股票估值達到異常高昂的水準時，通常無法長期維持。

歷史經驗與長期投資策略

儘管罕見警訊預示著潛在風險，Porrello仍為投資人提供了理性的應對思考。他引述嘉信理財(Charles Schwab)的歷史數據指出，自 1990 年以來，標普500指數至少經歷了 17 次回檔與熊市。雖然部分熊市(如網路泡沫)抹去了指數近一半的價值，但每一次熊市與修正最終都走向結束，這是股市投資的正常現象。

Porrello總結稱，試圖準確預測股市何時下跌或反彈是一場注定失敗的遊戲。面對 CAPE 比率所提示的熊市威脅，投資人最明智的策略是保持長期視角，選擇優質企業並跨越景氣循環長期持有，以安然度過市場的起伏波動。

news.Title: Palantir Billionaire Peter Thiel Buys 2 Brilliant AI Stocks (Hint: Not Nvidia or Micron)
news.Content:
Billionaire entrepreneur Peter Thiel is best known as one of the five co-founders of Palantir Technologies . But he also runs the investment company Thiel Macro, which has 42% of its portfolio invested in two artificial intelligence stocks, both purchased in the second quarter.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN): 28% of the portfolio.

Vistra Energy (NYSE:VST): 14% of the portfolio.

Thiel Macro beat the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) over the last six quarters despite holding zero stocks in two of those quarters. That makes Thiel a good source of inspiration for individual investors. Here's what you should know about Amazon and Vistra.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Amazon: 28% of Thiel Macro's portfolio

Thiel Macro's largest position is Amazon. While the company is officially classified as part of the consumer discretionary sector due to its large retail footprint, it is frequently listed alongside big technology companies due to its sizable cloud computing businesses. In both cases, Amazon stands to benefit from the artificial intelligence revolution.

In retail, Amazon has developed hundreds of generative AI applications that optimize things like inventory placement, demand forecasting, and last-mile delivery. Amazon is also the largest operator of industrial mobile robots, and it's using AI to make its fleet more efficient. For instance, next-generation Proteus robots can understand natural language, meaning human workers can give them instructions conversationally.

In cloud computing, Amazon Web Services (AWS) addresses AI demand at every layer of the stack, offering infrastructure, platform, and software services. It has designed custom AI accelerator chips that function as a less costly alternative to Nvidia GPUs. The company also offers development tools like Bedrock, and ready-to-use software like Kiro, an AI agent that automates coding.

In the second quarter, AWS revenue increased 37%, the fastest growth in more than four years. That is a clear sign that AI infrastructure investments are paying off, and investors have reason to believe the company will keep its momentum. CEO Andy Jassy told analysts, "We are unusually well-positioned for this AI inflection given our leading price-performance chips in both AI with Trainium and CPU with Graviton."

Story Continues

Amazon currently trades at 21 times earnings, a very reasonable valuation given that Wall Street estimates earnings will increase at 21% annually over the next three years. Indeed, most analysts think the stock is undervalued. Amazon has a median target price of $330 per share, implying 27% upside from its current share price of $259.

Vistra Energy: 14% of Thiel Macro's portfolio

Goldman Sachs estimates that U.S. data center power demand will reach 66 GW next year, more than double 31 GW last year. More broadly, analysts estimate U.S. electricity demand will compound at 3.5% annually through 2030, up from roughly 0% annually during the previous decade, driven in large part by heavy spending on AI infrastructure.

As the largest competitive power producer in the U.S., Vistra is well-positioned to benefit. The company generates electricity from a portfolio of nuclear, natural gas, coal, and renewable power plants, then sells it into wholesale markets through contracts with utilities and businesses. The company also sells electricity directly to residential and commercial customers via its retail business.

Vistra earlier this year announced a power purchase agreement with Meta Platforms covering 2.6 GW of nuclear generation capacity over two decades. Vistra also signed a similar power purchase agreement with Amazon. Those deals provide long-term revenue visibility, and the company could strike deals with other hyperscalers as the AI boom unfolds.

When valuing Vistra, investors should consider price-to-operating-cash-flow rather than price-to-earnings. The latter can be distorted by non-cash adjustments, such as unrealized gains and losses on derivatives used to hedge against volatility in natural gas and electricity prices. The former offers a clearer picture of the cash generated from the company's core business.

Vistra currently trades at 10.8 times operating cash flow, a discount to the 10-year average of 12. That looks particularly reasonable given that the company's operating cash flow is forecast to increase at 19% annually through 2030. Most Wall Street analysts agree. The median target price of $210 per share implies 29% upside from the current share price $162.

news.Title: 抽中1張爽賺12萬！特力屋、晶心科等3檔台股紅包申購倒數中
news.Content:

news.Title: 神山尾盤遭提款200億台股仍漲284點！南亞狂飆奪吸金王 國巨領被動元件搶鋒頭｜Yahoo財經掃描
news.Content:

台積電(2330)盤中最高漲至2535元，最後一盤撮合遭7999張賣單壓低，終場以2490元平盤作收，明日法說會展望仍是市場焦點。台塑四寶第三季財報帶動買氣，台塑(1301)、台化(1326)雙雙漲停，南亞(1303)大漲9.40%，且成交額居冠；台塑化(6505)則是小幅收紅；電子股由金像電(2368)勁揚7.69%、國巨*(2327)上漲4.67%吸引資金，被動元件、銅箔基板買盤回流，華新科(2492)、禾伸堂(3026)、聯茂(6213)、台燿(6274)同步走強。相較之下，部分權值股表現疲弱，聯發科(2454)下跌1.10%，大立光(3008)重挫5.43%，盤面呈現族群輪動、個股表現分歧。

亞洲市場未能延續早盤漲勢，日經指數小跌0.05%，韓國綜合指數下跌0.44%，香港恆生指數下跌0.15%，上海綜合指數下跌0.88%。

📝盤點熱門股：主動中信台灣收益、友達、國喬

今日熱門成交榜前五名全數收紅，主動中信台灣收益(00406A)以30.78萬張奪下成交王，在大盤反彈之際小幅走揚，交投熱絡。面板股友達(2409)強彈居次，為分析師點名的當沖熱門標的，短線交易人氣旺盛；塑化股國喬(1312)、台塑(1301)，分別勁揚、亮燈漲停，塑化景氣觸底回升與低基期補漲題材，帶動族群受到關注。玻纖布概念股台玻(1802)則是受惠AI需求帶動玻纖布商機，加上市場關注高階玻纖布、T-glass等題材，股價強勢上攻。

📌三大法人買賣超

三大法人今日合計賣超153.97億元，其中，外資賣超200.37億元，為法人賣壓主力；投信逆勢買超161.11億元，自營商則賣超114.71億元。整體來看，法人操作呈現分歧，投信持續加碼撐盤，但仍不敵外資與自營商的調節力道。

✨本日議題股：被動元件

被動元件漲價題材發酵，AI伺服器、高效能運算與消費電子備貨需求帶動買氣，日電貿(3090)透露部分客戶已預訂明年MLCC供貨量。今日大毅(2478)、日電貿(3090)、蜜望實(8043)、金山電(8042)、凱美(2375)同步亮燈漲停，華新科(2492)強彈8.67%，禾伸堂(3026)等...... 點我看更多

👥面板雙虎：

面板雙虎轉型題材發威，股價與人氣同步升溫！友達(2409)、群創(3481)受玻璃基板、Micro LED及面板級扇出型封裝（FOPLP）等題材帶動，成為市場關注焦點。Yahoo財經試算，若以去年10月低點買進、今年波段高點計算，同樣投入1萬元，友達最高可增值至約3.27萬元，群創更達約4.9萬元，兩者相差約1.63萬元。而股東人數也掀起「面板狂潮」...... 點我看更多

🔭重大財經事件展望

周四國際財經焦點，先看美國市場，將公布上周初領失業救濟人數、9月PPI與零售額，克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁哈瑪克也將發表演說；歐洲方面，歐元區將公布8月工業生產，英國則公布8月GDP；亞太區方面，日本將公布8月機械訂單與工業生產，日本央行理事小枝淳子也將發表演說，澳洲公布9月就業報告，韓國公布9月進出口；陸港澳方面，天貓「雙11」啟動預售，淘寶天貓海外亞太媒體交流會於香港登場、持續至16日，電商促銷與海外布局成為焦點。

台灣方面，主計總處將公布8月薪資統計，勞動部公布減班休息統計，行政院會也將召開，薪資成長、勞動市場與政策動向值得關注；上市金控9月及前三季獲利將全數揭曉，另有國銀8月中小企業放款、外幣存放款統計，以及金管會8月信用卡與電子支付資訊、國銀9月信用卡資訊。信義區周年慶開打，SHOPLINE也將舉行AI轉型新策略說明會；個股焦點以台積電(2330)法說會為主，市場將聚焦營運展望、AI需求與先進製程布局，毅嘉(2402)也將舉行法說會，華建(2530)、鼎炫-KY(8499)則召開股東會。此外，強盛新(1463)、長科*(6548)將除息，精華生醫(7806)將轉上櫃。

news.Title: 〈第四季台股展望〉資深股民信心爆棚！72.4% 樂觀看多台股、近九成押寶AI 與半導體
news.Content:
隨著第四季行情正式拉開序幕，台股投資人的心態備受市場關注。根據鉅亨與華南永昌證券最新出爐的「2026年第四季台股展望問卷調查」顯示，在 582 份有效樣本中，高達 72.4% 的受訪者對第四季台股整體抱持樂觀態度（其中 50.3% 偏多看待、22.1% 非常樂觀），僅有 3.8% 看空。整體投資信心平均分數高達 4.05 分（滿分 5 分），近八成（78.8%）的投資人給出 4 至 5 分的高分，顯示市場多頭氣氛濃厚。

核心動能：AI 與半導體需求續居主流

本次調查中最顯著的特徵在於市場共識高度集中。在支撐第四季上漲的主要因素中，高達 88.4% 的受訪者將票投給「AI 及半導體需求持續成長」，穩居各項因素之首；其次則是占比 63.4% 的「股市年底作帳行情」，以及「外資回流台股」（40.2%）與「上市櫃公司獲利改善」（38.2%）。

在產業與主題偏好上，AI 供應鏈同樣全面霸榜。最看好的前三大產業依序為半導體（76.2%）、AI 伺服器（62.5%）以及 PCB／載板（34.9%），後續如先進封裝、散熱、機器人及自動化等題材也獲得高度青睞。此外，多達 68.7% 的受訪者認為「AI 需求持續成長」是帶動第四季成長的最主要主題，反映出台股投資人對科技主軸的強烈信仰。

潛在隱憂：通膨再升溫與地緣政治成主要雜音

儘管多頭聲勢浩大，但居高思危的意識依然存在。在探討第四季最大的風險時，受訪者的憂慮主要集中在外部總體經濟與國際局勢：有 64.6% 的人擔心「通膨再度升溫」，61.3% 擔憂「地緣政治衝突」，其次則為「美國降息不如預期」（42.6%）。

值得注意的是，在科技股驚驚漲之際，有 40.9% 的受訪者坦言擔憂「美國科技股或 AI 類股估值過高」，另有 28.9% 擔心「融資餘額過高、籌碼凌亂」。這顯示出市場雖樂觀，但部分資金對於高檔震盪與評價面過熱仍存有一定戒心。

投資人結構與風險偏好：防禦型資產遭冷落

從受訪者輪廓來看，本次填答者以資深族群為主，50 歲以上占 57.2%，投資年資超過 10 年者更高達 57.7%，多數採自行選股（76.4%）或定期定額（50.3%）。交叉分析顯示，年資 1 至 3 年的較資淺投資人相對保守，信心指數（3.91 分）與 AI 押注比例較低；而年資較深的投資人則展現出較高的風險偏好。

有趣的是，在資金一面倒向科技成長股的同時，傳統的防禦型資產如高股息股、金融股及防禦型股票的支持度全面在 10% 以下，合計不到一成。這反映出第四季的盤勢結構中，市場主導權仍緊緊掌握在攻擊型的科技與 AI 族群手中。

整體而言，法人分析指出，第四季在基本面有 AI 長線需求撐腰、年底作帳行情即將啟動的雙重加持下，大盤具備向上攻堅的動能；然而面對高檔融資與評價過高的雜音，投資人在樂觀追價的同時，仍須密切關注總經數據與國際地緣政治的變化，靈活調配資產配置。

news.Title: 《韓股》AI支出疑慮拖累 KOSPI收跌0.44%
news.Content:

news.Title: 外資賣超200億！ 重砍台積電6752張 大買「這族群」網驚呆
news.Content:
台股今（14）日震盪走高，盤中一度大漲逾441點，但尾盤受到台積電賣壓影響，漲幅明顯收斂，終場指數上漲284點，收在48,625點，漲幅0.59%，成交量達9,286億元。三大法人合計賣超153.96億元，其中外資及陸資賣超200.37億元。

值得注意的是，台積電即將舉行法說會，今（14）日尾盤卻突然遭遇大筆賣單。最後5分鐘撮合時，台積電慘遭7,999張賣單摜壓，以收盤價2,490元估算，金額接近200億元，股價也瞬間從2,505元下挫15元，終場以平盤作收。外資今日同步賣超台積電6,752張，市場關注法說會前法人籌碼動向。

觀察外資買超個股，傳產股成為主要布局方向。中鋼（2002）以買超7萬7,005張居冠，台塑（1301）買超5萬3,390張排名第二，台玻（1802）也獲買超4萬6,522張，位居第三，顯示外資資金明顯流向原物料及傳產族群。其餘買超標的包括復華富時不動產（00712）買超2萬9,664張、華新（1605）買超2萬8,387張、台化（1326）買超2萬7,479張、中石化（1314）買超2萬2,491張，以及元大金（2885）買超2萬1,535張。

此外，陽明（2609）獲外資買超1萬6,326張，仁寶（2324）買超1萬6,300張。整體來看，外資買超前十名中，鋼鐵、塑化、玻璃及航運等傳產股占據多個席次，與市場聚焦AI及半導體族群的投資方向形成對比。

賣超方面，記憶體族群南亞科（2408）遭外資賣超2萬2,967張，排名第一；半導體測試廠京元電子（2449）遭賣超2萬2,655張，排名第二，顯示外資同步調節記憶體及半導體相關個股。台塑化（6505）遭外資賣超1萬9,974張，聯電（2303）賣超1萬6,001張，主動中信台灣收益（00406A）則遭賣超1萬2,770張。金融股方面，臺企銀（2834）遭賣超9,624張，台新新光金（2887）賣超8,324張，永豐金（2890）賣超7,598張。

另外，台亞（2340）遭外資賣超7,655張，元大台灣50（0050）賣超6,925張，台積電（2330）也遭賣超6,752張。台積電法說會前夕出現尾盤大單賣壓，加上外資持續調節部分半導體及記憶體個股，成為市場關注焦點。

外資買賣超名單曝光後，也引發PTT股市板網友討論。針對外資大舉買進中鋼、台塑、台玻等傳產股，有網友直呼「滿滿傳產」，也有人留言「錢進傳產」，認為資金流向值得觀察。

不過，外資調節南亞科與京元電，也讓不少股民感到無奈。有網友針對南亞科遭賣超表示疑惑，也有人對京元電連續出現在賣超名單表達不滿。另有網友注意到台塑化遭大幅賣超，認為傳產股內部也存在不同的籌碼方向。

news.Title: Is Apple Stock a Buy During the Holiday Quarter?
news.Content:
As we begin the holiday quarter, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) is in a time of transition. John Ternus took over as CEO from Tim Cook on Sept. 1, and he takes the helm at a time when the company benefits from an upgrade cycle but has not made the strides in artificial intelligence (AI) that many of its competitors have.

Given these struggles, should investors buy Apple as it benefits from holiday-related sales, or stand pat for now?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Apple is in its transition phase

Indeed, buying now means investors are taking a chance on the company just a few weeks into a new CEO's tenure. Although leadership runs such as Satya Nadella at Microsoft or Lip-Bu Tan at Intel have proven profitable for investors, CEO tenures often result in investor losses.

It is too early to tell how Ternus will do in the job. What we know is that he has taken a more hands-on role with Apple design. To make time for that involvement, he has delegated financial and supply chain responsibilities to other executives.

Considering Ternus's hardware engineering background, this move may make sense. While Cook was still CEO, Apple's AI is such that it chose Alphabet 's Google Gemini to become the core of Apple's next-generation Foundation model and enlisted it in helping to improve Siri.

Improved AI, no matter where it is from, and a recent upgrade cycle may be causes for optimism. After multiple quarters of sluggish growth, the $364 billion in net sales for the first three quarters of fiscal 2026 (ended June 27) increased by 16% compared to the same period in fiscal 2025.

Looking ahead, analysts believe Apple will finish the current fiscal year with 15% annual net sales growth, then slow to 11% in fiscal 2027. That includes an 8% growth forecast for the upcoming holiday quarter. That is still well above the 6% net sales increase in fiscal 2025, but the slowdown could be evidence that the upgrade cycle is starting to run its course.

Instead, the problem may come from valuation. As growth slows, Apple still has to contend with a 39 P/E ratio, and to some analysts, this is a red flag Apple investors can't afford to ignore . It also makes it difficult to choose Apple when its AI provider, Alphabet, trades at a forward P/E ratio of 29, a factor that, by itself, could make investors rethink positions in Apple stock.

Story Continues

Should investors buy Apple during the holiday quarter?

Given Apple's current state and stock price, investors should probably not add shares at this time.

Indeed, this is not a call for Apple's longtime investors to sell. Even if growth slows, it is unlikely to stop. It is also quite possible that Apple's products will improve as its new CEO becomes directly involved in the design process.

Nonetheless, net sales growth is on track to slow during the holiday season. This bodes poorly for the company when it trades at a relatively high P/E ratio.

Hence, without a substantial discount in the stock or meaningful signs of technical improvement, investors should probably not buy Apple at these levels.

news.Title: 《日股》半導體震盪承壓 日經收跌0.05%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-14 16:34:54 數位內容中心 發佈

日股今(14)日走弱，日經225指數收於67,744.29點，下跌33.23點或0.05%；東證股價指數(TOPIX)收於4,096.78點，下跌13.89點或0.34%。盤中雖有前一交易日大跌後的自律反彈買盤帶動，但午後半導體族群轉弱，使指數漲勢無法延續。

news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉中國9月出口額激增36.3% 市場不領情 三大指數走低
news.Content:
中國A股三大指數周三（14日）收盤走低，海關總署公布的數據顯示，9月出口總額為4,471.8億美元，較一年前增長36.3%，但市場並未領情。

上證指數周三收報3,767.23點，跌0.88%。深證成指收報12,110.59點，跌1.97%。創業板指收報2,866.76點，跌3.10%。

今年1～9月，中國出口總額為3.3707兆美元，較去年同期增長21.3%；進口總額為2.4325兆美元，增加27.5%，貿易順差為9,381.1億美元。

海關總署副署長王軍14日在國新辦記者會上表示，前三季外貿增速是近5年同期最快，季度和月度增速也總體呈現加快態勢。

王軍說，橫向看，最新國際數據顯示，這樣的貿易增速在主要經濟體中位居前列，中國繼續穩居全球貨物貿易第一大國地位。

王軍提到，前三季中國外貿有效應對外部衝擊，保持良好發展勢頭。儘管當前國際形勢變亂交織、各種風險挑戰層出不窮，但中國外貿發展的動力和活力增強、韌性彰顯。第四季進出口持續增長有基礎、有支撐。

news.Title: 外資賣超200.37億元　砍南亞科2.29萬張居首
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年10月14日電）台股今天上漲284.52點，收在48625.83點，成交值新台幣9286.24億元。外資賣超200.37億元，賣超南亞科 (2408) 2萬2967張最多，買超中鋼 (2002) 7.7萬張居首。

news.Title: 外資台股續賣，新台幣重貶後驚險翻升1.2分，以32.073元日高作收
news.Content:
【財訊快報／劉敏夫】台北外匯市場週三新台幣兌美元匯價大半場維持貶勢，午間一度下探32.228元、重貶1.43角或0.45%，尾盤獲買盤進場輸血翻升，以升值1.2分的日高價作收，新台幣繼週二爆量收挫後，週三走勢極具戲劇性。週二油價與全球債市殖利率走低，推動美元指數從三個月高點回落，加上台股反彈、日韓元升值，一定程度給予台幣支撐。新台幣兌美元匯率週三以32.073元作收，與前一交易日比較，台幣匯率升值1.2分。銀行間新台幣兌美元最高成交價為32.073元，最低成交價為32.228元，成交量仍達22億2,400萬美元。

外資週二大舉賣超台股1,653億元台幣後，市場關注外資後續的匯出力道。週三台股上揚，加權指數收漲0.59%，但是外資持續賣超上市股票200.3億元，累計近六個交易日賣超約3,300億元。

華僑銀行策略分析師Christopher Wong等人在報告中指稱，對台幣短期走勢略偏審慎，尤其是一旦外資持續流出台股且美債殖利率維持高檔。

news.Title: 鉅亨買基金：前20%投資高手 近九成資產重壓台股
news.Content:
投資市場波動不斷，績效表現相對突出的投資人，究竟都買哪些基金？「鉅亨買基金」觀察客戶近三年報酬表現，針對報酬率排名前20%的客群進行持倉分析，發現這群投資人的股票型基金占比高達96.6%，其中台灣股票及台灣中小型股票基金合計占這群客戶總基金資產88.1%，約為其他客群的2.7倍，顯示台股基金是這群客戶配置的主力。

除了股票型基金比重明顯偏高，績效前20%客群在基金類型與投資方式上，也呈現出與其他客群不同的特色。「鉅亨買基金」統計數據顯示，這群投資人持有累積型基金的比重達96.4%，明顯高於其他客群的62.5%；境內基金占比也達95.0%，相較其他客群的48.1%高出不少，反映其基金配置更集中於國內市場，且累積型基金是主要選擇之一。

「鉅亨買基金」投資研究部主管羅瑤庭表示，從這次持倉分析可以觀察到，績效前段客群的配置相對集中，尤其對台股基金有較高比重。這項結果呈現的是近三年報酬表現排名前20%客群的持倉特徵，有助於了解不同投資人之間的配置差異，但不能據此認定集中投資台股就是績效較佳的原因，也不代表採取相同策略就能複製過去的報酬表現。

進一步比較其他資產配置，績效前20%客群配置於多重資產與債券型基金的比重合計僅3.3%，遠低於其他客群的31.6%，兩者差異相當明顯。不過，羅瑤庭指出，股票型基金比重較高，代表投資組合的表現更容易受到股市行情影響；當市場震盪或回檔時，集中配置也可能放大資產波動。因此，選擇基金時仍應回到自身的投資目標、資金用途與投資期限，並衡量可承受的風險，而非只看過去績效排名。

累積型基金也是績效前20%客群的配置特色之一。羅瑤庭表示，累積型基金通常將收益留在基金內持續運作，對著眼長期資產累積的投資人而言，是可以評估的投資方式；但是否適合，仍須視個人資金需求與投資目標而定。若有定期現金流需求，或對資產波動較為敏感，也應一併考量不同基金類型的特性，而非單純跟隨市場上的熱門選擇。

「鉅亨買基金」提醒，績效前段客群的持倉可作為觀察市場投資行為的參考，但不宜直接複製為個人投資組合。投資人應先確認自身的投資目標、資金需求與風險承受能力，再規劃合適的資產配置，並定期檢視投資組合。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 知名空頭羅森柏格：美股泡沫與失衡 已達他40年職業生涯之最
news.Content:
總部位於多倫多的 Rosenberg Research & Associates Inc. 創辦人羅森柏格(David Rosenberg)表示，他40年的職業生涯中，從未見過美國股市在估值、槓桿率和投資者部位達到如此極端的水準，呈現出極高的泡沫風險與失衡現象。

羅森柏格強調，與網路泡沫時期相比，目前的牛市對人工智慧(AI)發展的依賴程度有過之而無不及。他認為美國是這波科技熱潮的震央，而投資人正付出過高代價，因此他在個人的資產配置中已轉向購買美國公債與海外股票。

除了市場對 AI 的過度依賴外，羅森柏格警告美國基礎經濟存在脆弱性，特別是消費者日益仰賴股市上漲來支撐日常生活消費。

他對下一波熊市可能引發的社會衝擊表達深切擔憂，並指出提早退休、靠投資組合過活的勞工未來恐面臨嚴峻抉擇，甚至面臨重返職場尋求收銀員工作卻已被機器人取代的困境。

羅森柏格向來以看空立場聞名，曾任美林證券北美首席經濟學家，因在 2008 年金融危機前成功預警美國房地產泡沫而聲名大噪，在 Gluskin Sheff 任職十餘年後，他離職創辦了自己的研究公司。

news.Title: 台股收漲284點！ 網見三法法人操作驚：內資軋外資
news.Content:

根據證交所公布資料，三大法人今日合計賣超153.96億元。其中，外資及陸資賣超200.37億元，自營商自行買賣賣超25.09億元，自營商避險賣超89.61億元；投信則大舉買超161.11億元，成為三大法人中唯一站在買方的法人。

觀察投信買超個股，台塑化（6505）以買超1萬4,106張居冠，遠東新（1402）買超1萬2,043張排名第二，華新（1605）買超6,556張、台泥（1101）買超5,637張，南亞（1303）買超4,541張、台塑（1301）買超4,315張，顯示投信資金明顯布局塑化與傳產族群。電子股方面，金像電（2368）獲投信買超3,725張；ETF則有元大高股息（0056）買超3,030張、元大台灣50（0050）買超1,350張。此外，大成鋼（2027）也獲買超1,354張。

在投信賣超方面，兆豐金（2886）以賣超6,743張居冠，聯電（2303）賣超5,909張排名第二，和碩（4938）賣超2,728張，緯穎（6669）賣超1,663張。金融股部分，玉山金（2884）遭賣超1,341張，台新新光金（2887）賣超1,212張；此外，華邦電（2344）賣超1,168張、文曄（3036）賣超879張、台灣高鐵（2633）賣超848張，強茂（2481）則賣超799張。

整體來看，投信今日買超集中在台塑化、遠東新等傳產股，賣超則涵蓋金融、半導體及電子通路族群，資金調整方向相當明顯。

三大法人買賣超數據公布後，也引發PTT股板熱烈討論。面對外資持續賣超、台股卻逆勢收漲的情況，不少網友好奇買盤究竟來自何方，留言直呼、「到底誰在買啦」，也有人笑稱「大哥回來了」、「投信我大哥」。有網友認為，投信大舉買超，對盤勢形成一定支撐，留言表示「大哥沒有輸」，甚至有人直言「內資軋外資的一天」，認為本土資金正在與外資形成對作。

不過，也有網友對後續走勢抱持保留態度，認為外資持續賣超仍是隱憂，提醒市場不能只看單日反彈就認定賣壓已經結束。另有網友質疑，指數上漲也可能讓外資有機會逢高調節，認為仍須觀察後續外資動向。

news.Title: 《台股盤後》量縮收漲284點 10日線及49K得而復失
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-14 15:46:56 新聞中心 發佈

台股今(14)日盤初呈現開高走高，在鴻海、國巨*、日月光投控走揚，加上塑膠、玻璃陶瓷、電器電纜等傳產族群強漲支撐下，加權指數盤中一度漲逾700點，重返4萬9000點關卡，不過因緯穎、聯發科、台光電與南亞科等走弱，且台積電尾盤拉回至平盤，壓抑漲勢，加權指數今終場收在48625.83點，上漲284.52點或0.59%，49K與10日線得而復失，成交量縮減至9286.24億元。

花旗(Citigroup)等美國大型銀行公布的財報好壞參半，再加上半導體設備、記憶體類股挫跌，拖累那斯達克指數、費城半導體指數13日走軟。亞洲股市方面，因日經225指數昨日重挫逾1,200點，吸引低接買盤湧入，AI、半導體相關股走揚，也帶動日經指數14日反彈，不過因獲利了結而翻黑，日經225指數終場下跌0.049%；韓國股市今日開高走低，KOSPI指數盤中一度大漲逾2%，隨賣壓出籠，KOSPI終場翻黑、下跌0.44%。

台股今日震盪走高，加權指數終場收在48625.83點，上漲284.52點。盤面資金明顯轉向傳產族群，推升大盤穩步墊高，市場買氣維持活絡，顯示投資人對後市仍偏向審慎樂觀。電子族群今日漲跌互見，台積電盤中最高來到2535元，不過尾盤拉回至平盤2490元；國巨*漲逾4%，創意、鴻海、健策、奇鋐、日月光投控、台達電等收紅，大立光跌逾5%，鴻勁、緯穎、南亞科都收黑，聯發科下跌1.1%。

觀察今日類股表現，塑膠類股最為強勢，漲幅達9.27%，成為盤面領漲焦點，台塑四寶今日漲勢強勁，其中台化、台塑都亮燈漲停，南亞也大漲9.4%。玻璃陶瓷類股上漲7.8%，走勢同樣亮眼，台玻勁揚逾8%。電器電纜類股漲幅3.66%，也擠進今日表現最佳前三名。而居家生活、光電及半導體族群今日表現則相對弱勢。從類股輪動來看，資金並非僅集中於電子權值股，而是擴散至多個傳產族群，帶動整體市場人氣回溫。整體而言，台股今日在傳產股帶動下收紅，後續仍須觀察資金輪動延續性，以及成交量能否維持高檔水準，作為大盤續強的重要依據。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人總計賣超153.96億元；其中，外資及陸資(不含外資自營商)賣超200.37億元，投信買超161.11億元，自營商賣超114.7億元。

news.Title: 【Follow法人】外資續賣超200億元！再提款台積電168億元 南亞科台塑化也中箭
news.Content:
（下午4點37分更新外資買賣超個股）

三大法人今（14）日合計賣超153.97億元，其中外資繼昨日創下史上第三大單日賣超紀錄後，今日再提款200.37億元。南亞科（2408）遭賣超逾2萬張居冠，台塑化（6505）也成為提款標的；台積電（2330）則遭調節6752張，以收盤價估算約168億元。分析師認為，外資今日偏向預防性避險，擔心稍晚公布的美國9月消費者物價指數（CPI）表現不佳，加上油價高檔可能推升升息壓力、台幣面臨貶值風險，因而先將資金抽回美國，不宜直接解讀為看壞台積電基本面或明日法說會。

外資賣超前三大：南亞科、京元電子、台塑化

外資賣超前十大中，電子股占4檔、金融股3檔、ETF2檔，傳產股1檔。南亞科遭賣超2萬2967張，登上賣超榜首；京元電子以2萬2655張居次，台塑化則遭調節1萬9974張，排名第三。

值得關注的是，電子權值股也淪外資提款機，聯電遭賣超1萬6001張，排名第四；台積電遭賣超6752張，排名第12，以今日收盤價2490元估算，提款約168.12億元。

聯發科遭賣超3512張，排名第17，以收盤價4475元估算，提款約157.16億元。

外資買超前三大：中鋼、台塑、台玻

外資買超前十大中，傳產股占7檔，金融股、電子股及ETF各1檔。中鋼獲買超7萬7005張居冠，台塑以5萬3390張排名第二，台玻則獲加碼4萬6522張，三檔合計吸引外資買超17萬6917張。

仁寶則以1萬6300張排名第十，成為榜上唯一電子股。

外資再提款200億元 連6日賣超台股3330億元

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日延續賣超態勢，合計賣超153.97億元，其中外資再砍200.37億元，呈連6賣，累計賣超3,330.8億元。

投信今日則是續站買方，買超161.11億元，連續4個交易日買超508.86億元。

自營商則合計賣超114.71億元，其中自行買賣賣超25.1億元，避險操作賣超89.61億元，已呈連5賣，累計賣超1,092.68億元。

分析師：非看壞明日台積電法說

運達投顧分析師陳石輝表示，外資今日調節力道已明顯降低，且「今天不是追殺台積電」。昨日台積電一早開低、股價向下，今日則早盤維持紅盤，直到尾盤才出現賣壓，兩天的交易型態不同。研判外資今日抽回資金，與短線籌碼流動、匯率及總體經濟風險的關聯較大，「跟看好、看不好台積電，其實關係沒有很大」。

陳石輝認為，外資可能擔心今晚即將公布的美國9月消費者物價指數（CPI）表現不佳，加上油價仍處高檔，恐使升息壓力再起，進而增加美元走強、台幣續貶的風險。尤其昨日台幣明顯貶值，反映資金匯出的壓力，因此外資先行調整部位，屬於預防性動作。

至於賣超是否代表不看好台積電明日法說會，陳石輝不太認同。他認為，外資可以透過持有台積電的ETF和在美國交易的存託憑證（ADR）調整相關部位或進行對沖。若台積電明日下午法說會釋出好消息，外資當晚便能在美國市場買進ADR，重新參與行情。

「寧可賣台灣的台積電，但是如果台積電真的很好，再買美國的ADR。」陳石輝表示，這樣的操作思路，是先降低台幣資產曝險，再視法說結果以美元布局。因此，今日賣超較偏向資金與風險管理，不應沿用昨日廣泛、大幅調節台股的方式解讀。

美股四大指數全面收黑，台股今日仍反彈，加權指數盤中一度收復4萬9000點、最高衝上49059.12點，尾盤漲幅收斂，終場收在48625.83點、上漲284.52點。
