news.Title: 台股反攻4萬9沒站穩 台積電收平盤.塑化續強
news.Content:
[ 非凡新聞 ]記者謝旻蓁,攝影蘇韋銘

台股周三止跌反彈，在台積電利多助攻下，指數一度大漲超過7百點，站回4萬9千點大關，中小型概念股也有買盤進駐，塑化族群多頭續攻，台塑、台化亮燈，南亞盤中也創新天價350.5元，其他像是矽光子、被動元件、面板等族群也輪番表態，不過尾盤台積電獲利了結賣壓出籠，股價跌回平盤價，大盤漲勢收斂，終場上漲284點，收在48625點，成交量達9286億元。

立委 羅民才：「覺得股市會觸及，會突破五萬點的請舉手，一個、兩個、三個、四個、五個。」

台股衝五萬內資信心滿滿，因為就在台積電法說會前夕，外資掀起目標價上修潮，最高喊到4410元，吸引資金提前卡位，股價領軍上漲，也為大盤注入一劑強心針，週三盤中上漲超過七百點，力拚站穩4萬9千點大關。

永誠國際投顧分析師 謝文琪：「在台股、亞股這部分其實都是有一個滿不錯的，一個跌深後的反彈，所以目前來看台股的話只要說，像成交量今天其實也是有預估到一兆以上的量。前波平台的最低點9月29日是47631點，只要沒有跌破47631點，那我認為這一波其實就是創新高的一個修正。如果台幣有稍微做一個轉升，那外資有沒有回來去停止轉賣變成轉買，那如果有的話，那其實我覺得對大盤的正向的加分效果會加大。」

盤面族群交投熱絡，台塑四寶股價續衝，南亞一度亮燈再刷新天價350.5元，台化也直奔漲停板，受惠於營收成長亮眼，矽光子概念股回神，華星光亮燈、聯亞漲半根停板，被動元件族群重拾多頭火種，面板三虎獲得買盤青睞，反觀先前漲勢暢旺的光學鏡頭概念股陷入拉回整理，記憶體則仍在消化長鑫存儲技術性突破消息，股價平盤震盪。不過專家認為，記憶體供給改善對AI發展是短空長多。

統一投顧總經理 廖婉婷：「如果這邊的供給瓶頸可以稍微克服的話，其實對於AI的整個零組件價格的壓力，我覺得是比較正面的。在明後年發展或者是備貨、拉貨會比較順的情況下，其實基建建造正向的話對於台灣的供應鏈都是好事。那這一次台積電法說市場也預期他會上修可能包括資本支出，然後第四季的展望也會因為輝達新平台的拉貨，還有GoogleTPU的拉貨，其實有機會開出一個雙位數的季成長。」

專家認為，隨著台股跌深反彈，加上台積電法說會即將登場，有望為市場注入多頭動能，不過短線要留意台幣匯率變化，以及外資買賣超動向掌握大盤後續走勢。（記者謝旻蓁／蘇韋銘 台北採訪報導）

news.Title: Alphabet vs. Meta Platforms: Here's What Revenue Trends Tell Investors About These Media Giants Turned Artificial Intelligence Companies
news.Content:
Alphabet: Steady Upward Revenue Growth

Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) primarily generates revenue by selling digital advertising space across its Google internet search engine and video properties.

Between July and October 2026, it introduced the newly developed Pixel 11 hardware series alongside updated operating system software integrations, and it navigated a proposed antitrust remedy framework formally filed by the United States Department of Justice regarding its core internet search operations.

Meta Platforms: Consistent Year-Over-Year Revenue Trends

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) primarily earns its revenue by displaying targeted advertisements to users across its interconnected social media applications.

Between July and October 2026, it debuted a new line of wearable hardware products including lightweight Meta VR Glasses for consumers, while the United Kingdom Office of Communications formally opened an official legal investigation into the specific child safety assessment protocols governing its various interactive mobile applications.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue provides investors with a metric showing the total money a business collects before management deducts any operating expenses. It serves as a fundamental baseline measure of overall consumer demand and business growth.

Foolish Take

Alphabet and Meta Platforms depend on advertising for the bulk of their revenue. That's why they both experience a spike in the fourth quarter, when advertisers raise their spending to capture customers during the holiday shopping season.

Story Continues

Now, both are battling to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom. Alphabet and Meta are heavily employing AI in their respective advertising platforms to help advertisers achieve strong performance. Doing so allows them to maintain their dominance in the digital advertising arena, where Google remains the top player and Meta is in second place.

That said, 2026 could be the pivotal year when Meta pulls ahead. The social media giant is growing ad sales at a faster clip than Google. As a result, Meta is projected to surpass Alphabet in advertising revenue for the first time this year, with global ad sales expected to reach $243.46 billion, exceeding Google's projected $239.54 billion. This would be a stunning transition, and validation that Meta's AI automation investments are producing superior results to its longtime ad rival.

news.Title: ASML Raises Full-Year Sales Outlook as AI Boom Drives Demand
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- ASML Holding NV upgraded the low end of its 2026 sales forecast, the third consecutive quarter it raised its outlook, as soaring artificial intelligence spending boosts demand for the Dutch company's chip-making machines.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Epic Games Delays Disney Project, Asks Developers to Use More AI

Apple Unveils $299 HomeView Hub as Part of New Smart Home Push

PepsiCo Cuts Estimates for Poppi Payout While Soda Sales Slump

Stocks Bounce From Lows on Williams' Rate Remarks: Markets Wrap

Billionaire Birla Says Investment Calls Becoming Tougher Now

The Veldhoven, Netherlands-based firm projected annual sales of between €44 billion ($49 billion) and €45 billion this year, it said in a statement Wednesday. The low end of the range was previously €43 billion.

ASML is the only company that makes the cutting-edge lithography machines used to produce semiconductors for the data centers powering the AI boom. Its outlook offers an indication of investment plans by chipmakers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics Co. and Intel Corp. as spending on AI infrastructure surges.

Industry players are increasingly questioning whether the AI boom is sustainable. There was a global selloff in semiconductor stocks this week after Broadcom Inc. Chief Executive Officer Hock Tan likened investor sentiment in the industry to a casino.

ASML's results can provide a window into chipmakers' plans because the company's advanced tools have a lead time of more than a year between order and delivery.

Net sales in the July to September quarter rose to €11.66 billion, ASML said. That compares with the average analyst estimate of €11.7 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Investors are also looking for indications that ASML can fulfill orders while the market is hot. In July, ASML said it plans to boost capacity by 30% next year for its second-most advanced tool, the low NA extreme ultraviolet lithography machine, which would take its annual shipment target to about 85 units.

ASML said it would not fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028.

Some customers "are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," Chief Executive Officer Christophe Fouquet said in the statement. "We are investigating ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase we previously communicated."

The company is working to ship tools faster to customers by reducing the cycle time, or the period between starting production in its clean rooms and shipping a completed machine. It began construction on its second industrial campus in the Netherlands, the first phase of which is set to be completed in 2029.

Story Continues

The AI spending spree propelled ASML to become Europe's most valuable company in 2026, with its shares up 64% so far this year.

Last quarter, top chipmakers announced plans to order ASML's most sophisticated chipmaking tool, which costs $400 million per unit. Samsung and TSMC said they would begin to mass produce chips with high NA EUV tools by 2028 and 2030, respectively. Intel Corp. said in September it had already processed more than a million wafers using the technology.

news.Title: Intel vs. Marvell Technology: What Revenue Trends Tell Investors About These Artificial Intelligence Companies
news.Content:
Intel: An Uptick After Flat Revenue

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) primarily earns its revenue by designing, developing, manufacturing, and selling a broad portfolio of client computing microprocessors, discrete graphics hardware, artificial intelligence server products, edge computing systems, and specialized advanced wafer fabrication services to original equipment manufacturers, cloud service providers, and telecommunications enterprises globally.

It recently priced an upsized $20 billion common stock offering, and it announced a broad technology collaboration with Applied Materials focused on next-generation transistors, interconnects, and advanced packaging hardware.

Marvell Technology: Consistent Quarter-Over-Quarter Revenue Expansion

Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) primarily earns its revenue by developing high-speed data infrastructure semiconductor architectures, mixed-signal networking switches, multiple core processors, ethernet controllers, optical transceivers, and custom application-specific integrated circuits designed specifically for enterprise data centers and broad global communications networks.

It recently expanded a multiyear strategic partnership with Google parent Alphabet that includes a performance-based stock warrant agreement, and it unveiled new rack-scale memory infrastructure components engineered to support complex artificial intelligence computing and enterprise storage workloads.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue helps individual investors understand the total amount of capital a given business generates from its primary commercial activities before subtracting operating expenses, debt interest obligations, and corporate taxes. This metric reveals whether a company is successfully attracting customers and growing its overall business volume over time.

Foolish Take

Comparing revenue trends between Intel and Marvell Technology shows the semiconductor veteran's sales overshadow the latter's by a wide margin today. That could change in the coming years thanks to the artificial intelligence boom.

During Marvell's investor day on Oct. 6, the company revealed it's seeing so much demand for its products related to AI data centers that it expects sales to grow from a total of $8.2 billion in its 2026 fiscal year, ended Jan. 31, to between $70 billion to $90 billion in its 2031 fiscal year.

While Marvell has seen consistent quarterly sales growth, Intel's revenue trend over the past eight quarters has been uneven. It struggled to capitalize on the AI market until new CEO Lip-Bu Tan took over in 2025.

This year, Tan's turnaround efforts appear to be taking hold, as Intel's quarterly sales trajectory looks like it is finally taking off. The company's fiscal Q2 revenue of $16.1 billion was a strong 25% year-over-year increase. If it can continue to experience excellent sales growth, it can maintain its revenue lead over Marvell.

news.Title: MIT dropout’s two startups announce shutdown weeks apart
news.Content:
The landscape of American entrepreneurship is dotted with college dropouts founding tech startups that went on to become the world's biggest companies.

For instance, Bill Gates dropped out of Harvard to co-found Microsoft . Mark Zuckerberg left Harvard after launching Facebook (now known as Meta).

Whereas Steve Jobs left Reed College to co-found Apple , and Jack Dorsey left New York University to co-found Twitter (now called X) and the Bitcoin-centric fintech Block .

All of these companies are among the world's most valued tech powerhouses, cementing the popular myth that most successful companies are built by college dropouts in the U.S.

However, not every such story ends on a successful note.

Related: Cathie Wood sells Meta shares after Zuckerberg's big AI launch

MIT dropout built crypto projects

Tieshun Roquerre, known by his online moniker "Pacman," is a Gen Z engineer who has balanced work with his studies since his teens.

He worked as an engineer at the e-commerce site Teespring and subsequently dropped out of high school. Next, he cofounded StrongIntro, a job-hunting site, and took it through the Y Combinator startup accelerator.

In 2016, he joined the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) to study mathematics and computer science. But he dropped out in 2018 to build products based on blockchain and crypto technologies.

The blockchain technology , which revolves around building a digital ledger of records agreed upon and stored across several computers, has gained immense popularity due to its rebellion against Big Tech's centralized control.

The most popular use case of the blockchain technology is cryptocurrency . It is a type of digital currency that is minted over a decentralized network of individual contributors (nodes). Unlike fiat currency, it is not issued by a government or a central bank.

Roquerre, drawn to these emerging technologies, started Namebase in 2018. It is a decentralized domain startup built on the Handshake (HNS) blockchain network. He raised $5 million for the project before selling it to Namecheap in 2021.

NFT marketplace Blur to shut down

In October 2022, Roquerre co-founded Blur, a marketplace to trade non-fungible tokens ( NFTs ).

It's a term many have heard of but few understand. In simple words, an NFT is a digital certificate of ownership recorded on a blockchain. An NFT can prove the ownership of a piece of original digital art, a tweet, or a meme.

The NFT market became extremely popular, and people paid millions for a few NFTs. In 2021, the most famous NFT by the American artist Beeple sold for $69.3 million . The same year, Jack Dorsey sold his first tweet as an NFT for over $2.9 million.

Story Continues

But after hitting the peak in 2021-22, the NFT market lost momentum in later years. Blur itself was once the largest marketplace to trade Ethereum NFTs.

But Blur announced on Oct. 12 that it's shutting down its website on Nov. 12. Its NFT lending service, Blend, will also halt new loans the same day next month.

Though the platform didn't specify any reason for the decision, the trading volume has fallen from the peak of $1.43 billion in March 2023 to less than $7 million in March 2026.

Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

Treasury Secretary Bessent drops a new bombshell on Iran

Ripple takes on Wall Street banks with a $35 billion client

Wall Street's youngest CEO of his day predicts $1M Bitcoin

Ethereum layer-2 Blast to shut down

After launching Blur in 2022, Roquerre launched an Ethereum layer-2 blockchain network called Blast in November 2023.

Blast gained popularity in the beginning and attracted a record total value locked (TVL) of $2.19 billion in May 2024, as per DeFiLlama . Its revenue hit a peak of $3.54 million in June 2024.

But the figures dropped quickly because speculative capital found another avenue. The math isn't mathing right now, and Blast's TVL and revenue stood at $24.81 million and $1,793 in September 2026.

Just because there is little trading activity, it doesn't mean a network doesn't have to spend money to keep it alive. For Blast, these costs were more than the revenue. This is why the network announced on Oct. 2 that it's shutting down.

Blast asked its users to withdraw their assets from Blast to the Ethereum mainnet by Oct. 26. Post that deadline, users will have to interact directly with the bridge contracts on Ethereum L1 to withdraw their assets, Blast said.

"We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26."

The recent months have proven to be disastrous for Roquerre as two crypto projects he founded have announced shutdowns within a fortnight.

news.Title: Here's Where Netflix and 3 Other Streaming and Media Stocks Could Be by 2030
news.Content:
The streaming sector remains as volatile as ever, and the push to consolidation has continued this year.

The merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount closed earlier this month, forming Skydance (NYSE: SKYD). This new Hollywood powerhouse will have to overcome roughly $80 billion in debt to deliver results for investors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Roku (NASDAQ: ROKU) agreed to be acquired by Fox Corporation in a move by Fox to expand its distribution and reach, as Alphabet's YouTube gains market share over traditional streamers.

Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) remains the industry leader, but a lot could change in the next few years. Let's take a look at where Netflix and its streaming peers could be by 2030.

1. Netflix

Netflix invented streaming and continues to lead the industry, though doubts about its future have grown this year.

The stock has tumbled as it's reported weak engagement and as it's lost market share to YouTube. Netflix no longer reports subscriber numbers, so we have less insight into the business than we once did.

The question for Netflix is whether it can maintain its current level of growth in the low-teens revenue range. If it can do that, the stock could be 50% higher or better by 2030. However, if the growth in the business continues to slow, Netflix stock is likely to underperform. While a decline in revenue seems unlikely, Netflix's original content has been underwhelming, and it will have to turn that around for its growth rate to stabilize.

2. Disney

Disney (NYSE: DIS) has been slow to find success with its streaming business after launching Disney+, but its streaming platform, which also includes Hulu and ESPN, is finally profitable and is delivering strong bottom-line growth.

Under new CEO Josh D'Amaro, the company is in the process of restructuring under his "One Disney" plan, which will enable viewers to easily use all three of its services in one app. Additionally, the company is embracing that strategy to do more to bundle its parks and experiences with streaming, using streaming to market the parks, and to better target its experiences to individual viewers' tastes.

The plan makes sense, but Disney has been slow to execute these strategies in the past, so investors may want to wait and see how the rollout goes. Disney stock has gone nowhere in the last decade, but it could finally make gains as streaming profits grow. After so much underperformance in recent years and with the entertainment business largely mature, I'm skeptical that the company can outperform the market between now and 2030.

Story Continues

3. Skydance

The newest kid on the block in streaming has the most to prove. Skydance combined two struggling legacy streaming platforms, Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount, into one, and absorbed roughly $80 billion in debt to do it.

It also settled a lawsuit with several state attorneys general. It made a number of compromises, including releasing at least 30 theatrical films per year over the next five years. That commitment, among others, could hamper its ability to turn profitable.

Given its debt and the restrictions from the settlement, Skydance faces an uphill battle through 2030. The stock will struggle to outperform the market.

4. Comcast

Finally, Comcast (NASDAQ: CMCSA) is the last major streaming stock on the list, following the wave of consolidation. However, the Peacock parent has less exposure to streaming than other companies on this list, as its primary business is broadband internet.

With its cable business declining and broadband mature, the company has struggled to grow. While Peacock offers a good mix of entertainment and has reached 48 million users in the U.S., it doesn't operate internationally and is unlikely to have a significant impact on Comcast's bottom line.

For dividend and value investors, Comcast may be attractive, but the business and the stock have been in decline for years, and that trend will be difficult to reverse.

What it means for investors

Legacy operators still face headwinds from the decline of the cable and box office businesses, giving Netflix an advantage over its peers.

Still, all of these companies are competing against big tech companies like Amazon , Alphabet, and Apple that see streaming as a way to pad their user ecosystems and make them stickier, and they have the means to operate at a loss if needed.

Therefore, all four of these stocks face challenges in addition to streaming reaching maturity in established markets like North America. Netflix still looks like the best bet, given its established global presence and scale, but its days of delivering market-crushing growth for investors may be over.

news.Title: How much MSFT stock does Microsoft founder Bill Gates actually own?
news.Content:
Everybody knows Bill Gates as the co-founder and longtime CEO of Microsoft. But Gates himself doesn't consider that to be his most important job .

Gates, along with Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, revolutionized the personal computing business in the 1970s and 80s. In the 1990s, Microsoft helped bring the Internet mainstream through its Windows operating system and Internet Explorer web browser.

These innovations brought the company enormous success—and tremendous personal wealth. In 1987, at the age of 31, Gates became the world's youngest self-made billionaire.

But just eight years after Microsoft's March 13, 1986 IPO, Gates' mind had already turned to philanthropy.

He set out to apply the same data-driven methods fueling Microsoft's explosive growth to help address global health inequities , founding the William H. Gates Foundation in 1994. In 2000, he joined forces with his then-wife, Melinda French Gates, to establish the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Both organizations were funded in large part by Gates' Microsoft stock holdings.

In 2010, Gates co-founded The Giving Pledge alongside French Gates and his good friend, Warren Buffett, encouraging the world's wealthiest individuals to donate at least half of their wealth to philanthropic causes during their lifetimes or upon their deaths.

"People will say a lot of things about me when I die, but I am determined that 'he died rich' will not be one of them," Gates has said . "There are too many urgent problems to solve for me to hold onto resources that could be used to help people."

So after a few decades of giving away his Microsoft fortune, just how much MSFT stock does Bill Gates own today?

How much of Microsoft does Bill Gates own in 2026?

While the Gates Foundation Trust sold its remaining 7.7 million Microsoft shares during the first quarter of 2026, Gates himself still owns a substantial stake in the company he led for 25 years.

According to Barron's , as of May 2026, Gates personally held approximately 103 million MSFT shares, valued at around $43 billion at the time.

Since then, Microsoft shares have climbed significantly. Based on MSFT's October 13 closing price of around $543, Gates' reported stake would now be worth approximately $55.9 billion, assuming he did not make any changes to his holdings.

Related: How much DELL stock does founder & CEO Michael Dell actually own?

Is Bill Gates the largest individual shareholder of Microsoft?

Actually, he's not. That distinction belongs to former CEO Steve Ballmer, who succeeded Gates in 2000 and is estimated by Bloomberg to still own 319 million shares, or approximately 4% of the company.

Story Continues

But since Gates and Ballmer stepped down from the company's board in 2020 and 2014, respectively, neither appears in Microsoft's latest Proxy statement .

Microsoft's current CEO, Satya Nadella, holds 900,572 shares, according to the Proxy statement, which would be worth $489.4 million as of MSFT's October 13 close.

That means that even in light of Gates' reduced ownership levels, he still holds over 100 times more shares than Nadella.

Related: How much Nvidia stock does CEO Jensen Huang actually own?

What was the peak number of MSFT shares that Bill Gates owned?

According to Forbes , if Gates and French Gates had "never discovered philanthropy," their combined net worths would be $1.5 trillion. Even after the couple's divorce, the publication continued, Gates himself would still be worth $1.2 trillion.

The reason? Right before Microsoft's 1986 IPO, Gates owned 11.2 million shares of Microsoft—a 49% stake in the company. Forbes calculated that if Gates had held onto those original shares, accounting for subsequent stock splits, Gates and French Gates would have owned 3.2 billion shares worth $1.4 trillion , with another $100 billion in after-tax dividends.

However, being one of the richest people on the planet was about the last thing Bill Gates wanted to do.

In a May 2025 Gates Notes blog post , Gates announced plans to accelerate his philanthropy, with the Gates Foundation expecting to give away more than $200 billion over the next 20 years before ending its operations on December 31, 2045.

This marked a change to the Foundation's original plan to sunset operations "several decades" after Gates and French Gates' deaths.

More on founders' wealth:

Warren Buffett's net worth: A look at his fortune in retirement

Mark Zuckerberg's net worth: How the Facebook founder hit $200 billion

"I now believe we can achieve the foundation's goals on a shorter timeline, especially if we double down on key investments and provide more certainty to our partners," Gates wrote.

"My net worth will drop 99% over the next 20 years," Gates added.

MSFT's biggest institutional shareholders

But even Microsoft's legendary founder doesn't own as many shares as its largest institutional investors.

According to Microsoft's Proxy statement , The Vanguard Group is Microsoft's largest institutional shareholder. It holds 664,882,153 shares, or approximately 8.95% of the company, worth approximately $359.8 billion.

BlackRock follows, holding 540,020,228 shares, or 7.30% of Microsoft. Its stake is worth approximately $293.4 billion as of MSFT's October 13 close.

news.Title: Franklin Templeton CEO says AI is hiding a bigger tech story
news.Content: Every gold rush has a quiet second act. The prospectors grab the headlines, but the people selling jeans, building railroads, and running the banks often walk away with the money. Wall Street has spent three years telling one story about technology. Chips, data centers, and power plants got the attention, and the stocks attached to them got the gains. That spending hasn't slowed. Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), Oracle (ORCL), and CoreWeave (CRWV) are on pace to pour about $785 billion into capital projects this year, with the total closing in on $1 trillion in 2027, Moody's projected, as reported by DatacenterDynamics . The productivity boom all that money is supposed to buy is much harder to find in the data. Your paycheck, your 401(k), and your employer's hiring plans are all quietly pricing in a payoff that hasn't fully arrived. One of the most powerful people in asset management thinks the market may be reading the wrong scoreboard. Real productivity gains from artificial intelligence are still to come as companies move past building AI infrastructure and start using it to unlock new revenue and efficiency, Franklin Templeton (BEN) CEO Jenny Johnson said in an Oct. 12 interview with CNBC . Johnson runs a firm that oversaw about $1.83 trillion in client assets at the end of August, according to Franklin Templeton . When she says the payoff is still ahead, she is talking about where trillions of retirement dollars could flow next. Jenny Johnson puts a later date on AI's productivity boom Her most striking line was about everything else. "AI probably masks so many other technological advances," Johnson said, CNBC noted. That's a telling remark from a CEO whose firm has made early bets on other new technology. Franklin's OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund, launched in 2021, was the first U.S.-registered fund to record share ownership on a public blockchain, according to Franklin Templeton . Related: AI won't trigger mass layoffs yet, Fed study says Johnson has been building toward this argument all year. Companies that "get it right will take off, leaving the others behind," she said at Davos in January, Bloomberg reported. Back then, she also noted that market enthusiasm had centered on the picks-and-shovels suppliers. Her Oct. 12 comments suggest the spotlight is about to swing toward the businesses actually using the tools. Fed survey of nearly 6,000 executives tells a slower story I wanted to know whether the hard data backs Johnson up, so I went to one of the largest firm-level AI surveys available. The March working paper polled nearly 6,000 CFOs, CEOs, and senior executives across the U.S., the U.K., Germany, and Australia, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta . Story Continues The results line up with Johnson's timeline almost exactly. About 70% of firms actively use AI. More than 80% of firms report no AI impact on employment or productivity over the past three years. Executives expect AI to lift productivity by 1.4% over the next three years. U.S. nonfarm business productivity rose 2.2% in the year through the second quarter, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics . Run the math on that third bullet, and it works out to less than half a percentage point a year. That's a modest return on a capital program approaching $1 trillion. The fourth bullet is the more interesting one. My analysis is simple: If eight in 10 companies saw no AI effect on productivity, AI can't be doing most of the work behind that 2.2% gain. Cloud and older digital tools are doing the heavy lifting Johnson has said as much before, crediting cloud computing and earlier digital advances for recent productivity gains rather than AI, according to TheStreet . I've covered payment rails and fintech for years, and the pattern feels familiar. Real-time payments, cloud-based banking cores, and tokenized funds rolled out with far less fanfare than chatbots, yet they changed how money actually moves. More Artificial Intelligence : Bots playing fake AI songs siphoned $8 million from real artists AI Is Deciding What You Pay for Groceries — And It Knows You OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has a biblical-level warning about AI That is the hidden story in Johnson's comment. AI gets credit for gains that older, less glamorous technology is quietly delivering, while AI's own payoff sits further out. Franklin's own portfolio managers see that delay as an opportunity. AI-driven productivity benefits "may not yet be fully reflected in earnings expectations," Franklin Templeton portfolio manager Grant Bowers wrote. Bowers added that the bottleneck is moving from chips to power, cooling and transmission, which can take years to permit and build. That pushes the timeline out further. What Franklin Templeton's CEO means for your 401(k) If you own a broad index fund, you already have a big stake in the AI build-out through the largest tech companies. You are paying for the shovels whether you meant to or not. What Johnson is describing is the next phase, when the winners are companies that turn AI into lower costs and new revenue. Those could be banks, insurers, retailers, or logistics firms that rarely show up in AI headlines. A practical check takes five minutes. Pull up your fund's top 10 holdings and ask how many of them sell AI capacity and how many buy it. If the list leans heavily toward the sellers, you are betting on the first act of this story far more than the second. The point of the exercise is knowing which half of Johnson's argument your retirement money is riding on. The risk cuts the other way, too. Moody's warned earlier this year of a possible "reassessment of creditworthiness" if hyperscaler profit growth fails to materialize, according to DatacenterDynamics. The next test arrives in late October, when the biggest spenders report third-quarter results. Watch the capital spending guidance, but watch the customers more closely. The AI trade so far has rewarded the people building the mine. Johnson is betting the next fortune goes to whoever figures out what to do with the gold. news.Title: Skyworks (SWKS) Pays 147% of Earnings as Dividends With Over 29% of Its Float Short. Can the Dividend Hold?
news.Content:
Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: SWKS ) closed at $76.56 on October 13. The stock has returned 35.5% over the last six months, compared to a 21.5% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 14% for State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

The payout ratio moved because the denominator collapsed, not because the dividend rose. Skyworks sells components that sit inside other companies' phones, so its revenue is decided in design meetings it does not attend. Everything difficult about owning this stock follows from that one fact.

SWKS ranked 11th in our list of the 11 Best 5G Stocks to Buy Now . To see which stocks outranked it, click HERE .

The Dividend Is Covered by Cash, Not by Earnings:

Earnings fell 67.70% in the most recent quarter while revenue fell only 3.10%, which is operating leverage running hard in reverse at a company with a large fixed cost base. That collapse in profit is what produced a payout above a hundred and forty percent of earnings. The dividend itself did not change.

What keeps it payable is cash. Free cash flow comfortably exceeded reported net income, which is the measure that matters for a distribution and the one the payout ratio ignores entirely. The balance sheet is not the constraint either, because cash slightly exceeds total debt and the current ratio is above three, which is a genuinely conservative position for a semiconductor company. A payout ratio measures earnings while this dividend is paid out of cash, a distinction that matters more across the chipmakers billionaires concentrated on than almost anywhere. The one they bought most of is up 18% since June.

The competitive picture also changed on October 5, when Skyworks completed its combination with Qorvo. Removing its closest rival in radio frequency chips improves the bargaining position of what remains, and management expects at least half a billion dollars of annual cost savings within three years.

DON'T MISS: 10 Most Undervalued Quality Stocks to Invest In

Who Actually Decides Skyworks' Revenue:

Short interest of 29.32% is among the highest in the sector, and the concern behind it is specific rather than general. A radio frequency chip supplier depends on a small number of handset programmes, and losing content in one phone generation moves revenue in a way no cost programme can offset.

That is the whole risk, and it is not hypothetical. The recent revenue decline reflects exactly this dynamic.

The multiples show the market pricing a recovery rather than a decline. The stock trades at 13.40 times forward against a trailing figure near forty-two, which requires earnings per share to roughly triple to $5.70.

Story Continues

A forward multiple deserves the most scepticism in exactly this kind of business, because handset demand is cyclical and consensus forecasts are least reliable when cycles turn. Every figure here describes Skyworks on its own, since the merger closed after the last reported quarter, and guidance for the combined company arrives with the November results. A forecast is an assumption, and handset cycles are where assumptions break, which is why a buyer is usually better served by the quality businesses still available at a discount .

The Valuation Case:

The verdict is that Skyworks looks cheap only if the recovery in the forward estimate actually arrives, and fully valued if it does not. The trailing figure reflects a trough and the forward figure reflects an assumption rather than a commitment. The balance sheet buys time to find out, which is worth something, because a company with net cash and a strong current ratio can wait through a weak handset cycle without issuing equity. What actually delivered is a fair check on what a forward estimate is worth, and on that score the stocks we tipped for high returns read better, with the top name up 24% since January.

Conclusion:

The dividend is safer than the payout ratio suggests and the business is weaker than the dividend implies. Free cash flow comfortably covers the distribution, cash exceeds total debt, and the balance sheet is conservative. However, earnings collapsed on a small revenue decline. A large share of the float is sold short, and the forward multiple requires earnings per share to roughly triple. A handset supplier that loses content in one generation rarely wins it back, so revenue is the only line that matters here.

Market Sentiment:

Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS) was held by 35 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $1.52 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is level with 35 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $1.40 billion in the previous quarter.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SWKS as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Dan Ives has laid out his top technology picks heading into 2027, naming Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ), Palantir ( NASDAQ:PLTR ), Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ), and CrowdStrike ( NASDAQ:CRWD ) as his five favorite stocks as he bets the AI spending boom still has much further to run. Ives, the former Wedbush technology analyst, initiated all five names at Outperform and argued investors are still underestimating the scale of the coming AI investment cycle. Initiating tech coverage tonite. In our view, investors underestimating the scale and scope of this $4 trillion dollar spending wave next few years, Ives said. Nvidia received a $300 price target , with Ives calling the company the foundational compute platform for the AI economy. Apple was assigned a $400 target , based on expectations that AI could support a stronger device-upgrade cycle and continued services growth. Microsoft received a $650 price target , while Palantir was given a $250 target as enterprise customers increasingly deploy AI across business operations. CrowdStrike received a $335 target , with Ives pointing to rising cybersecurity demand as companies deploy more AI agents. Ives also highlighted Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) as his preferred disruptive technology play, initiating the stock at Outperform and calling it one of the market's most important AI and robotics platforms. His broader thesis centers on infrastructure spending. Goldman Sachs estimates AI-related capital investment could reach roughly $4 trillion to $8 trillion over the next five years . Supply, not demand, defines this phase of the AI Revolution cycle, Ives said, arguing the industry remains in the early stages of the buildout. Investor Takeaway I think the most interesting part of Ives' list is how broadly he defines the AI trade. Nvidia captures compute. Microsoft captures cloud and enterprise AI. Palantir targets deployment. CrowdStrike adds cybersecurity. Apple offers a consumer-device angle. That makes the list less about one AI winner and more about owning different layers of the ecosystem. The obvious risk is valuation. Several of these stocks have already posted substantial gains, particularly CrowdStrike, which is up nearly 146% year to date according to the figures cited. For investors, the key question is whether earnings growth and AI monetization can keep pace with those expectations. If Ives is right that the market is still early in a multi-trillion-dollar spending cycle, these companies could continue benefiting. If spending slows or returns disappoint, the same premium valuations could become much harder to defend. news.Title: Does the Risk-Reward Profile Still Favor Alphabet (GOOGL) Investors?
news.Content:
Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) has outpaced the market by more than 26 percentage points during the last 1 year, and a massive gap between its operating cash flow and free cash flow reflects on how much this tech giant is betting on accelerated AI spending. Investors are less concerned about the quality of Alphabet's business, and more about whether its current valuation reflects future projections. Is it Now a Cloud Growth Story?

Alphabet was trading at $352.72 on October 12 closing. The stock has jumped 12.69% in 2026, but has fared higher over the past 52 weeks with a 44% gain. This compares with 17.4% for the S&P 500 during the stated period. Hence, much of the rally came during the last quarter of calendar 2025, and the pace has cooled this year.

A rapid growth in enterprise demand for AI capabilities has resulted in massive traction for Alphabet's cloud business. During the recently reported quarter, the Google Cloud revenue clocked in at $24.8 billion, representing an 82% growth compared to the corresponding period last year. It also yielded close to 36% operating margin.

The segment is seeing multi-year commitments from government and commercial customers, as its contracted backlog has grown to $514 billion. It also now accounts for a higher chunk of Alphabet's total revenue, contributing approximately 20.7% of Alphabet's total revenue in Q2 2026, compared with 14.1% a year earlier. Alphabet recently made it to our list of 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy Now According to Billionaires , ranked #2. Which other stocks made it to that list?

Balance Sheet Strength Yields Substantial Cushion

With a $4.12 trillion market capitalization, operational performance looks strong. On a trailing-twelve-month basis, total revenue came in at $445.87 billion. This includes a 24.2% year-over-year jump in its consolidated topline, which stood at $119.8 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2026. Alphabet generated $173.16 billion EBITDA, and with 34.03% operating margin one can say that the underlying growth is not coming at the expense of efficiency.

Story Continues

The balance sheet is one of the strong points for Alphabet, as the company sits comfortably with debt-to-equity ratio of 18.9%. A large debt balance of $120.8 billion is easily overpowered by its healthy holdings of around $242.5 billion. Alphabet's substantial net financial assets provide a meaningful cushion, although a portion consists of equity investments exposed to market fluctuations.

Institutional Sentiment

Based on data tracked across 1,000+ hedge funds by Insider Monkey, institutional sentiment toward the company remains strong. According to 13F filing data, number of smart-money managers with long-term exposure in the stock has been going up. A total of 275 hedge funds held positions by the end of Q2 2026, compared to 265 in Q1 2026.

Other notable institutional investors include Vanguard Capital Management and FMR, holding 6.53% and 4.27% of outstanding shares respectively.

Way Forward

Valuation metrics appear attractive at first glance. The stock trades at a trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 17.62x, which looks compelling for a company with this growth profile. However, the forward P/E ratio is higher at 22.83x. This does not necessarily imply a decline in underlying earnings, as trailing profits benefited from substantial non-recurring investment gains. But Alphabet's earnings multiple tells only part of the story. Is Microsoft actually the cheaper AI cloud stock once capital spending is factored in?

Overall, Alphabet looks reasonably valued rather than cheap on a forward basis. It's risk-reward profile remains cautiously favorable, provided cloud growth can justify its elevated AI spending.

The company's total commitments for leases that have not yet commenced were $329.1 billion as of the quarter ended June 30, Microsoft said Wednesday in a regulatory filing. That's up from $196.6 billion in the prior period.

"That's really a signal of the continued demand strength that we see," Jonathan Neilson, Microsoft investor relations chief, said in an interview. "These leases are going to be there to serve demand for many many years."

The future costs, which come on top of active leases, won't appear on Microsoft's balance sheet until it begins making payments on them. The company said they are "primarily" for data centers and some are "subject to certain contractual conditions being met."

This represents Microsoft's largest quarterly jump in data center leasing by far. The software giant continues to be held back by a lack of data center capacity after taking a pause on its leasing activity through much of 2025.

news.Title: Investors Are Paying More for Walmart Than Amazon. Here’s Why That Doesn’t Add Up.
news.Content:
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ: WMT ) has opened a fulfillment center of more than 900,000 square feet in Stockton, California. The site uses automation and machine learning to cut the usual 12-step order process down to five. It will also employ about 1,000 people. The company says its next-generation fulfillment centers, of which Stockton is the fifth, will enable it to reach 95% of the U.S. population with next-day or two-day shipping when combined with the rest of its network. The stock closed more than 2% higher on October 8, its fourth straight gain. Beyond its push for faster delivery, Walmart's defensive appeal remains a key attraction for investors. But which other companies joined WMT on our list of the 10 Best Bear Market Stocks to Invest In Right Now ?

Automation Is Changing Walmart's Business

I believe Stockton is just one piece of a much bigger shift. Walmart's U.S. e-commerce sales have grown more than 20% for 10 straight quarters, and fast deliveries jumped 48% last quarter. CFO John David Rainey said much of Walmart's recent spending has gone into supply chain automation and speed. That spending is also lifting higher-margin businesses. Advertising rose 38% last quarter, and membership fee revenue hit a record. Faster delivery brings more shoppers online, which feeds those businesses.

Still, Walmart remains a retailer at heart. Its stock fell 9% after its August report, despite beating estimates and raising its outlook. The decline reflected slow comparable sales and a soft Q3 guide, with operating income expected to grow just 2% to 4% as Walmart puts tariff refunds back into lower prices. Walmart's short-term margin pressure hasn't stopped hedge funds from backing the retail giant. See why WMT ranks No. 3 among the 10 Best Dividend Kings to Buy According to Hedge Funds and which other stocks made the list?

Walmart Costs More Than Amazon

Walmart's stock trades at a premium to its historical norms. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 37.48x sits about 24% above its 5-year average. That's even higher than Amazon, which trades at about 31x despite also owning AWS, a fast-growing, high-margin cloud business. The forward Price-to-sales ratio of 1.14x is also about 28% above its average. Yet analysts expect EPS to grow only 9% this fiscal year, about 12% in each of the next two, and 7% in fiscal 2030. Even based on fiscal 2030 earnings, the P/E would be around 28x. As of July 31, Walmart carried approximately $38.9 billion in net debt, excluding lease obligations. In my view, the automation story is big, but the stock already prices in a lot of it.

Story Continues

Hedge fund interest in Walmart is rising. Funds holding the stock rose from 99 in Q1 to 111 in Q2, while their stakes edged up from $10.9 billion to $11.1 billion.

Stockton shows Walmart is building a faster, more efficient business. At nearly 38 times earnings with about 10% annual growth, though, I'd wait for a better entry point.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of WMT as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than WMT and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

Compared with the fund's reported holdings as of June 30, 2026, the top of the portfolio looks different. Micron

Micron Technology develops, manufactures and sells semiconductor memory and storage products. It is the largest holding in RANK at 9.21% of net assets, compared with 6.65% at June 30, 2026.

On TipRanks, the stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating. Of the 28 analysts who rated the stock over the past three months, 27 rated it a Buy. The average price target is $1,621.67.

Demand for memory chips from AI data centers has outpaced supply, which has supported memory prices and Micron's revenue.

Five-star TipRanks-rated Robert W.Baird analyst Tristan Gerra recently reiterated his Buy rating on Micron with a price target of $1,520. He highlighted Micron's expectations for materially tighter Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM) supply in fiscal 2027–2028 versus 2026, alongside industry bit growth in the low‑20% range and incremental capacity ramps. This, he said, should underpin stronger pricing and justify a stock rerating over time.

He also pointed to a steady path of gross margin expansion through fiscal 2027, supported by long‑term customer supply agreements that lock in pricing bands and secure a large share of Micron's future output and revenue through 2030.

Nvidia

Nvidia designs graphics processors, computing platforms and networking products used in AI data centers. It is the second-largest holding in RANK at 6.73% of net assets, compared with 4.51% at June 30, 2026.

Schneider also cited Nvidia's tightly integrated hardware and networking stack as a structural advantage as customers seek higher performance and efficiency from their AI spending. He highlighted generative AI use cases in coding and cybersecurity, Nvidia's growing share of AI investment, and its ability to manage supply and data center capacity constraints.

Eli Lilly (LLY)

The pharmaceutical company, arguably best known for weight-loss drugs such as Zepbound, is the third-largest holding in RANK at 5.88% of net assets, compared with 4.60% at June 30, 2026.

On TipRanks, the stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating. Of the 23 analysts who rated the stock over the past three months, 20 rated it a Buy. The average price target is $1,366.05.

Lilly's revenue comes from a broad range of medicines, spanning weight-loss and diabetes treatments as well as cardiovascular and cancer drugs.

Berenberg analyst Kerry Holford recently upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold. She expects the drugmaker to exceed its 2026 guidance, driven by growth in weight-loss drug sales, and views Lilly as the market leader in obesity and diabetes medications.

Visa

Visa operates a global electronic payments network connecting consumers, merchants and financial institutions. New to the portfolio, it is the fourth-largest holding in RANK at 5.79% of net assets.

On TipRanks, the analyst consensus on Visa is a Strong Buy. Of the 28 analysts who rated the stock over the last three months, 26 rated it a Buy. The average price target is $425.54.

He also sees upside from newer growth drivers, including agentic AI, which he said is already driving incremental product discovery, and faster shipping.

news.Title: Microsoft’s New AI Model Is 35 Times Faster Than OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol. Wait Until You See the Price Tag.
news.Content:
On Oct. 9, CEO Satya Nadella announced that Microsoft (MSFT) has released a new AI model called Microsoft-Decision-1. Most AI models, like ChatGPT, write text and work through problems step by step. This one does something narrower. It makes quick choices, such as picking a category, sorting requests, or deciding an AI agent's next move. Microsoft says it runs about 35 times faster than OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol on these tasks. It's available through Microsoft Foundry and OpenRouter.

Why Cheap Decisions Matter

Then there's the price, which is almost too low to believe. Decision-1 costs $0.042 per million input tokens, and output is free. OpenAI's own decision model charges more than twice that. Price matters here because AI agents make dozens of small choices before finishing a single task. Running a large model for each one quickly gets slow and expensive. Microsoft's Xbox research team saw this firsthand. It used Decision-1 to sort over 10,000 pieces of player feedback. The model matched GPT-6 Sol in quality while running more than 14 times faster at about 1/200th of the cost.

​There's also a strategic angle many investors may overlook. Microsoft built Decision-1 on an open-source model from Alibaba's (BABA) Qwen family and plans to rebuild it later on with its own models and OpenAI's. That flexibility shows that Microsoft can build useful AI tools without depending on a single partner. If agents spread across businesses as Microsoft expects, cheap decision models like this could make them far more affordable to run.

​About Microsoft Stock

Microsoft Corporation is a global technology company that develops and sells a wide range of software, cloud services, devices, and business solutions, serving both individual users and enterprise customers worldwide. Its flagship products include Windows, Microsoft 365, Azure, LinkedIn, and Xbox. The company was founded in 1975 and is headquartered in Redmond, Washington.

Over the last 12 months, MSFT shares have gained 5%, underperforming the S&P 500's ($SPX) 17% rise during the same period. The stock hit its 52-week high in October 2025 but started falling after that. However, this year the stock is up 14% year-to-date (YTD), slightly outperforming the S&P 500's 13% gain over the same period.

Story Continues

Microsoft trades slightly below its historical valuation, which stands out given where its growth is heading. The forward non-GAAP price-to-earnings (P/E) of 27.07x is about 11% under its 5-year average of 30.50x. That discount is unusual because analysts expect growth to speed up. EPS is forecast to rise about 14% this fiscal year, then roughly 20% to 22% over the following two. I think the discount mostly reflects worries about how much Microsoft is spending on AI. As I covered earlier, that includes massive projects like its Fairwater data center in Wisconsin. That's where tools like Decision-1 come in. If cheaper AI models help those investments pay off sooner, Microsoft could return to its usual multiple and possibly earn a premium, given how fast its earnings are expected to grow.

Microsoft Guides for Strong Q1 Revenue

Microsoft Corp reported its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on July 29. It reported revenue of $90.01 billion, up 18% year-over-year (YoY). The earnings per share came in at $4.74, comfortably beating the Wall Street consensus of $4.24. The company said fiscal 2026 was its strongest year yet. The company's cloud business remained the main growth engine. Microsoft Cloud revenue exceeded $214 billion for the year, up 27%, while Azure passed $100 billion in annual revenue. Gross margin for the quarter was down 67% YoY because of a mix shift and AI infrastructure spending. However, the operating margin was 45%, slightly higher than a year earlier. The results indicated that Microsoft is still growing rapidly even at its large scale.

Looking forward, CFO Amy Hood guided Q1 fiscal 2027 total revenue to be between $89.85 billion and $90.95 billion. The company expects Azure growth to remain strong, with revenue in Intelligent Cloud projected at $40.95 billion to $41.25 billion for the quarter. For Productivity and Business Processes, the company guided revenue of $36.7 billion to $37 billion. Moreover, capital spending is likely to remain high, with first-quarter spending above $50 billion, including lease reclassification effects.

What Do Analysts Expect for MSFT Stock?

Barclays analyst Raimo Lenschow maintained a "Buy" rating on MSFT and set a price target of $600. Similarly, Deutsche Bank analyst Brad Zelnick reiterated a "Buy" rating while raising the firm's price target from $550 to $600. In contrast to these two, Phillip Securities downgraded MSFT to a "Hold" rating with a price target of $515.

Based on 51 Wall Street analysts covering the stock, MSFT holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. However, its mean price target of $579.78 suggests just 6% upside from current levels, indicating limited near-term gains at the average estimate. The high price target of $725 implies 33% upside, showing that some analysts see considerably greater potential.

news.Title: How to Play Microsoft Stock Ahead of an Upcoming Maia 300 Launch
news.Content:
The war for artificial intelligence (AI) supremacy has a new central battleground, and it is inference. Apart from the established winners of the training era, such as Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD), hyperscalers are increasingly becoming important players here by making their own custom AI chips.

Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google, with its TPUs, got a head start; however, Microsoft (MSFT), with the launch of the Maia 300 AI chip in 2027, is not willing to cede ground. Promising 40% more token output per megawatt than the GPU systems dominated by Nvidia and AMD, the company has developed the chip with a focus on inference. To be manufactured through TSMC's (TSM) leading 2nm process, Microsoft said in a statement, "Maia 300 is designed with an inference-first architecture optimized for long-context, memory-intensive and decode-heavy AI workloads. This involves balancing compute, memory bandwidth, networking and power efficiency at cloud scale."

More News from Barchart

Shares of Microsoft ended 1.1% higher on this news in yesterday's trading session to come, very close to regaining its $4 trillion market cap. Currently valued at a market cap of $3.97 trillion, MSFT stock is up 11.9% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The stock also offers a dividend yield of 0.7% and has been raising dividends consecutively for the past 21 years, with $10.2 billion returned to shareholders in the form of repurchases in Q2 2026.

Having said that, how does Maia 300 fit into Microsoft's wider AI strategy? Let's find out.

Mai(a) Own

Why are hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon (AMZN) spending billions to build their own chips? The chips from Nvidia and AMD are fulfilling their needs quite well at the moment, and the duo is in a constant mode of building new and more powerful generations of chips. Moreover, the hyperscalers are buying them as well, clearly signalling that even if they are developing their own chips, they will continue to source the ones produced by Nvidia and AMD.

Then, why? Well, there are a few reasons. First, the companies want to reduce their dependence on outsiders, specifically Nvidia, which has an almost hegemonic presence in the GPU market, which in turn gives it immense pricing power, leaving the hyperscalers vulnerable. Secondly, custom chips are cheaper (in terms of cost per AI workload) than those from the likes of Nvidia and AMD, and thirdly, the companies can build their own chips to cater to their particular needs and focus on aspects they want to. Finally, designing their own chips facilitates tighter integration between their processors, software, and broader data-center infrastructure, potentially improving performance while creating differentiated offerings for cloud customers.

Story Continues

Specifically with Microsoft, Maia 300 is a continuation of its attempt to get more AI work done inside the power and cooling limits of its data centers. Each Maia 300 accelerator is designed with 288 gigabytes of HBM4 memory and 18 TB/s of peak memory bandwidth. That bandwidth is two and a half times Maia 200's. Notably, Microsoft plans to put 96 accelerators in a rack drawing 167 kilowatts, with 27.6 terabytes of memory across the rack. It says that the configuration can generate up to seven times as many tokens per rack as Maia 200.

Ultimately, Microsoft intends to make Maia its primary inference system as it expands the family beginning in 2027. It names Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Dragon Copilot among the services that could benefit from the architecture. For a customer, the expected result is quicker responses or greater capacity when many people are using those services, not a new processor they must install. Lower serving cost might also allow Microsoft more room to price AI features competitively, though it has not promised a customer price cut yet.

Microsoft's Outstanding Q2

Microsoft reported solid financial performance as revenue advanced 18% year-over-year (YoY) to $90 billion, coming in $2.4 billion ahead of forecasts. The Intelligent Cloud segment, which includes Azure, grew 31.5% YoY to $39.31 billion. While operating margins for the segment remained roughly unchanged from the previous year, absolute operating income increased 31.4% to $15.96 billion. Azure revenue specifically rose 43% YoY, exceeding the expected range of 39% to 40%. For the full year, Azure crossed a $100 billion run rate for the first time. Commercial backlog nearly doubled YoY to $684 billion, with about 30% of that total expected to convert to revenue over the next twelve months, highlighting strong demand for the company's cloud products and services.

Earnings per share increased 23% to $4.74, surpassing the consensus estimate of $4.24 and extending the streak of consecutive earnings beats to nine quarters. This result includes a $3.2 billion gain associated with the company's investment in Anthropic, the developer of Claude.

Cash flow stayed robust, as net cash from operations climbed to $55.44 billion, reflecting a 30% rise from the year-earlier period. Microsoft ended the quarter with $76.8 billion in cash, substantially higher than its short-term debt of $9.23 billion.

From a valuation perspective, MSFT appears reasonably valued. The forward P/E and P/S of 27.07 and 10.15 are above the sector medians of 23.29 and 3.53, respectively, while on a forward P/CF basis, MSFT stock is trading at 17.43, lower than the sector median of 20.95.

What Do Analysts Think of MSFT Stock?

Thus, analysts have earmarked an overall rating of "Strong Buy" for MSFT stock. The mean target price of $579.78 indicates a potential upside of about 6% from current levels. Out of the 51 analysts covering the stock, 41 have a "Strong Buy" rating, five have a "Moderate Buy" rating, four have a "Hold" rating, and one has a "Strong Sell" rating.

news.Title: Alibaba Unveils Game-Changing Device to Challenge Meta
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Alibaba ( NYSE:BABA ) is pushing deeper into consumer AI hardware with a new generation of Qwen smart glasses starting at 2,999 yuan, or about $450 , putting the Chinese tech giant into more direct competition with Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ). Alibaba unveiled the Qwen Glasses N1 series in Hangzhou, roughly a year after launching its first-generation smart glasses. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with BABA. Is BABA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The new models feature upgraded cameras and sensors, while the Pro version adds eye-tracking capabilities . The glasses can support functions including shopping, payments and health tracking, while integrating more deeply with Alibaba's Qwen AI assistant. Battery life is rated at up to 25 hours of standby time or nine hours of music playback on a single charge. The Pro edition costs 3,499 yuan , according to Wu Jianjun, general manager of Qwen AI hardware products. The pricing is notable. Rather than aggressively undercutting rivals, Alibaba is positioning the devices in roughly the same range as Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses, suggesting the company wants to compete on features, integration and quality. Meta, meanwhile, recently expanded its own smart-glasses lineup with a simplified $349 camera-free model centered around its Muse AI assistant. Alibaba is also broadening Qwen beyond glasses. The company has begun selling Qwen Clip AI earbuds , developed with Bose, giving users another wearable interface for accessing its AI assistant. Alibaba shares were down about 1% in premarket trading. Investor Takeaway I think the bigger story is that Alibaba is trying to turn Qwen from a software product into a consumer hardware ecosystem . That matters because smart glasses could become one of the most important interfaces for AI assistants if users begin interacting with models through cameras, sensors and voice instead of phones and laptops. Alibaba also has an advantage Meta does not: a massive commerce ecosystem. Integrating shopping and payments directly into wearable hardware could make the glasses more useful in everyday transactions and potentially strengthen Alibaba's broader consumer platform. But adoption remains the key question. For investors, the important metrics to watch are unit sales, Qwen engagement, hardware margins and whether consumers actually use shopping, payments and health functions regularly . If the devices gain traction, Alibaba could create a much more direct consumer entry point for its AI strategy. news.Title: Marvell (MRVL) Raises Its 2028 Revenue Target to $20 Billion. Can Growth Justify the Premium?

Marvell's ambitious AI revenue targets also raise a compelling question for growth-focused investors: how does it compare with the 11 AI stocks that could go to the moon ? A closer look at Marvell's valuation and its path toward $90 billion in annual sales reveals another side of the debate, particularly why the stock's earnings multiple may look considerably different depending on which year's profits investors use. Google Makes the Long-Term Forecast Less Theoretical The biggest evidence is Marvell's agreement with Google. The arrangement could be associated with as much as $120 billion of cumulative qualifying purchases through fiscal 2033 if all warrant milestones are reached, although that figure is not a guaranteed purchase commitment. Story Continues The opportunity also extends beyond a single accelerator. Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) says the relationship spans inference accelerators, networking, storage, memory interfaces, and near-memory compute, effectively expanding custom silicon deeper into the AI data center. That breadth matters because hyperscalers increasingly want alternatives to Nvidia's general-purpose GPUs. But it also creates competition. Broadcom remains entrenched in Google's TPU ecosystem, while Qualcomm is pursuing the same custom-inference opportunity. That competition raises a bigger question: can Marvell turn its expanding AI partnerships into a lasting competitive advantage, or will rivals limit its ability to capture the opportunity? A separate analysis of Marvell's economic moat and whether it is widening or narrowing explores the competitive position behind its ambitious growth targets. Seaport Research captured that tension in September, initiating Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) at Buy with a $270 target while warning that custom silicon can be a "fickle business." That growth potential could justify the premium valuation if Marvell delivers on its ambitious targets. However, the scale and speed of execution required leave little room for disappointment. While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MRVL as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Title: Deutsche Bank Sees Major Reckoning Ahead for AI Investors
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Deutsche Bank says artificial intelligence could theoretically reach superintelligence by 2030 , but only if model scaling continues, AI systems learn to improve themselves and the industry can overcome enormous constraints around power, infrastructure and financing. Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The bank's Research Institute said the path depends heavily on whether future AI systems can autonomously improve the technology used to build the next generation of models. But the physical requirements are staggering. Deutsche Bank estimates that training a hypothetical AGI-like model could require $300 billion to $500 billion of infrastructure and roughly 6 gigawatts of power . Running an equivalent training cycle in just four months using Nvidia (NVDA) Vera Rubin chips could require approximately 7.8 million chips and 26 gigawatts of facility power , with the infrastructure costing about $900 billion at today's prices . The bank estimates a comparable cluster could fall to roughly $200 billion by 2030 if current improvements in computing efficiency continue. The industry is already spending aggressively. Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOG ), Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ), Meta ( NASDAQ:META ), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) and Oracle ( NYSE:ORCL ) are expected to invest almost $800 billion in capital expenditures this year , according to Deutsche Bank, with annual spending potentially exceeding $1 trillion through 2030 and beyond . Yet the bank stressed that the AI investment case does not require superintelligence. AI adoption by businesses is reportedly advancing roughly three times faster than previous mobile, internet and cloud computing waves , while AI-economy revenue outside China could exceed $200 billion in 2026 , up from less than $1 billion in 2022. Investor Takeaway I think the most important part of Deutsche Bank's report is not the 2030 superintelligence prediction itself. It is the sheer economic and physical infrastructure required even to attempt it . The numbers show why companies such as Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet could continue benefiting from massive AI spending even if true superintelligence remains elusive. But there is also a clear risk. Much of today's infrastructure spending is being financed on expectations of future revenue rather than cash flows already being generated. Deutsche Bank highlighted growing pressure on hyperscaler free cash flow as capex rises. Google DeepMind's Jasjeet Sekhon described the danger as an AI air pocket where spending arrives first but the expected revenue fails to follow. Story Continues For investors, I would watch hyperscaler capex, AI revenue growth, data-center power availability, financing costs and improvements in compute efficiency . If revenues scale alongside spending, the buildout can continue. If monetization lags too far behind infrastructure investment, capital rather than technology could become the biggest obstacle long before 2030. news.Title: Zuckerberg Admits Meta Lacked AI Certainty on $200 Billion Bet
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg said Meta Platforms Inc. had to commit to spending hundreds of billions of dollars last year on the infrastructure needed to power its artificial intelligence products before the company had any idea as to whether they would succeed.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Epic Games Delays Disney Project, Asks Developers to Use More AI

Apple Unveils $299 HomeView Hub as Part of New Smart Home Push

Chip Selloff Sparks 7% Korea Rout on Brewing Worries Over AI

Chip Selloff Rolls On as Big Bank Earnings Begin: Markets Wrap

PepsiCo Cuts Estimates for Poppi Payout While Soda Sales Slump

"We're going to write this check for like, I don't know, $100 billion or $200 billion," Zuckerberg said on the Cheeky Pint podcast posted Monday. "You sure this is going to work?" he recalled asking Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang.

It's a revealing disclosure for a company that has struggled to persuade investors to accept its ballooning expenses for ambitious AI bets. Zuckerberg has repeatedly said these bets will pay off, but shareholders are growing increasingly antsy over Meta's ability to bring in sales and profit at a fast enough pace.

Over the course of the two-hour-plus podcast with host John Collison, Zuckerberg and Wang revealed that Meta's Chief Financial Officer Susan Li warned on multiple occasions that the cost of failure would be enormous. "I think Susan scared you a little bit," Zuckerberg said.

"The joke every time we talked about it would just be like, 'Yeah, and we hope it's all going to work and be good,'" Wang recalled. Short of giving a "vibe report" on where the team was headed, he could not guarantee success despite the "obscenely large" amount of money the company was investing. It was "not clear at all that it was going to work."

On Monday, Meta debuted a long-awaited new AI model that it said is a big leap over its own predecessors, with "frontier capabilities" that its leadership said put it on par with OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC's Claude when it comes to coding, or working through financial or legal questions. The milestone will test whether Zuckerberg's multibillion-dollar push to rebuild its AI team has improved the technology enough to compete among leaders.

Meta also recently launched Muse, its personalized AI assistant designed to automate a range of tasks for consumers, including shopping, buying movie tickets and scheduling appointments. Zuckerberg admitted he wasn't sure what the consumer reaction would be like to Muse.

Story Continues

"Our median expectation was like, 'All right, we're probably going to have to like iterate on this a bit,'" he said.

The company is spending hundreds of billions of dollars to compete against American tech rivals, including Alphabet Inc., OpenAI and Anthropic, in a race to develop leading AI models and products. It is one of the tech industry's heaviest spenders when it comes to AI data centers.

Next week, investors will get another look at the company's financials when it reports results after the market closes on Oct. 21. Last quarter, Meta reported its lowest free cash flow in years — a sign of its compounding expenses on data centers and smart glasses — sending shares down 8%.

The stock is up more than 12% so far this year through Monday's close.

news.Content:

The jury found that Arm breached its architectural license agreement with Qualcomm, failed to honor its commitments, and intentionally acted to disrupt Qualcomm's business operations, according to a statement from Qualcomm.

The verdict, dated October 13, 2026, represents another legal setback for Arm in its ongoing dispute with the smartphone chipmaker. Qualcomm called the ruling a win for innovation and competition.

Qualcomm did not disclose whether the jury awarded damages in connection with the verdict.

Shares of Qualcomm briefly spiked higher and were trading up 2% on Tuesday following the announcement.

In the current case, Qualcomm accused Arm of multiple breaches of their licensing agreement, which extends through 2033. news.Title: Cathie Wood Trims $3.3 Million in Top Tech Stock
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Cathie Wood's ARK Invest trimmed its Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) position on Monday, selling roughly $3.36 million worth of shares while putting fresh capital into a group of biotechnology companies. ARK sold 4,520 Meta shares through the ARK Innovation ETF. Based on Meta's closing price of $742.96, the transaction was worth about $3.36 million. Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The sale is notable because ARK had aggressively added to Meta in September, suggesting the latest move may represent profit-taking or portfolio rebalancing rather than a wholesale change in conviction. Meta shares surged about 25% in September , helped partly by investor enthusiasm around the company's expanding AI strategy. That includes Muse , Meta's AI assistant designed to handle complex, multistep tasks such as booking travel, sending emails and completing transactions. Meta also introduced Muse Wonder , a more advanced family of AI models that CEO Mark Zuckerberg said pushes the company closer to the frontier of artificial intelligence. While trimming Meta, ARK was active on the buy side in biotech. The firm purchased roughly $2.56 million of Alamar Biosciences , around $2.34 million of CRISPR Therapeutics, $2.16 million of Freenome and $2.13 million of Guardant Health. ARK also added shares of Nurix Therapeutics, Intellia Therapeutics and Beam Therapeutics. The firm separately sold about $4.49 million of DraftKings across two of its ETFs. Investor Takeaway I think the most important thing here is not that Cathie Wood suddenly turned bearish on Meta. The timing suggests something more nuanced. ARK had been buying Meta heavily before a strong September rally, so selling a relatively modest $3.36 million position after a 25% monthly gain could simply reflect portfolio discipline. At the same time, ARK is rotating capital toward biotech names where valuations and upside potential may look more asymmetric. That fits Wood's broader strategy of backing disruptive technologies across multiple industries rather than remaining overly concentrated in one winner. For Meta investors, I would focus less on this single ARK trade and more on AI monetization, Muse adoption, advertising growth and whether Meta can turn its expanding AI ecosystem into meaningful incremental revenue . For ARK watchers, the bigger signal is the growing allocation toward genomics and biotech as Wood searches for the next major innovation cycle.
