news.Title: Apple Is Taking on Amazon and Google in the Smart Home With a $299 Siri AI Device. Is HomeView the First Big Win for New CEO John Ternus?
news.Content: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) has built an enormous business by making products that work together. From the iPhone and Apple Watch to the Mac and iPad, the technology giant has given customers plenty of reasons to stay within its family of devices. Now Apple is entering a market that Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) already occupy , hoping to carve out a new business in smart home products by using its upgraded Siri artificial intelligence assistant. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » The company introduced HomeView on Tuesday, a $299 smart home display powered by Siri. I think it could be an interesting opportunity for new CEO John Ternus to demonstrate where he wants to take the company. Apple CEO John Ternus. Image source: Apple. What is Apple's HomeView? HomeView features a 7-inch touchscreen that can sit on a table or be mounted on a wall. It combines entertainment features such as music, photos, and FaceTime video calls with controls for smart home devices, including lights, thermostats, cameras, and door locks. But the biggest attraction may be its upgraded Siri assistant. Apple introduced Siri AI in June, promising more natural conversations and the ability to understand personal information across applications. HomeView takes those capabilities beyond personal devices. It recognizes up to six household members by their faces, automatically displaying personalized information while keeping their private content separate. With a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri can also use information from messages, calendars, and other applications to answer questions or complete tasks. Apple says HomeView uses on-device processing and its Private Cloud Compute technology to handle personal information securely, while compatible security cameras can provide end-to-end encrypted video. A look at the competition Amazon's Echo Show 8 and Echo Show 11 already use Alexa+ to control smart home devices, manage family calendars, and deliver personalized information. Google is also integrating Gemini AI into its Nest smart home products, offering more conversational controls and the ability to handle complicated requests. At $299, HomeView is priced above similar-sized Echo Show products as well as the Google Nest Hub. But that hasn't been a problem in the past; Apple smartphones can run more than $1,000 each, and the company has a loyal customer base -- something that famously attracted Warren Buffett to the stock when Berkshire Hathaway became Apple's largest shareholder. Story Continues AAPL data by YCharts And Apple has an advantage with customers who already own its products. HomeView connects to the iPhone, Apple Watch, and other Apple devices, allowing users to continue Siri conversations across devices. The company also announced a new Apple TV 4K with Siri AI, an upgraded HomePod mini, and a collection of smart home accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Each is a product that can make HomeView more useful and give customers more reasons to invest in Apple and its connected devices. Could HomeView be a win for Apple's new CEO? When Ternus became Apple's CEO in September, he inherited a company with a massive customer base but also questions about its ability to compete in artificial intelligence. Apple faces pressure to deliver meaningful product improvements rather than simply introduce another generation of familiar hardware. With HomeView, Apple is using artificial intelligence to make its existing products more useful while introducing new devices that leverage those capabilities. If HomeView encourages customers to purchase more Apple accessories, use additional services, and keep their existing devices longer, it could strengthen a business model that has served Apple extremely well. For Ternus, making AI a useful part of everyday life could prove more valuable than simply promising the next big technological breakthrough. Missed AI's "Act 1"? "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. news.Title: Nebius (NBIS) Has Pricing Power. Its Earnings Don’t Show It Yet.
news.Content:
Cloud companies don't usually raise prices. Competition in renting out computing power tends to push the other way, with each new chip generation cheapening the last. Yet at the start of this month, Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS ) reset compute prices on its NVIDIA B300, B200, H200, and H100 virtual machines, the exact hardware AI developers are scrambling to rent.

Nebius runs a cloud built specifically for artificial intelligence. It buys NVIDIA GPUs, installs them in data centers across Europe and the US, and rents that capacity to AI labs, start-ups, and tech giants such as Microsoft and Meta. Customers either pay as they go or sign multi-year contracts for dedicated capacity, a surge in infrastructure demand that has turned Nebius into one of the 12 High-Flying Stocks to Invest In . The harder question is whether pricing power can outrun the enormous bill for building it, and the answer hinges on a forecast that looks, at first glance, like bad news.

Scarcity Is the Moat

Nebius doesn't sell patent-protected technology. Its edge is something AI customers currently prize more: GPUs that are powered, networked, and ready to use. Power and data center space have become the scarce inputs in AI, and Nebius has moved aggressively to lock them up. It expects to end 2026 with 5 GW of contracted power and plans to deploy more than 1 GW a year starting in 2027.

The proof shows up in pricing. In its second-quarter 2026 shareholder letter, the company said pricing for older-generation GPUs rose more than 30% from the first quarter, and deals signed in the quarter averaged above $20 million in revenue per MW. In recent weeks, Nebius also introduced spot pricing for preemptible machines, letting the price of spare capacity float with demand.

Growth With Leverage Built In

Second-quarter 2026 revenue reached $582.3 million, up 454% from a year earlier. Annualized recurring revenue (ARR, the current revenue pace stretched over a full year) hit $3.0 billion at the end of June, up from $1.9 billion at the end of March. Adjusted EBITDA swung to $236.2 million, from a $21.0 million loss a year earlier.

Costs are scaling more slowly than sales. Cost of revenue fell to 23% of revenue from 29%, and SG&A dropped to 30% from 65%. That operating leverage sets Nebius apart within a fast-growing group of 11 AI Stocks That Will Go to the Moon , challenging the hyperscalers.

Demand looks locked in, too. Nebius has more than $40 billion in customer commitments. It delivered every contracted capacity tranche to Microsoft and is working on a second agreement with Meta.

Story Continues

Is the Buildout Outrunning the Business?

Nebius spent $8,130.3 million on property, equipment, and intangibles in the first half of 2026 alone, and total debt stood at $8,545.7 million at the end of June. Interest expense jumped to $119.1 million in the quarter from $4.8 million a year earlier, while depreciation climbed to $259.7 million from $75.2 million. The upshot was a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $190.4 million.

The company has leaned on shareholders, too, raising roughly $2.8 billion by selling stock through an at-the-market program, even as news that Nebius Group (NBIS) plans to hike prices sent shares rocketing on strong cloud GPU demand. And with Microsoft and Meta anchoring so much of the demand story, a pullback by either would leave a hole that's hard to fill, a concentration risk common among AI infrastructure stocks.

Prepayments soften the blow. About 70% of second-quarter deals included them, covering 50% to 60% of the related capex, and Nebius expects more than $9 billion in customer prepayments in 2026. But the company is still betting its balance sheet on demand staying tight.

Paying Up for Shrinking Earnings

At 46.08 times forward earnings, as of October 9, Nebius trades well above the sector's 23.23 multiple. Investors usually pay that kind of premium for earnings that are about to grow fast.

Instead, analysts expect earnings per share to fall 62.73% in 2027. That forecast reflects timing more than fading demand: most second-quarter deals are tied to capacity arriving in late 2026, so the depreciation and interest land before the revenue fully does. Even so, a premium multiple on shrinking earnings means you're paying today for profits that sit years out, and the contrast with cash-rich cloud giants like Amazon shows how much faith that takes.

Sentiment reflects the split. Short interest stands at 19.81% of the float, a sizable bet against the stock. Hedge funds moved the other way, with 87 holding Nebius in the most recent quarter, up from 70 in the prior one.

Where the Evidence Points

Nebius's pricing power is real, and the backlog suggests demand isn't fading. But at this multiple, the stock already assumes a smooth handoff from a costly buildout to fat profits, just as earnings are expected to shrink. The setup suits investors comfortable with sharp swings who believe AI compute stays scarce through 2027. Softening GPU pricing, or trouble funding the next gigawatt without heavy dilution, would weaken the case quickly.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of NBIS as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than NBIS and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: MercadoLibre vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
The e-commerce landscape is shifting as regional giants and global software leaders battle for market share. Deciding between MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) and Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) requires weighing hyper-local execution against worldwide scale.

MercadoLibre operates a vertically integrated marketplace and payments system tailored for the unique challenges of Latin America. Shopify offers a versatile software infrastructure that enables merchants to build independent brands globally. Both companies are core holdings for investors seeking exposure to digital commerce, but they vary significantly in valuation and regional focus.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a vast ecosystem through its marketplace and its fintech arm, Mercado Pago. Among retail stocks , it differentiates itself by providing logistics and credit solutions to millions of users. The company partners with Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) for its cloud infrastructure while integrating services from Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) into its loyalty programs.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $28.9 billion, representing a significant 39.1% increase over the prior year. This expansion was supported by a net income of approximately $2.0 billion. The company continues to benefit from its dual-engine model, in which its marketplace drives adoption of its financial services, resulting in a net margin of nearly 6.9%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, stands at nearly 1.2x. The debt-to-equity ratio, representing total debt as a proportion of shareholder equity, is roughly 1.7x. Free cash flow, calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, reached nearly $10.8 billion during the same fiscal period.

The case for Shopify

Shopify provides the essential internet infrastructure that allows merchants of all sizes to start, run, and grow their businesses. The platform serves millions of businesses globally, providing tools for sales across web, mobile, and physical locations. It maintains strategic dependencies on Alphabet for cloud hosting and integrates payment services from providers like Stripe and PayPal to streamline merchant operations.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $11.6 billion, marking a growth of approximately 30.1% over the previous twelve months. The company reported a net income of roughly $1.2 billion for the year, achieving a net margin of nearly 10.7%. This growth illustrates the continued demand for independent storefront solutions as more businesses move away from centralized third-party marketplaces.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Shopify has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, indicating negligible debt relative to its shareholders' equity. The current ratio stands at a robust 6.0x, providing significant liquidity for future investments. Free cash flow reached nearly $2.0 billion, though note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.1% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because it is a non-cash expense.

Risk profile comparison

MercadoLibre faces significant risks from intensifying competition, particularly from Asian e-commerce entrants employing aggressive pricing and logistics strategies. The company is sensitive to macro-economic volatility in Latin America, including high inflation and currency devaluations. Regulatory risks are also acute, as its fintech arm operates under varying financial regimes and faces evolving antitrust scrutiny regarding its platform algorithms and logistics integration.

Shopify faces intense competition from established platforms like Amazon and niche providers, with risks amplified by the potential integration of competing technologies. The company is susceptible to macroeconomic downturns, which disproportionately affect its small and medium-sized merchant base. Legal and regulatory risks include evolving privacy laws, potential liability for merchant activities, and reliance on third-party cloud providers and artificial intelligence models for core operations.

Valuation comparison

MercadoLibre offers a lower valuation on both an earnings and sales basis compared to the premium pricing currently assigned to Shopify.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

To compare MercadoLibre and Shopify, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

To start, there's growth. Let me be clear: Both of these companies have excellent growth. Over the last five years, MercadoLibre has averaged 44% year-over-year revenue growth. Shopify, meanwhile, has averaged 27%. Moreover, these are not small companies. MercadoLibre has generated about $35.2 billion in revenue over the last 12 months; Shopify has recorded about $13.3 billion. Nevertheless, MercadoLibre comes out ahead in the head-to-head comparison given its exceptional revenue growth.

Another factor to consider is each company's valuation. We'll use forward price-to-earnings (P/E) to compare them. MercadoLibre's forward P/E is 49x, which is well above the market average. However, Shopify's 91x forward P/E multiple is not quite double that of MercadoLibre. While both companies are far from value darlings, MercadoLibre gains the edge in this category.

Last, we should take a closer look at each company's balance sheet. In short, both have solid balance sheets. Shopify has over $4.7 billion in net cash, giving it plenty of room for future acquisitions, capital investments, or stock buybacks. MercadoLibre, meanwhile, has around $484 million in net cash, meaning it can easily cover its debt obligations with cash alone.

In summary, both stocks are worthy of serious consideration for growth-oriented investors. However, if forced to choose between the two, I prefer MercadoLibre for its faster growth and relatively more modest valuation.

news.Title: Should You Buy Sandisk Stock Before Oct. 29?
news.Content:
Earnings season is getting underway, and one of the more interesting reports on the calendar belongs to Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK). Since spinning off from Western Digital in February 2025, Sandisk has emerged as a key beneficiary of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom.

Sandisk stock has surged as demand for memory and storage outpaces supply, creating an unusually favorable pricing environment. With fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings scheduled for Oct. 29, Wall Street is expecting another blockbuster quarter. Investors are now wondering whether it is better to buy Sandisk stock before earnings or wait until afterward.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Wall Street has high expectations for Sandisk

Sandisk manufactures NAND flash memory, the technology powering solid-state drives (SSDs), smartphones, computers, and enterprise storage systems. As AI infrastructure expands, data centers require increasingly sophisticated storage systems to manage enormous amounts of data. That's creating an attractive value proposition for Sandisk.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Wall Street expects Sandisk to generate $10.7 billion in revenue alongside earnings of roughly $46 per share. These are extraordinary numbers considering the company generated $20.2 billion in revenue during its entire previous fiscal year.

What makes the upcoming report particularly interesting is that investors have already received an encouraging preview of memory industry conditions from another major manufacturer.

Micron's earnings could be a proxy for Sandisk

On Sept. 30, Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.2 billion, representing a jaw-dropping increase of 379% year over year. The company also reported a gross margin of 87%, underscoring the pricing power memory producers currently possess.

Management's outlook is what has me thinking Sandisk could surprise to the upside. During the earnings call, Micron's management said it expects memory and storage supply-and-demand conditions to be "much tighter" in fiscal 2027 and 2028 relative to last year.

In my eyes, this commentary suggests that both Micron and Sandisk will benefit when demand exceeds available manufacturing capacity. Sandisk's management has echoed similar thoughts around supply constraints and growing customer demand in the storage market. In turn, if NAND prices continue climbing while production remains constrained, Sandisk should be in a position to deliver stronger-than-expected revenue, profit margins, and earnings.

Story Continues

Should you buy Sandisk stock before Oct. 29?

Sandisk stock trades around $1,500, while Wall Street expects approximately $215 in earnings per share during fiscal 2027. That translates into a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 7.

On the surface, that looks inexpensive for a company experiencing explosive growth. But remember, memory manufacturers historically trade at relatively low multiples because their profits fluctuate dramatically with supply-and-demand cycles. With that said, all signs point to AI infrastructure spending being a secular tailwind. If production shortages persist through 2028, investors could begin assigning Sandisk a higher multiple.

Of course, there's no guarantee that Sandisk stock will rally following a strong earnings report. The stock could decline even after delivering impressive results if investors take profits or if management's guidance disappoints. This is why I wouldn't make Oct. 29 the deciding factor for an investment in Sandisk stock.

Instead, investors who believe in Sandisk's multiyear growth opportunity should consider dollar-cost averaging -- purchasing shares in smaller increments over a long-term time horizon rather than committing their entire allocation before one earnings announcement. While this approach doesn't eliminate downside risk, it reduces dependence on timing the perfect entry point.

Overall, I see Sandisk as an attractive semiconductor stock. Rather than trying to predict the stock's immediate reaction to the upcoming earnings report, smart investors may consider accumulating shares gradually as the more sensible long-term strategy throughout the AI infrastructure supercycle.

news.Title: Bearish AI Headlines: An Artificial Wave of Panic
news.Content:
Misleading AI Headlines Drag Down Memory Names

Over the past few weeks, three bearish AI headlines have dragged down the industry and sparked fear, uncertainty, and doubt among investors. Although short-term price action has been negative and bears have been in control, the headlines are misleading or downright inaccurate. Below are the three headlines:

1. "OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Nears $50B, Below Earlier $70B Reports": Earlier this month, the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's recent revenue growth was $20 billion below what Wall Street had expected. However, the article's editor failed to account for how OpenAI calculates revenue. In reality, the $70 billion revenue figure was never revised down, it was a completely different number. The $70 billion annualized revenue reported in late September by Axios and Reuters included enterprise sales, which more than doubled since July. Conversely, the FT's $50 billion OpenAI revenue figure did not include the full value of sales through cloud partners. In other words, nothing has changed. The $70 billion gross revenue and $50 billion net revenue remained the same, signaling that OpenAI's business is still growing rapidly.

2. "Meta Muse Growth Plateaus": Recent headlines suggest that Meta Platform's ( META ) agentic AI platform "Muse" is seeing sluggish growth. However, data show that Muse is growing faster than any AI platform since ChatGPT launched in late 2022.

3. "Why this Little Known Chinese Chipmaker Has Caused a Global Stock Rout": Earlier this week, memory-related stocks like Micron ( MU ), SK Hynix ( SKHY ), and SanDisk ( SNDK ) fell amid reports that China-based ChangXin Memory Technologies has made progress on new architecture that will increase memory density on its AI chips. Memory stocks have soared over the past few years as demand has dramatically overwhelmed supply. While a higher memory supply is bearish for names like Micron, investors have overreacted for a few reasons. First, CXMT has difficulty accessing chipmaking equipment from companies like ASML ( ASML ) due to U.S. export controls. Second, the legacy memory makers still have a wide technological advantage over CXMT. In other words, companies are unlikely to dump SKHY or MU in favor of CXMT technology.

Bottom Line

Short-term headline noise has led to bearish price action among AI leaders. However, misinterpreted revenue metrics, overstated platform slowdowns, and exaggerated competitive threats have created an artificial wave of panic.

Story Continues

news.Title: Heavy Unusual Call Option Activity in Chip Designer Arm Holdings Plc - Are Investors Still Bullish?
news.Content:
A Barchart report today shows unusually heavy call option trading in Arm Holdings Plc (ARM) , an advanced semiconductor chip designer. Despite today's chip stock selloff, is this bullish, or are some stockholders selling covered calls?

ARM is up slightly today at $256.79 , despite the chip-stock turbulence. However, in the last three weeks, it has dropped from a Sept. 22 peak of $333.20. In effect, it has been flat over the last three months, as the Barchart chart below shows.

Bear Call Spread Ideas for Tesla Earnings Next Week

Unusual Call Options Activity in SNAP Stock - Investors Turning Bullish?

This Options Strategy Could Extract a 100% Payout from Exelon (EXC) Stock

This could be positioning ahead of the upcoming Nov. 4 fiscal Q2 earnings report date for the quarter ending Sept. 30. Nevertheless, analysts have significantly higher price targets (PTs) for ARM stock.

For example, Yahoo! Finance's survey of 43 analysts shows an average PT of $290.70. Similarly, Barchart's mean analyst survey PT is $292.72. These imply upside of 13.6% in ARM.

Moreover, analysts forecast 23% revenue growth this year (to the year ending March 2027) at $6.06 billion, and 36% next year ($8.25 billion). Moreover, free cash flow (FCF) soared last quarter to $705 million, representing 54.69% of revenue.

If this keeps up during Q2 and for all of this FY, FCF could reach $3.31 billion (i.e., $6.06b x 0.5469) this year and $4.51 billion next FY. That is why ARM stock does not necessarily look overvalued.

For example, using a 1.0% FCF yield metric and applying it to the next 12-month (NTM) forecast of $3.91 billion , Arm Holdings could be worth $391 billion (i.e., $3.91b / 0.01).

Even at a 1.25% FCF yield, the stock is worth $312.8 billion , or 13.84% over today's market cap of $274.78 billion.

That leads to a price target of $292.33 (i.e., 1.1384 x $256.79 price today). That's why analysts have set their PTs at this level. Howewer, next year, it could be worth even more, especially if its higher revenue estimates come into focus.

For example, FY 28 $4.51 billion FCF / 0.0125 = $360.8 billion fair value. That is 31.3% higher than today's market cap, leading to a PT of $337.17 .

That could be why some investors are willing to buy unusual volumes of out-of-the-money call options at $330, and some investors are selling at this price.

Unusual Call Options Activity in ARM

Barchart's Unusual Stock Options Activity Report today shows that almost 21,000 call options have traded at a $330 strike price for expiry on Dec. 18, 2026. That's 66 days from now and would include any upgraded price targets after the company's upcoming fiscal Q2 earnings and FCF report.

Story Continues

This volume is almost 20x the prior number of calls outstanding at that price. Moreover, the call premium is $7.46, so investors buying these calls may expect to see ARM rise to over $337.46 . (Note: this is close to our PT of $337.17 shown above).

On the other hand, it is very likely that some existing shareholders are willing to sell their shares at this strike price. They are happy to receive $7.46 in premium now for the obligation to sell at $330 in just over 2 months.

In effect, the covered call yield is high at 2.91% (i.e., $7.46/$256.79). On an annualized basis, if this can be repeated every two months, the effective yield is 17.43%, a very attractive expected return.

So, does this mean investors are still bullish on ARM? Maybe. But not necessarily. The call option seller could be doing a multi-leg trade where they are booking a call credit spread. It could also be offsetting a different leg.

But some investor, even if it is the bookmaker or brokerage firm, has to be buying these out-of-the-money calls. As I have shown, there is some basis for ARM stock to move higher and approach this call option strike price.

The bottom line is the upcoming Nov. 4 earnings release is very important. If it shows that the company's free cash flow (FCF) is staying strong and FCF margins are over 50%, ARM stock could indeed move higher.

In effect, analysts' higher PTs will be vindicated and could even rise. That would push ARM stock up.

news.Title: Is Meta Platforms Stock Heading for $1,000?
news.Content:
Social media giant Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) has rallied 15% this year as it looks to be on track to hit a new all-time high. The business has done well despite adversity and legal challenges relating to the addictiveness of its platforms.

The company generates billions in revenue from advertisers, and the hope is that its new artificial intelligence (AI) assistant, Muse, could drive even more revenue growth. Despite a market cap of around $2 trillion, the stock doesn't look overpriced and may still have more upside. Could it hit $1,000 in the near future?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Meta's stock doesn't look expensive, based on its expected growth

Although Meta's stock is approaching $800, in terms of earnings, its valuation is not enormous. It's trading at 28 times its trailing earnings. But based on analyst projections of how profitable the business will be in the year ahead, it's at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 22.

A key metric growth investors look at is the PEG multiple, which takes into consideration the earnings multiple and the future earnings growth that analysts expect over the next five years. A PEG of less than 1.0 suggests the stock is a good buy when considering future growth. Meta is just under that cutoff right now.

However, analyst expectations can change over time. If Muse proves to be a big moneymaker for the business, the company's outlook may be more promising, leading to greater returns for shareholders.

Is Meta's stock worth buying today?

Despite the optimism around the business, the consensus analyst price target for Meta's stock is around $796, suggesting it's unlikely to rise much higher. However, the most bullish forecast does project it will reach $1,000. Price targets are typically the levels analysts expect a stock to reach over the next 12 to 18 months.

Meta has a strong business, but I'm not convinced it's worth investing in at its current share price. Its Muse assistant may open up more growth opportunities, but there's also likely to be considerable competition in the space as more companies develop AI assistants. Whether consumers will truly need them and see value in paying for them is also debatable.

The social media stock may hit $800 within a few weeks or even days, but I don't think $1,000 is on the horizon just yet, maybe in the long run. I'd take a wait-and-see approach with the stock first to gauge how well Muse is doing before buying Meta's stock, as its future gains may hinge heavily on how successful its AI strategy proves to be.

Story Continues

news.Title: Jeff Bezos Says Blue Origin’s Goal Is a Flight to Space Every Minute — ‘They Think I’m Crazy. I’ve Seen Crazy Things Come True.’
news.Content:
Jeff Bezos has spent billions chasing a future most people will never see up close. Now, the Amazon (AMZN) founder wants his rocket company to reach a point where launching into space becomes almost routine — with a rocket taking off every minute. His own team thinks that goal sounds crazy, and Bezos knows it.

"Our goal is to fly every day. And then once we're flying every day, we want to fly every hour. And then once we're flying every hour, we want to fly every minute," Bezos said in an October interview with Bret Baier on Fox News' "Special Report."

More News from Barchart

Elon Musk Sets the Record Straight on Terafab. What It Means for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX Stocks.

Why Super Micro Stock Is Heading to $60

A $1.3 Billion Reason Why IONQ Stock Is Down Today

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

That last step is where he starts to lose his audience, even inside his own company.

"That's where I lose the team. They think I'm crazy [for wanting] to fly every minute. But I've seen crazy things before come true," Bezos said.

Sponsored Content: A $9 Trillion Flying Car Market Is Taking Shape. This Company Is Open to Investors.

He pointed to Amazon's early ambitions as an example of goals that once seemed out of reach but eventually became reality. For Bezos, the point isn't that launching rockets every minute will happen tomorrow. It's that a seemingly impossible target can push a company to do things it otherwise might never attempt.

Jeff Bezos Has Put $28 Billion Into Blue Origin

Bezos isn't pitching the vision from the sidelines. He said he has personally invested $28 billion in Blue Origin, the space company he founded in 2000.

The company also recently raised $10 billion from outside investors for the first time, marking a shift for a business that has largely relied on Bezos' personal fortune. He said the funding round was oversubscribed and that he waited until the company's financial prospects became clearer before bringing in outside capital.

An initial public offering (IPO) could eventually be part of the plan, too.

"Someday […] several years from now," Bezos said, an IPO would "probably make sense."

He didn't give a timetable for taking Blue Origin public. For now, the focus is on building the business and expanding its ability to launch rockets.

Blue Origin's Next Rocket Launch Is a Crucial Test

The immediate goal is much more grounded than a rocket every minute.

Blue Origin is targeting December for the next flight of its New Glenn rocket after an engine-test explosion in May damaged launch infrastructure and delayed its plans. The upcoming mission is expected to carry Blue Ring, a vehicle designed to transport payloads between orbits and support missions farther into space.

Story Continues

The company is also building additional launch pads, with plans to increase its capacity from roughly 12 launches a year toward 50 using its current pad.

That would still leave Blue Origin far short of launching every day, let alone every hour. But the gap between today's operations and Bezos' long-term goal is precisely the challenge he wants the company to tackle.

Bezos Wants to Beat China to the Moon — And Stay There

The launch ambitions are tied to a larger plan. Bezos wants the United States to beat China in the race to return humans to the moon, with a potential landing in 2028.

"We have to beat China to the moon, and I believe we will," Bezos said.

He wants the next lunar effort to last longer than a brief visit. His vision includes a sustainable lunar base supported by regular cargo deliveries, with lunar resources potentially used to produce solar cells and liquid oxygen that could serve as rocket propellant.

The moon, in his view, is a stepping stone to a broader human presence in space, including eventual missions to Mars.

Can Blue Origin Turn Bezos' Big Vision Into Reality?

Bezos has the money, the ambition, and a clear idea of what success could look like. What remains uncertain is how quickly Blue Origin can turn that vision into a working business.

A rocket launch every minute is an extraordinary goal, not an announced timetable. Reaching anything close to that pace would require major advances in launch infrastructure, rocket reuse, manufacturing, and customer demand.

For now, the next New Glenn mission is a more immediate measure of progress. If Blue Origin can return to flight and steadily increase its launch rate, Bezos' vision will begin to look less like science fiction and more like a long-term business plan.

The minute-by-minute rocket schedule can wait. First, Blue Origin has to prove it can keep launching.

news.Title: Is Amazon Stock Poised to Gain on Strong Free Cash Flow Growth?
news.Content:
Amazon AMZN is laying the groundwork for a free cash flow rebound, even as heavy AI spending pressures near-term cash generation. Last month, Amazon announced that Wiwynn will expand its Texas facility to build server systems and racks for Amazon's data centers, which strengthens its custom hardware supply. On Oct. 2, it committed more than $1 billion over five years to communities that host its data centers through its Built Together program, easing the path for capacity expansion.

Amazon still generates a lot of cash from operations. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 33% to $161.4 billion as of June 30, 2026. However, free cash flow swung to an outflow of $7.6 billion from an inflow of $18.2 billion a year ago. That reflects a $66.1 billion increase in net capital spending, mainly for AI. Second-quarter net sales grew 20% to $200.6 billion, while operating income jumped 43% to $27.5 billion. AWS sales climbed 37% to $42.2 billion.

Strong visibility into future demand supports the spending. AWS backlog reached $496 billion, growing at a triple-digit rate, and 2027 capacity is largely reserved. Most AI capacity is contracted for at least five years. Servers break even in under three years and have a useful life of five to six years, indicating solid cash returns once new data centers go live. The AI and chips businesses each exceeded a $25 billion annual run rate.

For the third quarter, Amazon expects net sales of $197-$202 billion and operating income of $22.5-$26.5 billion, up from $17.4 billion a year ago. However, Amazon now expects 2026 cash capex of about $220 billion, up from $200 billion, partly because of higher memory costs. That signals continued free cash flow headwinds and capacity constraints into 2027.

While near-term free cash flow remains under pressure, Amazon's surging operating cash flow and contracted AWS demand position the stock to gain as its investment cycle matures.

How Rivals Stack Up on Free Cash Flow

Microsoft MSFT and Alphabet GOOGL are also balancing cash generation against AI-driven spending. In the June 2026 quarter, Microsoft generated $55.4 billion in operating cash flow against $35.8 billion of capital expenditures, leaving about $19.6 billion in free cash flow. For fiscal 2026, Microsoft's operating cash flow totaled $182.9 billion. Alphabet, by contrast, posted second-quarter free cash flow of negative $5.9 billion, as quarterly capex of $44.9 billion outpaced $39.1 billion of operating cash flow. Alphabet raised its 2026 capex outlook to $195-$205 billion, while Microsoft continues expanding data center capacity to meet strong Azure cloud demand.

Story Continues

news.Title: Marvell Technology Just Gave Its Investors Great News
news.Content:
Earlier this year, Nvidia CEO called Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) the next trillion-dollar business. At around $230 billion, Marvell is a fraction of the size of Nvidia, whose market cap is well over $5 trillion. But the business has been doing exceptionally well, and its share price is up around 200% this year.

Recently, Marvell's management gave investors more reasons to remain bullish, revealing some promising guidance for the future.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Marvell projects revenue to reach $80 billion by fiscal 2031

Artificial intelligence (AI) has unlocked massive growth opportunities for Marvell, as it has for other tech companies . In its most recent fiscal year, which ended in January, the company's revenue totaled $8.2 billion, which was up an impressive 42% year over year.

However, in the longer run, by fiscal 2031, management expects revenue to be around $80 billion. With a significantly larger business, it's not difficult to see why Huang is so bullish about Marvell's upside. At about 10 times the size, its valuation could conceivably be 10 times larger as well, which could lead to Marvell blowing past the $1 trillion mark on the way to $2 trillion.

The assumption, of course, is that it continues to trade at multiples similar to those it trades at today and that its margins are comparable. But with so much growth on the horizon, there is clearly a lot of upside for Marvell's stock.

Is Marvell's stock a no-brainer buy right now?

As demand for custom chips grows due to AI, Marvell is in an excellent position to benefit from those growth opportunities. Its valuation is elevated today, with the stock trading at close to 90 times its trailing earnings, but the company's recent forecast highlighted why it may still be worth buying. With so much more growth in the long run, there's reason to remain bullish that, although the stock may look pricey right now , its valuation may still rise a lot higher in the future.

The caveat, however, is that in five years, a lot could change with respect to AI and the broader tech sector. There may be more competition as well. There's always going to be some risk when looking that far out, as forecasts can change. And that's something investors should consider.

Marvell's stock isn't cheap, and it does price in a lot of future growth already, but for investors who are prepared to hang on for at least five-plus years, this may be one of the better tech stocks to buy right now.

news.Title: 3 Best AI Stocks to Buy on This Pullback (SNDK, LITE, JBL)
news.Content:
Rising risk-off sentiment is once again weighing on AI and semiconductor stocks, with some of the market's strongest performers selling off. Concerns over rapidly rising interest rates and uncertain central bank policy, compounded by geopolitical tensions and persistently strong energy prices have prompted investors to rotate into more defensive sectors.

We've seen this play out numerous times throughout the AI bull market. Periodic corrections shake out weaker hands, but the underlying growth trends continue to strengthen. And for investors willing to look beyond short-term volatility, these pullbacks have consistently presented attractive buying opportunities.

The key, in my view, is focusing on companies supplying the mission-critical infrastructure behind the AI buildout, particularly businesses benefiting from supply constraints, strong pricing power and accelerating earnings growth.

Three stocks that stand out today are Sandisk Corporation (SNDK), Lumentum (LITE) and Jabil (JBL). Each represents a different but essential piece of the AI infrastructure boom, spanning memory and storage, optical networking, and advanced electronics manufacturing.

More importantly, all three are benefiting from powerful fundamental tailwinds that appear likely to persist well beyond the current market correction.

Sandisk (SNDK): AI's Insatiable Demand for Memory and Storage

Sandisk has emerged as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI-driven memory boom. Following its separation from Western Digital, the company has become a more direct way to invest in the rapidly expanding demand for NAND flash memory and data storage.

AI systems generate and process enormous volumes of data, and that information needs to be stored, retrieved and moved efficiently. As AI workloads expand, particularly inference applications, demand for high-performance storage continues to grow.

At the same time, memory manufacturers have struggled to keep up with demand, creating one of the most significant supply-demand imbalances the industry has experienced in years. The result has been extraordinary pricing power.

Sandisk's latest quarterly results illustrate just how powerful this trend has become. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue surged 372% year over year to nearly $9 billion, including a 51% sequential increase. Approximately two-thirds of that sequential growth came from higher pricing, with the remainder driven by increased shipment volumes.

Profitability has exploded alongside revenue. Gross margins reached 84.6%, compared with just 26.2% a year earlier, while non-GAAP earnings climbed to $39.25 per share. The company's data center business has been particularly impressive, with annual revenue surging 437% to more than $5.1 billion.

Story Continues

And according to consensus estimates, the momentum is expected to continue.

For fiscal 2027, analysts forecast revenue growth of 143% to $49.25 billion, followed by another 18.7% increase to $58.46 billion in fiscal 2028. Earnings estimates are even more impressive, with EPS expected to surge 201% this year to $213.31, before climbing another 18.5% to $252.80 next year.

These are extraordinary numbers, and even more remarkable considering the scale of the business.

Yet despite the enormous earnings growth, Sandisk currently trades at just 7x forward earnings and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) .

Of course, that seemingly cheap valuation needs to be considered in the context of the highly cyclical memory industry. When supply is constrained and pricing is exceptionally strong, earnings can surge, making stocks appear unusually inexpensive near the peak of a cycle.

That is the primary risk here. Today's extraordinarily high margins should not be assumed to persist indefinitely, and additional supply or a slowdown in demand could eventually reverse some of the pricing gains.

However, the AI infrastructure boom has introduced a significant new source of structural demand, potentially making this cycle more durable than those of the past. If memory pricing remains elevated longer than investors anticipate, Sandisk's valuation could prove genuinely attractive.

Following its extraordinary rally over the last year, SNDK shares have spent the past six months consolidating in a wide and volatile trading range. Given the size of that range, the most attractive tactical opportunities may come either on a pullback toward support near $1,200 or on a decisive breakout above resistance around $1,800.

The former would offer a more favorable entry near support, while the latter would signal renewed bullish momentum and potentially the start of another leg higher.

Image Source: TradingView

Lumentum (LITE): The Optical Networking Bottleneck

One of the most significant challenges facing the AI infrastructure buildout is no longer simply obtaining enough computing power. Increasingly, it is figuring out how to connect all that computing power efficiently.

This is creating an enormous opportunity for Lumentum, a leading developer of advanced optical and photonic technologies.

The company manufactures high-performance lasers, optical components and networking systems that allow enormous quantities of data to move through modern data centers.

As AI clusters become larger and more sophisticated, moving information between GPUs, servers and data centers has become an increasingly difficult engineering challenge. And while adding more computing power is essential, that hardware is only as useful as the networks connecting it.

Traditional electrical connections are increasingly challenged by the bandwidth, distance and power requirements of next-generation AI systems. Optical technologies offer substantially greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency, making them a critical part of the industry's ongoing expansion.

Demand has become so intense that Lumentum recently indicated that some of its AI-related optical components are effectively sold out through early 2029.

That is an extraordinary level of demand visibility, particularly for a hardware supplier, and suggests the industry's capacity constraints are unlikely to disappear overnight.

The financial implications are becoming increasingly apparent.

Lumentum's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue more than doubled year over year to approximately $1.01 billion, while non-GAAP earnings surged to $3.23 per share from $0.88 in the year-ago quarter. Operating margins have also expanded dramatically, reaching 36.6% from just 15% a year earlier.

And based on current analyst forecasts, the company is only getting started.

According to Zacks consensus estimates, fiscal 2027 revenue is projected to more than double, rising 107% to $6.25 billion. Analysts then expect another 60.5% increase in fiscal 2028, bringing annual sales above $10 billion.

Earnings growth should be even more explosive. EPS is expected to surge 146.8% to $21.40 this fiscal year, followed by another 64% increase to $35.08 next year.

These forecasts represent one of the more aggressive growth trajectories anywhere in the AI infrastructure industry.

That growth comes at a price, however. Lumentum currently trades at approximately 46.4x forward earnings , a considerable premium even among rapidly growing technology companies.

While the valuation is elevated, it is not necessarily unreasonable given the company's extraordinary earnings outlook and unusually strong demand visibility.

Beyond its existing products, Lumentum is positioned to benefit from emerging technologies including optical circuit switching, 1.6-terabit networking modules and co-packaged optics. These technologies should become increasingly important as hyperscalers build larger AI clusters while attempting to contain networking costs and power consumption.

The main risk is that expectations have become exceptionally high. Any disappointment in orders, capacity expansion or margins could trigger substantial volatility, particularly following the stock's enormous rally.

Nevertheless, with its products occupying an increasingly critical position in AI infrastructure and demand expected to substantially exceed available supply, Lumentum remains one of the most compelling growth stories in the sector.

After breaking out from a significant consolidation earlier this month, LITE shares have pulled back to retest the breakout level.

This is a critical area to watch. Ideally, the stock should find support here and resume its uptrend, confirming the breakout. A failure to hold this level, however, could open the door to further downside and potentially serve as an early warning sign for the broader AI infrastructure trade.

Jabil (JBL): My Favorite AI Stock on This Pullback

Of the three stocks discussed today, Jabil may offer the most compelling combination of growth, valuation and technical positioning.

Unlike Sandisk and Lumentum, which operate in highly specialized areas of memory and optical networking, Jabil provides advanced manufacturing, engineering and supply chain services to some of the world's largest technology companies.

Its capabilities span data center hardware, server infrastructure, networking equipment, power systems and other sophisticated electronics.

Building AI infrastructure at scale involves far more than purchasing GPUs. Companies need complex server assemblies, networking systems, power distribution equipment, cooling infrastructure and an enormous network of components and suppliers.

Jabil helps customers manage this complexity, allowing them to ramp production and deploy infrastructure more efficiently.

And as hyperscalers continue committing hundreds of billions of dollars to AI infrastructure, Jabil is capturing a rapidly growing share of that spending.

In fiscal 2026, revenue increased 21% to $36 billion, while core operating margins expanded by 40 basis points. The company also generated more than $1.5 billion in adjusted free cash flow.

More importantly, management expects the growth to accelerate considerably in fiscal 2027.

The company recently guided for approximately $44.5 billion in revenue this year, representing 24% growth, while core earnings are expected to rise 34% to $17.55 per share.

AI-related revenue alone is expected to surge 54% to approximately $22.1 billion, approaching half of total sales.

That is a remarkable transformation for a company that has historically operated in the relatively mature electronics manufacturing industry.

And the consensus outlook suggests the momentum should continue well beyond the current year.

Analysts expect fiscal 2027 revenue of $44.62 billion, followed by another 15.3% increase to $51.45 billion in fiscal 2028. Earnings are expected to grow 34.5% to $17.61 per share this year, then another 25% to $22.02 next year.

What's particularly attractive is that investors aren't being asked to pay an excessive premium for that growth.

Jabil currently trades at just 17.7x forward earnings and carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , highlighting the strength of its earnings outlook and estimate revision trends.

For a company expected to grow earnings more than 34% this year and another 25% next year, that valuation looks especially reasonable.

Jabil also offers some diversification beyond AI infrastructure, with exposure to healthcare, automotive, industrial and other end markets. While AI has become an increasingly important growth driver, the company is not entirely dependent on a single industry.

There are risks, of course. Electronics manufacturing is a relatively low-margin business, and even modest disruptions to customer spending or manufacturing efficiency can have an outsized impact on profitability.

However, the combination of accelerating revenue growth, improving margins and substantial free cash flow generation puts Jabil in a particularly attractive position.

Along with the broader AI trade, JBL shares began correcting over the summer. Since then, the stock has carved out a compelling bullish wedge pattern, with support near $285 and resistance around $320.

A decisive breakout in either direction would provide an important signal, with a move above resistance suggesting the uptrend is ready to resume, while a breakdown below support could open the door to further downside.

Of the three stocks highlighted today, I think Jabil has the cleanest technical setup. Combined with its Zacks Rank #1, impressive growth forecasts and comparatively modest valuation, it stands out as my favorite opportunity on the current pullback.

AI Infrastructure Still Offers Compelling Opportunities

The recent selling pressure across AI-related stocks is understandably frustrating, particularly after the enormous gains many of these companies have delivered.

But investors should distinguish between deteriorating business fundamentals and a correction driven by changing sentiment, crowded positioning or valuation concerns.

For now, the fundamental picture across the most critical areas of AI infrastructure remains exceptionally strong.

Importantly, these companies are not merely trading on distant expectations of AI adoption. Their revenue, earnings and forward guidance already reflect significant real-world demand.

That doesn't mean the stocks cannot fall further. Valuations remain elevated in parts of the sector, and a meaningful slowdown in hyperscaler capital expenditures would present a serious risk to the broader investment thesis.

But until there is convincing evidence of a sustained deterioration in AI infrastructure spending or earnings expectations, I continue to view these corrections as opportunities rather than a reason to abandon the theme.

For investors looking to take advantage of the current weakness, Sandisk, Lumentum and Jabil represent three compelling ways to gain exposure to some of the most important and supply-constrained segments of the AI infrastructure boom.

news.Title: Tesla's Robotaxi Lands in Paris—But Europe's Real Fight Is Over Cheap EVs
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Tesla, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Tesla unveiled its Cybercab robotaxi in Europe at the Paris Motor Show while emphasizing its Full Self-Driving technology amid unresolved European regulatory approval.

Stellantis, Renault's Dacia brand, and Chinese makers like BYD showcased competing strategies emphasizing affordability, local production incentives, and low-cost EV models.

Investors should watch European incentive policies tied to vehicle manufacturing location and Tesla's upcoming Q3 earnings report for updates on FSD approval progress.

Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA) is sure to generate headlines at the Paris Motor Show as the electric vehicle (EV) giant unveils its Cybercab robotaxi in Europe for the first time.

Looking a bit closer at Europe's largest automotive stage, however, investors may find that the bigger story is about affordable EVs overall, with numerous competitors showing off their latest models.

→ 5 Retail Picks to Watch as the Holiday Shopping Season Nears

Stellantis N.V. (NYSE: STLA), for example, returns to the show with more than 60 vehicles across eight brands, while local Renault Group (OTCMKTS: RNLSY) will show a Dacia Spring that was built in Europe and designed to meet local incentives. Chinese competitors will also be in attendance in a bid to broaden their intercontinental appeal.

The contrast between these offerings highlights some of the different strategies companies are attempting to win Europe's coveted EV market—from autonomous driving tech to low-cost alternatives that take advantage of local opportunities.

→ Insider Buying Signals Opportunity in H.B. Fuller, FocalTherics, Cardinal

Tesla Makes a Big Bet on Autonomous Driving

Tesla is offering test drives on multiple vehicles equipped with the company's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system (though not in the Cybercab), a clear choice by the company to emphasize what it sees as a technological advantage. The company may be emphasizing this in addition to—or in place of—vehicle pricing and specs.

However, a critical factor for Tesla will be European regulations surrounding autonomous driving, which continue to evolve. This may be why the company is also focusing on its FSD Supervised, the driver-assistance tech, at the auto show. The vehicle authority of the Netherlands granted certain approval for FSD Supervised earlier this year, although it is not yet approved across all of Europe.

→ Broadcom's Anthropic Bet Gets Bigger as $60 Billion Financing Raises the Stakes

Story Continues

Nonetheless, approval for a driver-assistance platform is very different from that for a fully self-driving system, leaving Tesla still needing to convince European regulators of the safety and viability of its goal. One of the company's latest bids to do so is to drop the FSD name entirely in favor of "Assisted Driving."

Stellantis Attempts to Win Back European Buyers

European firm Stellantis has a new leader in CEO Antonio Filosa, as well as a renewed emphasis on its extensive portfolio of brands and a push to connect with European customers once again. Its display in Paris includes vehicles ranging from Fiat and Opel to Peugeot, Alfa Romeo, and Citroën, plus new products and concepts that aim to show how the company is transforming traditional brands into EV competitors.

The scale of Stellantis' display suggests the company is going all-out in an effort to rebuild momentum among European customers as it faces increased pressure in the market from Chinese EV makers and the cost of transitioning its many vehicles to EV.

To be successful at the transition, Stellantis will need to make electrification accessible for European customers without losing the perception of quality long associated with its brands. The company will need to turn its product launches into sales while also keeping an eye on margins.

A Lesser-Known Brand With Affordability Appeal

Renault's Dacia brand is offering a redesigned Spring electric city car at the show, another way of responding to the affordability challenge impacting all EV makers.

This model is produced in Europe—the previous version was built in China—thereby helping it meet European incentives favoring domestically made vehicles.

Taking advantage of local incentives like this can help Renault to keep the purchase price of Springs down without forcing the company to eat some of those costs itself. Incentives can play a massive role for buyers as well. Renault is banking on pricing and production decisions to make the math work, rather than leaning on brand recognition like Stellantis.

Chinese Competitors Bring Low-Cost Options

Chinese makers like BYD—trading over the counter in the United States as BYD (OTCMKTS: BYDDY)—are pressuring European rivals with low-cost EVs, including some new products unveiled at the show in Paris.

BYD presents the Atto 8, a seven-seat electric SUV that the company claims can charge from 10% battery to 97% in nine minutes under optimal conditions.

EV makers in China have sought to corner the market for entry-level pricing on EVs, but the Paris show may reveal competition at other pricing levels as well.

The show could also be an opportunity to highlight AI tools and autonomous driving tech these companies have developed.

What to Watch Going Forward

Investors should keep an eye on how European governments change the battlefield for EV makers with incentives linked to where cars are built, helping to potentially narrow the price gap between European-made EVs and imported rivals. Programs and requirements differ by country, though, so it's a complex system that may not yield clear winners.

For Tesla, a major catalyst will be its Q3 earnings report in the week following the Paris show, where investors will watch for updates on cash generation, capital spend, margins, and more. Of course, any progress on FSD approval will likely draw attention as well.

news.Title: Should You Buy Amazon Stock Before October Ends?
news.Content:
Amazon 's (NASDAQ: AMZN) fall sales event came and went last week. There could be one lingering Prime Big Deal Days opportunity worth exploring: Amazon stock itself.

Shares of the leading online retailer have declined 10% since peaking two months ago. Concerns about Amazon's surging capital expenditures in support of AI and a rotation out of consumer tech stocks have weighed on the bellwether's momentum. The downticks aren't a problem. They're an opportunity.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

It's time to go shopping

Amazon stock is slightly lagging the market in 2026, somewhat surprising given where it's at right now. The 20% in net sales it reported for its latest quarter was its strongest year-over-year jump since 2021. Amazon Web Services (AWS) -- its web-hosting business that is now accounting for a fifth of Amazon's revenue but three-fifths of its operating profit -- has been the key driver. That segment's revenue surged 37% in the second quarter, fueled by the AI boom.

It's not the only business that's accelerating at Amazon. The e-commerce business that put Amazon on the map three decades ago saw its North American sales rise 16% in its latest quarter. The bottom line is growing faster.

It's hard not to like Amazon after its recent pullback. Yes, it's spending a lot of money on AI. It also happens to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of the revolution, given AWS' growth. The early success of its own AI-powered conversational shopping assistant -- Rufus -- is also helping on the e-commerce end in a win-win way.

Paying less than 25 times next year's earnings isn't cheap for most stocks, but it's a bargain for Amazon. It has a strong moat in online retailing. AWS is a fast-growing cash cow. Amazon deserves a market premium. Today, you can ironically buy that premium at a discount. That's a sale. That's a Prime Big Deal Days sale that may not last long.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Dropped Again on Tuesday
news.Content:
Uh-oh. It's starting again. Competition from China on computer memory sales is roiling stock markets, and once again, Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock looks caught in the turmoil.

Last time this happened, in July, it cost Sandisk stock a near-50% decline in a month . Should investors expect a repeat of July's troubles?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Well, Sandisk stock shed 6% on Monday, and as markets reopen Tuesday, Sandisk stock is falling another 3.5% as of 11 a.m. ET.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

CXMT in the news

Blame Chinese DRAM company ChangXin Memory Technologies, CXMT. CXMT went public in July with a $487 billion market capitalization and a promise to expand DRAM production and steal market share from Western computer memory makers . In a supply-constrained market, even Apple was looking to buy memory chips from CXMT!

That plan fell apart after Apple discovered CXMT wanted it to pay the same (or worse) prices for DRAM as SK Hynix and Samsung were charging. And seeing as CXMT's chips were "two or three generations" behind current DRAM technology, Apple declined.

But now, CXMT is making a move to improve its technology. The company's new "4F square" stacked DRAM architecture promises to increase the storage density of its chips and make the product more competitive with Micron's, SK's, and Samsung's wares. CXMT hopes to use the new technology to begin producing high-bandwidth memory (HBM) later this year.

Should Sandisk investors worry?

Memory supply remains in deficit and may get even tighter next year. So long as CXMT's chips primarily supply the low end of the mobile phone market, rather than AI data centers, Sandisk's high-margin AI sales should be safe. Moreover, CXMT isn't (yet) producing NAND chips, which are Sandisk's specialty.

Although both companies target HBM, they're approaching from different directions. I see greater risk to Micron stock than to Sandisk.

news.Title: Meta Platforms Rises 12% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms META shares have rallied 12.4% in the past three-month period, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's return of 5.8%.

The company's shares have also outperformed its peers, which include Reddit RDDT, Amazon AMZN and Alphabet GOOGL. All three companies are expanding their footprints in the advertising space. While Reddit and Alphabet shares have lost 21.3% and 1.9%, respectively, Amazon shares have risen 4.9% in the past three-month period.

The outperformance can be attributed to robust advertising demand, AI-driven improvements in ad targeting and content recommendations, and growing user engagement across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Expanding adoption of Advantage+ advertising solutions and AI-powered creative tools is further supporting growth. The launch of Muse also remains a key catalyst. These factors are helping Meta Platforms fend off its competitors like Reddit, Amazon and Alphabet.

META Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

META Benefits From Strong AI-Led Ad Performance

Meta Platforms' strong growth in the advertising business has been noteworthy. The company's focus on integrating AI into its platforms — Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger and Threads — is driving user and advertising engagement. In the second quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms reported $59.4 billion in ad revenues, up 27% year over year, with a 14% increase in ad impressions and a 12% rise in average price per ad.

AI is heavily dependent on data, of which META has a trove, driven by its more than 3.6 billion daily users. Instagram reached 2 billion daily active users and Threads surpassed 500 million monthly active users in the second quarter of 2026. AI-powered recommendation and ranking systems are also strengthening engagement across META's platforms. Instagram time spent grew double digits year over year, while Facebook video time spent increased 9% globally. Meta Platforms is using large language models (LLMs) to better understand content and user preferences, enabling more personalized recommendations across Feed and Reels.

In the second quarter of 2026, the deployment of Meta Generative Recommender and other advanced models led to an 8.3% increase in ad clicks and a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook. More than 9 million small businesses now use at least one of Meta Platforms' AI-powered ad creative tools. Early LLM-powered initiatives also drove a 1% increase in app event conversions on Instagram. Its Advantage+ AI-powered advertising solutions also surpassed a $75 billion annual revenue run rate in the second quarter of 2026, highlighting growing advertiser adoption.

Story Continues

META Benefits From Expanding Muse AI Portfolio

Meta Platforms is benefiting from the expansion of its Muse AI model portfolio, which is further strengthening user engagement, advertising efficiency, and AI monetization opportunities. The company's Muse Spark 1.1 model offers advanced agentic capabilities, including computer use, tool use, and multimodal understanding. Following the integration of Muse Spark into Meta AI, daily interactions with the assistant increased 60%, reflecting growing adoption.

Further expanding its Muse AI portfolio, META recently introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its most advanced AI models, designed for complex agentic tasks across finance, law, health and coding. Built on Muse Spark, the models feature Active Memory for retaining relevant information across conversations and Active Focus for handling complex tasks and recovering from errors. Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, with broader Muse integration planned.

META Grapples With Rising Costs and AI Competition

Despite strong advertising growth and expanding AI capabilities, Meta Platforms faces challenges from rising infrastructure investments, higher operating expenses and regulatory uncertainties. In the second quarter of 2026, total expenses surged 55% year over year to $42 billion, while operating income declined 8%.

Higher AI talent costs, infrastructure spending and legal charges are pressuring profitability. In second-quarter 2026, capital expenditures jumped to $31.08 billion from $17.01 billion in the year-ago period, while free cash flow plunged to just $784 million from $8.55 billion.

The company now expects 2026 capital expenditures of $130-$145 billion as META builds servers, data centers and network infrastructure to support AI. The balance sheet quality also deteriorated, with long-term debt increasing to $83.66 billion as of June 30, 2026, from $58.74 billion at the end of 2025. Meta Platforms issued nearly $25 billion of long-term debt during the first half of 2026.

Stiff competition from AI agents like Google's Gemini, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Apple's AI ecosystem, and other emerging agent platforms also remains a headwind for META's AI agents.

META's Q3 Guidance Not So Rosy

Meta Platforms' strong advertising momentum and expanding AI capabilities support its growth outlook, but rising infrastructure costs, margin pressures and stiff competition remain a concern.

For the third quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms expects revenues between $61 billion and $64 billion. The forecast assumes foreign currency will create an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year revenue growth.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the third quarter of 2026 revenues is pegged at $63.18 billion, suggesting a year-over-year increase of 23.30%.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $6.39 per share, up 0.94% over the past 30 days, suggesting an 11.86% decline from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Meta Platforms, Inc. Price and Consensus

Meta Platforms, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Meta Platforms, Inc. Quote

META Shares Trade at a Premium

Meta Platforms shares are trading at a premium, as suggested by the Value Score of C.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, META is trading at 6.41X, higher than the broader Computer & Technology sector's 6.05X.

META Valuation

Conclusion

Meta Platforms' strong advertising momentum, AI-driven engagement and expanding Muse portfolio support its long-term growth prospects. However, rising infrastructure costs, margin pressures and stiff competition remain headwinds. Stretched valuation also remains a concern. Investors may consider holding META shares until AI investments translate into stronger earnings growth and profitability.

news.Title: MG vs. KLAC: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
news.Content:
Investors with an interest in Electronics - Miscellaneous Products stocks have likely encountered both Mistras (MG) and KLA (KLAC). But which of these two stocks presents investors with the better value opportunity right now? Let's take a closer look.

We have found that the best way to discover great value opportunities is to pair a strong Zacks Rank with a great grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system. The proven Zacks Rank emphasizes companies with positive estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight stocks with specific traits.

Mistras and KLA are both sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) right now. Investors should feel comfortable knowing that both of these stocks have an improving earnings outlook since the Zacks Rank favors companies that have witnessed positive analyst estimate revisions. However, value investors will care about much more than just this.

Value investors also tend to look at a number of traditional, tried-and-true figures to help them find stocks that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

The Style Score Value grade factors in a variety of key fundamental metrics, including the popular P/E ratio, P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a number of other key stats that are commonly used by value investors.

MG currently has a forward P/E ratio of 19.86, while KLAC has a forward P/E of 34.96. We also note that MG has a PEG ratio of 1.24. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. KLAC currently has a PEG ratio of 1.68.

Another notable valuation metric for MG is its P/B ratio of 2.74. The P/B ratio is used to compare a stock's market value with its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. For comparison, KLAC has a P/B of 39.11.

These are just a few of the metrics contributing to MG's Value grade of A and KLAC's Value grade of D.

Both MG and KLAC are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that MG is the superior value option right now.

news.Title: Amazon Isn’t Done Spending on AI: How a $7B Acquisition Could Help Take AMZN Stock Higher
news.Content:
Amazon (AMZN) is considering another multibillion-dollar investment in artificial intelligence, according to a published report.

According to The Wall Street Journal , Amazon is in talks to acquire Decart, an artificial intelligence startup, for approximately $7 billion. The potential deal would add another substantial commitment to Amazon's AI ambitions as the company competes with Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), and other technology giants.

More News from Barchart

Why Super Micro Stock Is Heading to $60

A $1.3 Billion Reason Why IONQ Stock Is Down Today

But there's an important distinction here. Amazon has already committed billions of dollars to AI infrastructure and partnerships. Buying a startup would give it more direct control over technology and talent that could help it develop new products.

About Amazon Stock

Amazon has been pouring money into artificial intelligence, particularly through Amazon Web Services (AWS), its cloud computing business. AWS provides the computing infrastructure that companies use to develop and operate AI applications, putting Amazon in direct competition with Microsoft's Azure and Alphabet's Google Cloud.

Amazon also has a major relationship with Anthropic, the developer of the Claude family of AI models. The partnership gives AWS a prominent AI customer while supporting demand for Amazon's custom-designed Trainium chips.

A potential Decart acquisition would represent a different approach. Rather than supplying the computing power behind another company's AI products, Amazon could bring additional AI development capabilities directly into its own business.

Decart develops software that makes it easier for developers to switch between different AI chips. That's important for Amazon, which is developing its own Trainium processors to compete with Nvidia (NVDA). Amazon reportedly gave Decart early access to its chips in 2025, so the companies already have a relationship. Acquiring Decart could help Amazon make its processors more attractive to AI developers who don't want to be locked into one company's hardware.

AMZN stock has been up 14% so far this year and 19% in the past 12 months, which roughly mimics the performance of the S&P 500 ($SPX). The stock has been bolstered through the company's success in building its AI business, indicating that investors are more than willing to forgive the company's ambitious spending plans as long as it delivers returns.

Story Continues

The company currently has a market cap of $2.8 trillion.

Beats on Earnings

Amazon's earnings report for the second quarter was nothing short of outstanding. Revenue was $200.6 billion, up from $167.7 billion a year ago. Sales in North America were up 16% to $116.2 billion, while international sales increased 15% to $42.2 billion.

But the biggest percentage increase was with AWS.

"AWS is booming, growing 36.7% year-over-year in Q2—our fastest growth in 18 quarters—and our AI and Chips businesses each eclipsed run rates of more than $25 billion," CEO Andy Jassy said.

Amazon also recorded $53.39 billion in non-operating income, which the company attributed to its investment in Anthropic. Net income was $62.64 billion, up from $18.16 billion a year ago, and earnings per share were $5.75.

Management issued guidance for the third quarter for revenue in the range of $197 billion and $202 billion, which would be growth between 9% and 12% from a year ago. The company is also expecting operating income between $22.5 billion and $26.5 billion, up from $17.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025.

What Do Analysts Expect From AMZN Stock?

Sentiment surrounding AMZN stock has remained bullish, and there's nothing in Amazon's current situation that has changed that. Fifty-three of 56 analysts surveyed by Barchart have "Buy" ratings on the stock, with the other three suggesting shareholders hold. The mean price target of $328.56 represents a potential upside of 29%.

Amazon isn't afraid to invest in itself to gain an advantage in the AI race. The company has the resources to make substantial investments in AI while continuing to operate its established e-commerce and cloud businesses. A Decart acquisition could give it another way to develop AI products rather than relying entirely on outside partners.

The price tag would be substantial, but Amazon has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to spend heavily when it sees an opportunity to build a business for the long haul. For investors who believe AI will drive future demand for computing and digital services, that's a compelling reason to keep Amazon on the radar.
